questions.stem: A kicker is charged late and the ball goes directly into touch. Other than at the place of the charge, where may the penalty be taken?

options.text: On the touchline where the ball went out
On the 15-metre line, level with where the ball crossed the touchline
On the half-way line, 15 metres in from touch
On the 5-metre line, level with where the ball crossed the touchline

questions.explanation: When the ball is kicked directly into touch, the alternative mark is on the 15-metre line in line with where it went out.

questions.stem: A kicker is charged late and the ball lands in in-goal. Other than at the place of the charge, how far from the try line may the penalty be taken?
questions.explanation: If the ball lands in in-goal, the alternative mark is five metres from the try line, in line with where the ball crossed it and at least 15 metres from touch.

questions.stem: A kicker is charged late and the ball strikes a goal post. Other than at the place of the charge, where may the penalty be taken?

options.text: On the 5-metre line in front of the posts
On the 22-metre line in front of the posts
At the foot of the post

questions.explanation: If the ball hits a goal post or the crossbar, the alternative mark is where the ball lands.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for an act against the spirit of good sportsmanship?
questions.explanation: Acts against the spirit of good sportsmanship are misconduct, sanctioned with a penalty.

questions.stem: A player loudly disputes the referee's decision. What is the sanction?

options.text: No sanction for a first offence

questions.explanation: Players must respect the referee's authority and must not dispute decisions.

questions.stem: What does the law require of players when the referee blows the whistle to stop play?

options.text: To stop once the ball is dead
To stop when their captain tells them

questions.explanation: Players must stop playing at once when the whistle goes.

questions.stem: A player is shown a yellow card. For how long is the player suspended?
questions.explanation: A yellow card means a caution and 10 minutes' suspension.

questions.stem: A player who has already had a yellow card commits another yellow-card offence. What must happen?

options.text: The player is given a final warning
The player serves a second 10 minutes
The player must be sent off

questions.explanation: A second yellow-card offence by the same player means a sending off.

questions.stem: What does a red card mean for the player shown it?

options.text: The player is suspended for 20 minutes
The player takes no further part in the match
The player may return in the next half
The player is suspended for 10 minutes

questions.explanation: A player shown a red card is sent off and plays no further part.

questions.stem: Outside elite rugby, may a player who has been sent off be replaced?

options.text: Yes, after 10 minutes of playing time
Yes, after 20 minutes of playing time
No, a player sent off may not be replaced
Yes, from the start of the second half

questions.explanation: As a general rule a player who is sent off may not be replaced. The 20-minute replacement applies only in elite rugby.

questions.stem: In elite rugby a player is sent off for an action that was not intentional and highly dangerous. When may the player be replaced?
questions.explanation: In elite rugby, for actions that are not intentional and highly dangerous, the sent-off player may be replaced after 20 minutes of playing time.

questions.stem: In elite rugby a player is sent off for an intentional and highly dangerous action. May the player be replaced?

options.text: Yes, after 20 minutes of playing time
Yes, after 10 minutes of playing time
No, the player cannot be replaced

questions.explanation: For intentional and highly dangerous actions the player cannot be replaced, even in elite rugby.

questions.stem: Where must a player shown a yellow card go?

options.text: To the in-goal area behind the posts
To the sin-bin, a designated place outside the playing area
To the team's technical zone, with the replacements

questions.explanation: A yellow-carded player goes to the sin-bin, which is a designated place outside the playing area.

questions.stem: According to the principle of the offside law, by whom is the game played?

options.text: By any player behind the ball-carrier
By every player in the playing area
Only by players who are onside
By any player within 10 metres of the ball

questions.explanation: The principle is that the game is played only by players who are onside.

questions.stem: How do the laws define offside?

options.text: Standing in front of the hindmost foot of any team-mate
A positional offence that leaves a player unable to take part without risking sanction
Being in the opponents' half before the ball arrives
Being nearer the opponents' try line than the ball when it is kicked

questions.explanation: Offside is a positional offence: the player can take no part in the game without being liable to sanction.

questions.stem: When is a player offside in open play?

options.text: When in front of a team-mate who is carrying the ball or who last played it
When nearer the opponents' try line than two defenders
When in front of the ball at any moment
When within 10 metres of an opponent who has the ball

questions.explanation: In open play a player is offside if in front of a team-mate who has the ball or who last played it.

questions.stem: A player is in an offside position in open play but takes no part in the game and is retiring. Is the player liable to be penalised?

options.text: Yes, a scrum is awarded where the player stands
Yes, a free-kick is awarded where the player stands
No, not unless the player interferes, advances or fails to retire
Yes, a penalty is awarded where the player stands

questions.explanation: Being in an offside position is not penalised by itself. The player must not interfere with play.

questions.stem: An offside player picks up a loose ball in open play. How does the law treat this?

options.text: As legal, because the ball was loose
As legal once the ball has bounced

questions.explanation: Playing the ball is the clearest example of an offside player interfering with play.

questions.stem: An offside player tackles the ball-carrier. How does the law treat this?

options.text: As legal if the tackle is made from the side
As interfering with play, so the player may be penalised
As legal once the ball-carrier has run five metres

questions.explanation: An offside player must not tackle the ball-carrier. Doing so is interfering with play.

questions.stem: An offside player does not touch the ball but stands in the defenders' way so they cannot play as they wish. Is the player interfering with play?

options.text: No, only playing the ball counts
Only if there is physical contact
Yes, that counts as interfering with play

questions.explanation: Preventing the opposition from playing as they wish is listed as interfering with play.

questions.stem: What do the laws call remaining in an offside position?
questions.explanation: A player who stays in an offside position is loitering, which is a form of interfering with play.

questions.stem: A loitering player is put onside by something the opposing team does. What does the law say about the player gaining from it?

options.text: The player may join play at once
The player may tackle but not play the ball
A loiterer must not benefit from being put onside
The player may join play after three seconds

questions.explanation: A loiterer is not allowed to benefit from being put onside by what the opposing team does.

questions.stem: Where in the playing area can a player be offside?

options.text: Only in the field of play, not in in-goal

questions.explanation: A player can be offside anywhere in the playing area.

questions.stem: A player in front of the passer catches a pass that was thrown forward by accident. Is the catcher offside?

options.text: No, receiving an unintentional throw forward is not offside
Yes, and it counts as accidental offside
Only if the catcher runs on with the ball
Yes, and a penalty is awarded

questions.explanation: A player who receives an unintentional throw forward is not offside. The throw forward itself is dealt with by a scrum.

questions.stem: Which of these makes an offside player liable to be penalised?

options.text: Retreating towards their own try line
Making no effort to retreat and interfering with play

questions.explanation: An offside player who does not try to retreat and interferes with play may be penalised.

questions.stem: An offside player in open play starts moving towards the ball. What does the law say?

options.text: The player becomes onside within 10 metres of the ball
The player can only be warned
The player may carry on if no opponent is near

questions.explanation: Moving towards the ball from an offside position is enough for the player to be penalised.

questions.stem: A player is penalised for offside in open play. What choice does the non-offending team have?

options.text: A scrum or a lineout at the place of infringement
A penalty where the ball landed, or a lineout
A penalty or a free-kick at the place of infringement
A penalty at the place of infringement, or a scrum where the offending team last played the ball

questions.explanation: The non-offending team chooses between a penalty where the offence took place and a scrum where the offenders last played the ball.

questions.stem: A team chooses a scrum instead of a penalty for offside in open play. Where is the scrum?

options.text: Where the offending team last played the ball
At the place of the infringement

questions.explanation: The scrum option is taken where the offending team last played the ball.

questions.stem: What does the 10-metre law require?

options.text: An offside player in front of a kicker to retire at once from where the ball lands or is caught
Every player to stay at least 10 metres from the kicker until the kick
Every kick in open play to travel at least 10 metres before it is played
Defenders to stand at least 10 metres back whenever a kick is taken

questions.explanation: A player in front of a team-mate who kicks must retire immediately behind an onside team-mate or a line 10 metres from where the ball lands or is caught.

questions.stem: A player is in front of a team-mate who kicks ahead. If no onside team-mate is nearer, how far from where the ball lands or is caught must the player retire to?
questions.explanation: The player must retire behind an imaginary line across the field 10 metres on their own side of where the ball lands or is caught.

questions.stem: A player in front of the kicker is close to where the ball will land. What must the player do to avoid being penalised?

options.text: Stand still until the ball is caught
Wait for the catcher to run five metres
Wait for the catcher to pass the ball
Retire immediately behind an onside team-mate or the 10-metre line

questions.explanation: The player has to retire at once, either behind an onside team-mate or behind the line 10 metres back from where the ball comes down.

questions.stem: Several players are offside within 10 metres of where a kick lands and none of them retires. Which one is penalised?

options.text: The one who was furthest in front of the kicker
The one closest to where the ball lands or is caught
The one who was last to become offside
The one the referee notices first

questions.explanation: When more than one player is involved, the one nearest to where the ball lands or is caught is penalised.

questions.stem: A kick strikes a goal post before landing. Does the 10-metre law still apply to offside players near where it lands?

options.text: Only if the ball rebounds into the field of play
Only if a defender catches the rebound
Yes, it applies even if the ball hits a post or the crossbar first
No, a rebound off the posts puts everyone onside

questions.explanation: The 10-metre line is measured from where the ball is caught or lands, even if it hits a goal post or crossbar first.

questions.stem: A kick is touched in flight by an opponent, but not charged down, before it lands. Does the 10-metre law still apply to the kicker's offside team-mates?

options.text: Only if the ball goes into touch
Only if the opponent then catches the ball
No, any touch by an opponent puts them onside

questions.explanation: The 10-metre law still applies when the ball touches or is played by an opponent. Only a charge down removes it.

questions.stem: A kick is charged down. Does the 10-metre law apply to the kicker's team-mates who were in front of the kicker?

options.text: Yes, but only those within five metres
No, it does not apply when the kick is charged down
Yes, they must still retire 10 metres
Yes, unless the ball goes backwards

questions.explanation: A charge down is the one case in which the 10-metre law does not apply.

questions.stem: A player is offside under the 10-metre law. The opponent who catches the ball then kicks it. Is the player put onside?

options.text: No, only a charge down by an opponent can do that
Yes, an opponent's kick puts the player onside
Yes, if the player was standing still
Yes, once the kick has travelled 10 metres

questions.explanation: A player offside under the 10-metre law cannot be put onside by anything an opponent does, apart from a charge down.

questions.stem: Which single action by an opponent can put onside a player who is offside under the 10-metre law?

options.text: Running five metres with the ball

questions.explanation: Under the 10-metre law, no action by an opponent puts the player onside except a charge down.

questions.stem: When is a player accidentally offside?

options.text: When the player is offside for less than three seconds
When the player did not realise they were in front of the ball
When the player is offside inside their own half
When the player cannot avoid being touched by the ball or by a team-mate carrying it

questions.explanation: Accidental offside is where the player could not avoid being touched by the ball or by a team-mate who has it.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for accidental offside when the offending team gains an advantage?
questions.explanation: Accidental offside is sanctioned with a scrum, and only if the offending team gained an advantage.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier bumps into a team-mate in front who could not get out of the way. The team gains no advantage. What happens?
questions.explanation: Play stops for accidental offside only if the offending team gains an advantage.

questions.stem: A player's kick hits a team-mate in front who could not avoid it, and the kicker's team regathers and gains an advantage. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: The team gained an advantage from an unavoidable contact, so it is accidental offside and a scrum.

questions.stem: When should the referee stop play for accidental offside?

options.text: Only if it happens inside a 22
Only if the other captain appeals
Only if the offending team gains an advantage

questions.explanation: The referee stops play for accidental offside only when the offending team gains an advantage.

questions.stem: An offside player runs back behind the team-mate who last played the ball. What is the player's status?

options.text: Offside until the next phase of play
Offside until an opponent plays the ball

questions.explanation: An offside player becomes onside by moving behind the team-mate who last played the ball.

questions.stem: An offside player moves behind a team-mate who is onside. What is the player's status?

options.text: Offside until the referee calls them onside
Offside until they reach their own 22
Offside until the kicker passes them

questions.explanation: Moving behind any onside team-mate puts an offside player onside.

questions.stem: In open play an onside team-mate runs past an offside player, and it is not a 10-metre law case. What is the effect?

options.text: The player stays offside until the next ruck
Nothing: only the kicker can do that
The offside player is put onside
The player is onside only after touching the team-mate

questions.explanation: An onside team-mate who moves past the offside player puts that player onside.

questions.stem: A kicker chases the kick by running through touch and back in. To put team-mates onside by passing them, where must the kicker be?

options.text: Within five metres of the ball
In the playing area, or back in it

questions.explanation: The onside team-mate must be within the playing area, or have re-entered it, when moving past the offside player.

questions.stem: Leaving aside 10-metre law cases, which action by an opponent puts an offside player onside in open play?

options.text: The opponent runs five metres with the ball
The opponent catches the ball cleanly

questions.explanation: In open play an opponent puts an offside player onside by kicking the ball, or by intentionally touching it without gaining possession.

questions.stem: An opponent intentionally touches the ball but does not gain possession. It is not a 10-metre law case. What is the effect on an offside player?

options.text: The player is onside after three seconds
The player is onside only if the ball goes forward

questions.explanation: An opponent intentionally touching the ball without gaining possession puts the offside player onside.

questions.stem: In open play an opponent catches a kick and runs five metres with the ball. Does that put the kicker's offside team-mates onside?

options.text: Yes, as soon as the ball is caught
No, running with the ball does not put them onside
Yes, once ten metres have been covered
Yes, once five metres have been covered

questions.explanation: In open play only an opponent's kick, or an intentional touch without gaining possession, puts offside players onside.

questions.stem: In open play an opponent catches a kick and passes the ball. Does the pass put the kicker's offside team-mates onside?

options.text: Yes, once the pass is caught
Yes, if the pass goes backwards
No, a pass by an opponent does not put them onside
Yes, as soon as the ball leaves the hands

questions.explanation: A pass is not one of the opponent's actions that puts an offside player onside in open play.

questions.stem: A player is offside at a ruck when the ruck ends. What is the player's status?

options.text: Onside if within a metre of the ball
Onside as soon as the ruck ends

questions.explanation: A player who is offside at a ruck, maul, scrum or lineout stays offside even after it has ended.

questions.stem: How can a player who was offside at a scrum become onside by their own action?

options.text: By raising a hand to show they are out of play
By moving sideways away from the ball
By immediately retiring behind the applicable offside line
By standing still until the ball is passed

questions.explanation: The player's own remedy is to retire at once behind the offside line that applies.

questions.stem: After a maul ends, how far must an opponent carry the ball to put a retiring offside player onside?
questions.explanation: An opposition player carrying the ball five metres in any direction puts the retiring player onside.

questions.stem: A player is retiring from an offside position after a lineout has ended. An opponent kicks the ball. What is the player's status?

options.text: Offside until behind the offside line
Onside only if the kick goes forward

questions.explanation: A kick by an opposition player puts the retiring player onside.

questions.stem: A player offside at a ruck is retiring when an opponent passes the ball. Does the pass put the player onside?

options.text: Yes, any pass puts the player onside
Yes, if the receiver is then tackled
Yes, if the pass travels five metres
No, a pass does not put the player onside

questions.explanation: The player is put onside only by retiring behind the offside line, by an opponent carrying the ball five metres, or by an opponent's kick.

questions.stem: A retiring player dawdles and so is in a better position when an opponent's kick puts the player onside. What may the referee do?

options.text: Award a scrum for accidental offside
Penalise the player for failing to retire without undue delay
Nothing, because the player was put onside

questions.explanation: A player who does not retire promptly and benefits from being put onside in a better position may be penalised.

questions.stem: A player left offside after a ruck, maul, scrum or lineout interferes with play. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Interfering with play from that offside position is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: A player left offside when a scrum ends moves towards the ball instead of retiring. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: An offside player who moves towards the ball may be penalised.

questions.stem: What was a knock forward previously called?
questions.explanation: The law book notes that a knock forward was previously called a knock-on.

questions.stem: In the laws, what does "forward" mean?

options.text: Towards the middle of the field
Away from the player's own hands

questions.explanation: Forward means towards the opposing team's dead-ball line.

questions.stem: A player drops the ball forward and it lands on the ground. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Losing possession so that the ball goes forward and touches the ground is a knock forward.

questions.stem: A player fumbles the ball forward but catches it again before it touches the ground or anyone else. Is it a knock forward?

options.text: No, the player caught it before it touched anything
Yes, because the ball travelled forward
Only if an opponent was within a metre

questions.explanation: It is a knock forward only if the ball touches the ground or another player before the original player can catch it.

questions.stem: A player juggles the ball forward three times and finally catches it without it touching the ground or another player. What is the decision?

options.text: Knock forward if it travelled more than a metre
Knock forward at the first fumble

questions.explanation: However many touches it takes, there is no knock forward if the player catches the ball before it touches the ground or anyone else.

questions.stem: The ball strikes a player's arm and goes forward to the ground, although the player made no attempt to catch it. Is it a knock forward?

options.text: Yes, the ball hit the arm and went forward
No, the player must have been holding the ball
Only if the arm was raised

questions.explanation: A ball that hits the hand or arm and goes forward to ground is a knock forward, even without an attempt to catch.

questions.stem: A player loses the ball forward and it hits a team-mate before the player can catch it again. What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, because a team-mate touched it

questions.explanation: The ball touched another player before the original player could regather it, so it is a knock forward.

questions.stem: A player loses the ball forward and it strikes an opponent before the player can regather it. Is it a knock forward?

options.text: Only if the opponent then drops it
No, a touch by an opponent cancels the knock forward
Yes, it touched another player before the original player could catch it
No, unless the opponent was offside

questions.explanation: A knock forward is complete when the ball touches the ground or any other player before it is caught again.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier is tackled and the ball spills backwards, towards the ball-carrier's own try line. Is it a knock forward?

options.text: Only if it touches the ground
Yes, any loss of possession is a knock forward
No, the ball did not go forward
Yes, if an opponent picks it up

questions.explanation: A knock forward requires the ball to go forward, which means towards the opposition's dead-ball line.

questions.stem: At the base of a ruck a scrum-half hits the ball forward with a hand and it touches the ground. What is this?
questions.explanation: Hitting the ball forward with the hand so that it touches the ground is a knock forward.

questions.stem: Where in the playing area can a knock forward occur?

options.text: Only in the field of play

questions.explanation: A knock forward may occur anywhere in the playing area.

questions.stem: A player knocks the ball forward in the opponents' in-goal. Can it be a knock forward there?

options.text: Only if the ball then goes dead
Only if a defender then grounds the ball
Yes, a knock forward can occur anywhere in the playing area

questions.explanation: In-goal is part of the playing area, so a knock forward can happen there.

questions.stem: What is the normal sanction for a knock forward?
questions.explanation: An unintentional knock forward is sanctioned with a scrum.

questions.stem: A player knocks the ball forward and it rolls into touch. What options does the non-offending team have?

options.text: A scrum, a quick throw or a lineout

questions.explanation: If a knock forward goes into touch, the non-offending team may take a quick throw or lineout in place of the scrum.

questions.stem: A knock forward sends the ball into touch. Which team may choose a lineout in place of the scrum?

options.text: The team that knocked the ball forward
The team in whose half it happened

questions.explanation: The choice of a quick throw or lineout instead of the scrum belongs to the non-offending team.

questions.stem: A knock forward sends the ball into touch. May the non-offending team take a quick throw?

options.text: No, a scrum must be taken
No, only a formed lineout is allowed
Only if the knock forward was deliberate
Yes, a quick throw may replace the scrum

questions.explanation: The non-offending team may opt for a quick throw or a lineout.

questions.stem: A defender attempting a tackle misses the player but hits the ball, which flies forward off the defender's arm. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player who, in tackling or trying to tackle, makes contact with the ball so that it goes forward has knocked it forward.

questions.stem: In making a tackle, a defender's hand hits the ball and sends it towards the ball-carrier's own try line. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: The ball went forward from the defender's point of view after contact in the tackle, so the defender has knocked it forward.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for intentionally knocking the ball forward with the hand or arm?
questions.explanation: An intentional knock forward is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: A defender sticks out one hand and deliberately slaps a pass forward to break up an attack, with no chance of catching it. What is the decision?

options.text: Penalty for an intentional knock forward

questions.explanation: Deliberately knocking the ball forward with the hand or arm is penalised.

questions.stem: Does the law on intentional knock forward cover a ball knocked with the arm as well as the hand?

options.text: Yes, it covers the hand or arm
Only if the fist is closed

questions.explanation: A player must not intentionally knock the ball forward with the hand or the arm.

questions.stem: A defender reaches for an interception with a realistic chance of catching the ball, but knocks it forward. What is the decision?

options.text: Penalty for an intentional knock forward
Scrum for a knock forward, as it was not intentional

questions.explanation: A genuine attempt to catch, with a reasonable expectation of gaining possession, is not an intentional knock forward.

questions.stem: What test decides whether a failed catch that goes forward is an intentional knock forward?

options.text: Whether the player could reasonably expect to gain possession
Whether the player used one hand or two
Whether the ball travelled more than a metre
Whether the player was in their own half

questions.explanation: It is not intentional if the player was trying to catch the ball with a reasonable expectation of gaining possession.

questions.stem: Reaching one-handed for a pass with no realistic chance of catching it, a defender knocks the ball forward. How should the referee treat it?
questions.explanation: Without a reasonable expectation of gaining possession, the knock forward is treated as intentional.

questions.stem: A player charges down an opponent's kick and the ball goes forward off the player's hands. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: There is no sanction for knocking the ball forward immediately after an opponent has kicked it.

questions.stem: What do the laws call knocking the ball forward immediately after an opponent has kicked it?
questions.explanation: Knocking the ball forward straight after an opponent's kick is a charge down, and play continues.

questions.stem: For a block of an opponent's kick to count as a charge down, when must the ball be knocked?

options.text: At any point in the ball's flight
Before the opponent's foot touches it
Immediately after the opponent has kicked it

questions.explanation: A charge down is a knock forward made immediately after the opponent has kicked the ball.

questions.stem: A player charges down a kick with the arms, the ball goes forward, and the same player regathers it and grounds it in in-goal. What is the decision?

options.text: Penalty for an intentional knock forward

questions.explanation: A charge down brings no sanction and play continues, so the try stands.

questions.stem: In which of these cases does a ball going forward off a player's hands bring no sanction?

options.text: A one-handed slap at a pass
A fumbled catch from a kick-off
A charge down of an opponent's kick

questions.explanation: Play continues after a charge down, and when the ball is ripped from an opponent and goes forward from the opponent's hands.

questions.stem: A defender rips the ball from the ball-carrier's grasp and it falls forward from the ball-carrier's hands, towards the defender's own try line. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: When the ball is ripped or knocked from an opponent and goes forward from the opponent's hand or arm, there is no sanction.

questions.stem: A defender knocks the ball out of the ball-carrier's hands and it travels forward from the ball-carrier's hands. Who, if anyone, is sanctioned?

options.text: The defender, for an intentional knock forward
The ball-carrier, for a knock forward
The defender, for a knock forward

questions.explanation: There is no sanction when a player knocks the ball from an opponent and it goes forward from the opponent's hand or arm.

questions.stem: How do the laws decide whether a pass is a throw forward?

options.text: By whether the ball lands ahead of where it was thrown
By whether the ball crosses a line on the pitch
By whether the passer's arms move forward
By whether the receiver is ahead of the passer

questions.explanation: A throw forward is a pass in which the arms of the player passing the ball move forward.

questions.stem: A player sprinting upfield passes with the arms moving backwards, but momentum carries the ball so it is caught ahead of where it was released. Is this a throw forward?

options.text: No, the passer's arms did not move forward
Only if the receiver was ahead of the passer
Yes, the ball travelled forward over the ground
Yes, if it gained more than a metre

questions.explanation: The test is the movement of the passer's arms, not where the ball ends up over the ground.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for an unintentional throw forward?
questions.explanation: An unintentional throw forward is sanctioned with a scrum.

questions.stem: Where in the playing area can a throw forward occur?

options.text: Only in the field of play

questions.explanation: A throw forward may occur anywhere in the playing area.

questions.stem: A pass is thrown forward by mistake inside a team's own in-goal. Can a throw forward be given there?

options.text: Only if an attacker is nearby
Yes, anywhere in the playing area
No, only in the field of play

questions.explanation: In-goal is part of the playing area, so a throw forward can be given there.

questions.stem: A pass goes forward out of the hands and is caught by a team-mate, with no intention to throw it forward. What does the referee award?
questions.explanation: An accidental throw forward is sanctioned with a scrum.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for intentionally throwing or passing the ball forward?
questions.explanation: Deliberately throwing or passing the ball forward is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: With the defence closing in, a player deliberately throws the ball forward to a team-mate. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: An intentional throw forward is penalised, unlike an accidental one, which is a scrum.

questions.stem: What separates a throw forward that earns a scrum from one that earns a penalty?

options.text: How far forward the ball travelled
Where on the field it happened

questions.explanation: An accidental throw forward is a scrum. An intentional one is a penalty.

questions.stem: What separates a knock forward that earns a scrum from one that earns a penalty?

options.text: How far forward the ball travelled
Whether an opponent picked it up
Where on the field it happened

questions.explanation: An accidental knock forward is a scrum. An intentional one is a penalty.

questions.stem: Which of these describes a charge down?

options.text: Tackling an opponent just as the ball is kicked
Blocking an opponent's pass with one outstretched hand
Knocking the ball forward immediately after an opponent kicks it
Catching an opponent's kick before it touches the ground

questions.explanation: Knocking the ball forward immediately after an opponent has kicked it is a charge down, and play continues.

questions.stem: A player hands the ball to a team-mate who is slightly ahead, with the arms moving forward. What is this?
questions.explanation: A pass includes handing the ball to another player, and it is a throw forward if the passer's arms move forward.

questions.stem: A player deliberately bats a high ball forward with an open hand to a team-mate, who catches it. What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, as a team-mate caught it
Penalty for an intentional knock forward

questions.explanation: The ball was hit forward with the hand and touched another player. Doing so intentionally is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: What are kick-offs used for?

options.text: To restart play after a missed penalty goal attempt
To restart play after the ball goes into touch-in-goal
To restart play after every stoppage
To start each half of the match and each period of extra-time

questions.explanation: Kick-offs start each half and each period of extra-time. Restart kicks are used to resume play.

questions.stem: What kind of kick must a kick-off be?

options.text: Either a place-kick or a drop-kick

questions.explanation: All kick-offs and restart kicks are drop-kicks.

questions.stem: A player takes the kick-off with a place-kick from a tee. What may the non-kicking team choose?

options.text: To have the kick retaken, or a scrum
A lineout on the half-way line

questions.explanation: A kick-off that is not a drop-kick gives the non-kicking team the option of a retake or a scrum.

questions.stem: From where is a kick-off taken?

options.text: On or behind the kicking team's 22-metre line
On or behind the centre of the half-way line

questions.explanation: A kick-off is taken on or behind the centre of the half-way line.

questions.stem: A kick-off is taken from the half-way line but ten metres to one side of the centre. What may the non-kicking team choose?

options.text: A lineout where the ball lands
To have the kick retaken, or a scrum

questions.explanation: A kick-off taken from the wrong place gives the non-kicking team the option of a retake or a scrum.

questions.stem: Which team kicks off the second half?

options.text: The team that kicked off the match
The team that is behind on the scoreboard
The opponents of the team that kicked off the match
The winner of a second toss

questions.explanation: The second half is started by the opponents of the team that kicked off the match.

questions.stem: Where must the kicker's team-mates be when a kick-off is taken?

options.text: Within five metres of the kicker

questions.explanation: Team-mates of the kicker must be behind the ball when it is kicked.

questions.stem: A team-mate of the kicker is in front of the ball when the kick-off is taken. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Team-mates in front of the ball at a kick-off are sanctioned with a scrum.

questions.stem: Where must the receiving team be when a kick-off is taken?

options.text: At least five metres from the half-way line

questions.explanation: Opposition players must be on or behind the 10-metre line when the ball is kicked.

questions.stem: A receiving player is in front of the 10-metre line when the kick-off is taken. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: If opponents are in front of the 10-metre line when the ball is kicked, the kick is retaken.

questions.stem: Which line must the ball reach from a kick-off?
questions.explanation: A kick-off must reach the 10-metre line.

questions.stem: A kick-off does not reach the 10-metre line and no opponent plays it. What may the non-kicking team choose?

options.text: To have the kick retaken, or a scrum
A lineout on the half-way line

questions.explanation: A kick-off that falls short gives the non-kicking team the option of a retake or a scrum.

questions.stem: A kick-off travels eight metres and a player of the kicking team gathers it. What may the non-kicking team choose?

options.text: To have the kick retaken, or a scrum

questions.explanation: The ball did not reach the 10-metre line and no opponent played it, so the non-kicking team has the option of a retake or a scrum.

questions.stem: A kick-off reaches the 10-metre line and is then blown back by the wind. What happens?
questions.explanation: Once the ball has reached the 10-metre line, play continues even if the wind blows it back.

questions.stem: A kick-off is falling short of the 10-metre line when an opponent steps forward and catches it. What happens?
questions.explanation: If an opponent plays the ball before it reaches the 10-metre line, play continues.

questions.stem: A kick-off goes directly into touch. How many options does the non-kicking team have?

options.text: Four: a retake, a scrum, a lineout or a quick throw
Two: a retake or a scrum
Three: a retake, a scrum or a lineout
One: a scrum at the centre

questions.explanation: When a kick-off goes directly into touch, the non-kicking team chooses between a retake, a scrum, a lineout and a quick throw.

questions.stem: A kick-off goes directly into touch. Which of these may the non-kicking team choose?
questions.explanation: The four options are a retake, a scrum, a lineout or a quick throw.

questions.stem: A kick-off bounces in the field of play and then rolls into touch. Do the options for a kick directly into touch apply?

options.text: Yes, if it bounced only once
Yes, any kick-off into touch gives the four options
No, the ball was not kicked directly into touch
Only if it went out beyond the 22-metre line

questions.explanation: A ball is kicked directly into touch only if it goes out without first landing in the playing area or touching a player or the referee.

questions.stem: A kick-off flies untouched into the opponents' in-goal and a defender grounds it at once. What may the non-kicking team choose?

options.text: To have the kick retaken, or a scrum

questions.explanation: When a kick-off reaches in-goal untouched and is grounded without delay, the non-kicking team may have a retake or a scrum.

questions.stem: A kick-off rolls untouched through the opponents' in-goal and over the dead-ball line. What may the non-kicking team choose?

options.text: To have the kick retaken, or a scrum

questions.explanation: A kick-off that goes dead through in-goal without touching a player gives the option of a retake or a scrum.

questions.stem: A kick-off lands untouched in the opponents' in-goal. To keep the option of a retake or a scrum, how quickly must a defender ground the ball?
questions.explanation: The option applies when an opponent grounds the ball without delay.

questions.stem: A kick-off is blown back into the kicking team's own in-goal, where a player of that team makes it dead. What is awarded?

options.text: A five-metre scrum to the non-kicking team

questions.explanation: If the ball goes into the kicking team's own in-goal and is made dead there, the non-kicking team gets a five-metre scrum.

questions.stem: What are restart kicks used for?

options.text: To end a period of advantage

questions.explanation: Restart kicks resume play, for example after a score.

questions.stem: What kind of kick is a restart kick after a score?
questions.explanation: Play is restarted after a score with a drop-kick.

questions.stem: After a team has scored, who restarts play?

options.text: The team that kicked off the half
The opponents of the team that scored
The team that lost the toss

questions.explanation: After a score, the opponents of the scoring team restart play.

questions.stem: After a score, from where is play restarted?

options.text: At the place where the score was made
On or behind the centre of the half-way line
On the 10-metre line of the team that conceded

questions.explanation: The restart kick is taken on or behind the centre of the half-way line.

questions.stem: A restart kick after a try is taken from the wrong place. What may the non-kicking team choose?

options.text: To have the kick retaken, or a scrum

questions.explanation: A restart kick from the wrong place gives the non-kicking team the option of a retake or a scrum.

questions.stem: A penalty kick at goal misses and a defender grounds the ball in in-goal. How does play restart?

options.text: With a scrum at the place of the penalty

questions.explanation: A failed penalty goal attempt that the defending team grounds or makes dead in in-goal leads to a 22-metre drop-out.

questions.stem: A dropped goal attempt misses and the ball rolls over the dead-ball line. How does play restart?

options.text: With a scrum where the kick was taken

questions.explanation: When an unsuccessful dropped goal or penalty goal attempt goes dead through in-goal, play restarts with a 22-metre drop-out.

questions.stem: Which of these leads to a 22-metre drop-out?

options.text: An attacker being held up over the try line
An attacker knocking forward in in-goal
A punt in open play grounded in in-goal by a defender
A missed penalty goal attempt made dead in in-goal by the defenders

questions.explanation: The 22-metre drop-out follows an unsuccessful penalty goal or dropped goal attempt. The other three lead to a try line drop-out.

questions.stem: From where is a 22-metre drop-out taken?

options.text: On or behind the half-way line
On or behind the defending team's try line
On or behind the defending team's 22-metre line

questions.explanation: A 22-metre drop-out is taken on or behind the defending team's 22-metre line.

questions.stem: What is the sanction line for a 22-metre drop-out?
questions.explanation: For a 22-metre drop-out the sanction line is the 22-metre line itself.

questions.stem: An attacker carries the ball over the try line and is held up by defenders. How does play restart?

options.text: With a 5-metre scrum to the attacking team
With a 5-metre scrum to the defending team

questions.explanation: When an attacker takes the ball into in-goal and it is held up, play restarts with a try line drop-out.

questions.stem: An attacker carries the ball into in-goal, loses it, and a defender grounds it there. How does play restart?

options.text: With a scrum on the 22-metre line
With a 5-metre scrum to the attacking team

questions.explanation: A ball taken into in-goal by an attacker and then grounded by an opponent leads to a try line drop-out.

questions.stem: An attacker's grubber kick in open play rolls into in-goal, where a defender grounds it. How does play restart?

options.text: With a 5-metre scrum to the attacking team
With a scrum where the kick was made

questions.explanation: An attacking kick in open play that the defenders ground or make dead in in-goal leads to a try line drop-out.

questions.stem: Which attacking kick, when grounded in in-goal by a defender, leads to a try line drop-out?
questions.explanation: Kick-offs, restart kicks, drop-outs, dropped goal attempts and penalty attempts are excluded. A punt in open play is not.

questions.stem: An attacking player knocks the ball forward in the opponents' in-goal. How does play restart?

options.text: With a 5-metre scrum to the defending team
With a scrum where the player last had the ball

questions.explanation: An attacker knocking forward in the opponents' in-goal results in a try line drop-out.

questions.stem: From where is a try line drop-out taken?

options.text: On or behind the dead-ball line
On or behind the defending team's try line
On or behind the defending team's 22-metre line

questions.explanation: A try line drop-out is taken on or behind the defending team's try line.

questions.stem: What is the sanction line for a try line drop-out?
questions.explanation: For a try line drop-out the sanction line is the five-metre line.

questions.stem: Which line must a try line drop-out cross?
questions.explanation: A drop-out must cross its sanction line, which for a try line drop-out is the five-metre line.

questions.stem: What kind of kick is used for a drop-out?
questions.explanation: Drop-outs are restart kicks, and all restart kicks are drop-kicks.

questions.stem: A player punts a 22-metre drop-out out of the hands instead of drop-kicking it. What may the non-kicking team choose?

options.text: To have the kick retaken, or a scrum

questions.explanation: A restart kick that is not a drop-kick gives the non-kicking team the option of a retake or a scrum.

questions.stem: A drop-out is taken from the wrong place. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A drop-out not taken at the specified location is sanctioned with a scrum.

questions.stem: A team delays taking a drop-out. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A drop-out must be taken without delay. Delay is sanctioned with a free-kick.

questions.stem: A drop-out fails to cross its sanction line. What may the non-kicking team choose?

options.text: To have the kick retaken, or a scrum
A free-kick on the sanction line
A penalty on the sanction line
A lineout level with the sanction line

questions.explanation: If the drop-out does not cross the sanction line, the non-kicking team may choose a retake or a scrum.

questions.stem: A drop-out goes directly into touch. What may the opposing team choose?

options.text: A free-kick, a penalty or a scrum
A lineout or a quick throw, but not a scrum
A retake, a scrum, a lineout or a quick throw
A retake or a scrum, but not a lineout

questions.explanation: A drop-out kicked directly into touch gives the opposing team four options: retake, scrum, lineout or quick throw.

questions.stem: An opponent moves in front of the sanction line before a drop-out is kicked. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Opponents must not advance in front of the sanction line before the kick. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: An opponent in front of the sanction line deliberately delays a drop-out. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: An opponent in front of the sanction line who delays or obstructs the drop-out concedes a penalty.

questions.stem: Two offences by opponents at a drop-out carry different sanctions. Which pairing is correct?

options.text: Advancing early is a free-kick; obstructing the kick is a penalty
Advancing early and obstructing the kick are both penalties
Advancing early is a penalty; obstructing the kick is a free-kick
Advancing early and obstructing the kick are both free-kicks

questions.explanation: Crossing the sanction line early costs a free-kick. Delaying or obstructing the drop-out from in front of that line costs a penalty.

questions.stem: A drop-out crosses the sanction line and is then blown back. What happens?
questions.explanation: Once the ball has crossed the sanction line, play continues even if it is blown back.

questions.stem: A drop-out does not cross the sanction line, but the opposing team gathers the ball with a chance to attack. What may the referee do?

options.text: Award a scrum in every case
Order a retake in every case

questions.explanation: If the ball does not cross the sanction line, advantage may apply.

questions.stem: A 22-metre drop-out carries untouched into the opponents' in-goal and a defender grounds it at once. What may the non-kicking team choose?

options.text: A free-kick where the kick was taken
To have the kick retaken, or a scrum

questions.explanation: A drop-out that reaches the opponents' in-goal untouched and is grounded without delay gives the option of a retake or a scrum.

questions.stem: Where must the kicker's team-mates be when a drop-out is taken?

options.text: Within five metres of the kicker

questions.explanation: Team-mates of the kicker must be behind the ball when a drop-out is kicked.

questions.stem: A team-mate of the kicker is in front of the ball at a quickly taken drop-out. How can that player avoid sanction?

options.text: By standing still until the ball lands
By retiring until put onside by a team-mate
By raising a hand to the referee

questions.explanation: Players in front of the ball escape sanction if they retire and do not interfere until a team-mate's action puts them onside.

questions.stem: A team-mate who was in front of the ball at a drop-out interferes with play. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Team-mates in front of the ball at a drop-out who do not retire are sanctioned with a scrum.

questions.stem: Under the principle of this law, by whom is the game played?

options.text: By players on their feet or on their knees
By any player not held by an opponent
By any player within reach of the ball
Only by players who are on their feet

questions.explanation: The principle is that the game is played only by players who are on their feet.

questions.stem: A player lying on the ground wants to take part in play again. What must the player do first?

options.text: Wait for the next phase of play

questions.explanation: The game is played only by players on their feet, so the player has to get up first.

questions.stem: When is a player off their feet under the definitions?

options.text: When the player is held by an opponent and no longer moving forward
Only when the player is lying flat with the back or chest on the ground
Only when both of the player's knees are on the ground together
When any other part of the body is supported by the ground or grounded players

questions.explanation: A player is off their feet when any part of the body other than the feet is supported by the ground or by players who are on the ground.

questions.stem: When is a player on their feet under the definitions?

options.text: When no other part of the body is supported by the ground or grounded players
When both of the player's knees are clear of the ground
When the player's upper body is upright and above the hips
When at least one of the player's feet is in contact with the ground

questions.explanation: A player is on their feet only if nothing but the feet is supported by the ground or by players on the ground.

questions.stem: A player has one knee on the ground and reaches for the ball. Under the definitions, is the player on their feet?

options.text: Yes, if nobody is holding the player
Yes, one foot is still on the ground
No, a knee is supported by the ground
Yes, unless both knees are down

questions.explanation: With a knee on the ground, a part of the body other than the feet is supported, so the player is off their feet.

questions.stem: A player is leaning with their weight on a team-mate who is lying on the ground. Is the player on their feet?

options.text: No, the player is supported by a player on the ground
Yes, unless the player's knees touch the ground
Yes, both feet are on the ground
Yes, because the player's hands are not on the ground

questions.explanation: Being supported by players who are on the ground means a player is off their feet.

questions.stem: How quickly must a player who goes to ground with the ball act?
questions.explanation: A player who goes to ground with the ball, or to gather it, must act immediately.

questions.stem: Which three options does a player have after going to ground with the ball?

options.text: Release it, roll away, or wait for a ruck
Pass it, kick it, or hold it until tackled
Get up with it, kick it, or release it
Get up with it, play it without kicking, or release it

questions.explanation: The player must immediately get up with the ball, play it (but not kick it), or release it.

questions.stem: A player dives on a loose ball and gathers it on the ground. Which of these may the player do next?

options.text: Lie on the ball until support arrives
Kick the ball away while on the ground
Hold the ball until an opponent arrives

questions.explanation: Getting up with the ball is one of the three things the player may do immediately.

questions.stem: A player dives on a loose ball, gets straight back up with it and runs on. What is the decision?

options.text: Penalty for playing the ball on the ground

questions.explanation: Getting up with the ball immediately is exactly what the law allows.

questions.stem: A player on the ground with the ball passes it to a team-mate straight away. Is this allowed?

options.text: Only if no opponent is within a metre
No, the player must get up first
No, the ball must be released on the ground
Yes, the player may play the ball immediately

questions.explanation: A player who has gone to ground with the ball may play it immediately, as long as it is not kicked.

questions.stem: A player who has gone to ground to gather the ball kicks it away while still lying down. What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, because the ball was moved away
Free-kick, because it was a technical offence
Penalty, because the ball may be played but not kicked
Scrum, because the ball went forward

questions.explanation: A player on the ground with the ball may play it but is not allowed to kick it.

questions.stem: Which action is excluded when a player on the ground with the ball plays it?
questions.explanation: The law allows the player to play the ball, but not to kick it.

questions.stem: A player goes to ground with the ball and can neither get up nor pass. What must the player do?

options.text: Hold on until a team-mate arrives
Roll over to shield the ball

questions.explanation: If the player does not get up or play the ball, it must be released at once.

questions.stem: A player goes to ground with the ball and holds on to it so that nobody can play it. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Failing to get up, play or release the ball immediately is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: A player goes to ground with the ball and takes several seconds to release it, slowing the opposition. What is the decision?

options.text: Penalty, because the player did not act immediately
Play on, because the ball was released in the end
Scrum, because the ball became unplayable

questions.explanation: The player must get up, play or release the ball immediately, not after a delay.

questions.stem: A full-back falls on a rolling ball near their own try line as attackers arrive. What must the full-back do at once?

options.text: Hold on to it until a team-mate arrives and binds on
Wait on the ground until an attacker makes contact
Get up with the ball, play it without kicking, or release it
Curl around it and wait for the referee's whistle

questions.explanation: Any player who goes to ground to gather the ball has the same three immediate options.

questions.stem: To whom does the duty to act immediately on the ground apply?

options.text: Only the first player to reach the ball
Any player who goes to ground with or for the ball
Only players who have been tackled

questions.explanation: It covers players who go to ground to gather the ball and players who go to ground with the ball.

questions.stem: A player on the ground has released the ball. What must the player do next?

options.text: Stay over the ball until it is picked up
Push the ball back to a team-mate
Immediately move away from the ball or get up
Stay still so as not to interfere

questions.explanation: Once the ball is played or released, players on the ground must at once move away from it or get up.

questions.stem: After passing the ball from the ground, a player stays lying where the ball was played, in the way of opponents. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Players on the ground must move away or get up as soon as the ball has been played or released.

questions.stem: Once the ball has been played or released, how quickly must players on the ground move away or get up?

options.text: When the ball has travelled five metres

questions.explanation: The duty to move away from the ball or get up is immediate.

questions.stem: After releasing the ball on the ground, a player rolls towards the ball instead of away from it. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: After the ball is released, a player on the ground must move away from it or get up.

questions.stem: A player on the ground releases the ball and at once gets to their feet. May the player then play the ball again?

options.text: Only once the ball has moved a metre
No, the player is out of the game until the next phase
Only after an opponent has touched the ball
Yes, a player back on their feet may play the ball

questions.explanation: The game is played by players on their feet, so a player who has got up may take part again.

questions.stem: A player is on the ground in the field of play without the ball. What is the player's status?

options.text: In the game if within a metre of the ball
In the game if facing the opposition's try line
In the game if not being held

questions.explanation: A player on the ground in the field of play without the ball is out of the game.

questions.stem: Where does the rule that a player on the ground without the ball is out of the game apply?

options.text: Only within a metre of a touchline

questions.explanation: The law refers to a player on the ground, without the ball, in the field of play.

questions.stem: What must a player on the ground without the ball allow opponents who are on their feet to do?

options.text: Play or gain possession of the ball
Kick the ball into touch only
Step over without touching the ball
Form a scrum over the ball

questions.explanation: The player must let opponents who are not on the ground play the ball or gain possession of it.

questions.stem: An opponent on their feet bends to pick up a ball lying next to a player on the ground. What must the player on the ground do?

options.text: Knock the ball away with a hand
Allow the opponent to play or take the ball

questions.explanation: A player on the ground without the ball must allow opponents on their feet to play or gain possession.

questions.stem: A player lying on the ground reaches out and scoops a loose ball back to a team-mate. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player on the ground without the ball is out of the game and must not play the ball.

questions.stem: A player slips over and the ball rolls against the player's body. The player stays down and traps the ball with an arm. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player on the ground without the ball must not play it, and trapping it is playing it.

questions.stem: A player on the ground without the ball grabs the legs of an opponent running past with the ball. What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, because a tackle has been made
Free-kick, because it was a minor offence
Penalty, because a player on the ground must not tackle
Scrum, because the ball became unplayable

questions.explanation: A player on the ground without the ball must not tackle or try to tackle an opponent.

questions.stem: Which of these is forbidden to a player who is on the ground without the ball?

options.text: Letting an opponent pick up the ball

questions.explanation: Such a player must not play the ball or tackle, and must let opponents on their feet play the ball.

questions.stem: What is the sanction when a player on the ground without the ball plays the ball?
questions.explanation: Interfering with play while on the ground without the ball is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: A player on their feet dives on top of an opponent who is on the ground holding the ball. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players on their feet must not fall on or over players on the ground who have the ball.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for falling on or over a player who is on the ground with the ball?
questions.explanation: Falling on or over players on the ground who have the ball, or are near it, is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: Players on their feet must not fall on or over a player on the ground who has the ball. Does this also cover players on the ground who are near the ball?

options.text: Only if the player on the ground is an opponent
No, only a player holding the ball
Yes, it covers players who have the ball or are near it

questions.explanation: The ban applies to players on the ground who have the ball or who are near it.

questions.stem: In the laws, "near" means within what distance?
questions.explanation: The definitions say that near means within one metre.

questions.stem: A player on their feet deliberately flops over a team-mate who is on the ground with the ball, to shield it. What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, as they are team-mates

questions.explanation: The law forbids falling on or over any player on the ground with the ball, team-mate or opponent.

questions.stem: Which players does the law forbid from falling on or over players on the ground with the ball?

options.text: Players on their feet without the ball
Only opponents of the player on the ground
Only the first player to arrive

questions.explanation: The restriction is on players who are on their feet and do not have the ball.

questions.stem: A player is kneeling on one knee beside the ball and picks it up without standing. What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, because one foot was on the ground
Free-kick, because it was a technical offence
Penalty, because the player was off their feet
Scrum, because the ball was not played correctly

questions.explanation: A player with a knee on the ground is off their feet, and a player on the ground without the ball must not play it.

questions.stem: A player goes to ground to gather the ball. Which of these is the only one the law permits?

options.text: Lying over the ball to protect it
Holding the ball until support arrives
Kicking the ball clear from the ground

questions.explanation: The player must immediately get up with the ball, play it without kicking, or release it.

questions.stem: A player goes to ground with the ball and at once places it back for a team-mate. Is this allowed?

options.text: No, the player must get up with the ball
Only if no opponent is within a metre
No, the ball must be passed and not placed
Yes, releasing the ball immediately is one of the options

questions.explanation: A player who goes to ground with the ball may release it immediately.

questions.stem: A player dives on a loose ball, and an opponent on their feet immediately tries to take it. The player on the ground holds on. Who has offended?

options.text: No one, as a ruck has formed
No one, as play simply continues

questions.explanation: A player who goes to ground to gather the ball must immediately get up with it, play it or release it. Holding on is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: Two things are open to a player on the ground once the ball has been played or released. What are they?

options.text: Stay still, or roll towards the ball
Get up, or hold on to an opponent
Lie over the ball, or push it back
Move away from the ball, or get up

questions.explanation: Once the ball is played or released, players on the ground must immediately move away from it or get up.

questions.stem: A player is knocked to the ground in open play, and the ball then rolls to within reach. What may the player do?

options.text: Play the ball while still on the ground
Trap the ball until a team-mate arrives
Get to their feet and then play the ball
Tackle the next ball-carrier from the ground

questions.explanation: A player on the ground without the ball is out of the game and must not play the ball, so the player must first get up.

questions.stem: A player on the ground without the ball lies in the way, so that an opponent on their feet cannot reach the ball. Which duty has the player failed in?

options.text: To let opponents on their feet play the ball
To stay still until play has moved on
To get up within three seconds

questions.explanation: A player on the ground without the ball must allow opponents who are not on the ground to play or gain possession of the ball.

questions.stem: Which of these does the law forbid for a player who is on their feet without the ball?

options.text: Tackling a ball-carrier who has got back up
Stepping over a player on the ground to follow play
Picking up a ball lying near a player on the ground
Falling on or over a player on the ground who has the ball

questions.explanation: Players on their feet and without the ball must not fall on or over players on the ground who have the ball or are near it.

questions.stem: Where can a tackle take place?

options.text: Anywhere in the field of play
Anywhere in the playing area, in-goal included

questions.explanation: The principle of the law is that a tackle can take place anywhere in the field of play.

questions.stem: What does the principle of the tackle law say players' actions must allow?

options.text: The ball to be available for play immediately
The tackler to regain their feet first
The referee to reach the tackle

questions.explanation: Players involved in the tackle must ensure a fair contest and allow the ball to be available for play immediately.

questions.stem: What two things must happen to the ball-carrier for a tackle to occur?

options.text: The ball-carrier is stopped and loses the ball
The ball-carrier is knocked over by any contact
The ball-carrier is held and brought to ground
The ball-carrier is held and stops moving forward

questions.explanation: A tackle needs the ball-carrier to be both held and brought to ground by one or more opponents.

questions.stem: How many opponents are needed to make a tackle?
questions.explanation: A tackle is made when the ball-carrier is held and brought to ground by one or more opponents.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier is held by two opponents and stays on their feet. Has a tackle occurred?

options.text: No, the ball-carrier has not been brought to ground
Only if a team-mate also binds on
Yes, the ball-carrier is held by opponents
Yes, once forward movement has stopped

questions.explanation: A tackle needs the ball-carrier to be held and brought to ground. A player held on their feet has not been tackled.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier trips on the turf and falls with no opponent holding them. Has a tackle occurred?

options.text: Only if the ball touches the ground
Yes, the ball-carrier is on the ground
No, the ball-carrier was not held by an opponent
Yes, if an opponent is within a metre

questions.explanation: With no opponent holding the ball-carrier there is no tackle. The player is simply on the ground with the ball.

questions.stem: A held ball-carrier has one knee on the ground. Has the ball-carrier been brought to ground?

options.text: No, the player must be lying or sitting
Only if the ball also touches the ground
No, both knees must be down
Yes, one knee on the ground is enough

questions.explanation: Brought to ground means lying, sitting, or having at least one knee on the ground or on another player who is on the ground.

questions.stem: A held ball-carrier ends up sitting on top of a tackler who is lying on the ground. Has the ball-carrier been brought to ground?

options.text: No, unless a knee touches the grass
Yes, being on a player who is on the ground counts
No, the ball-carrier has not touched the ground
Only if the tackler then lets go

questions.explanation: Being brought to ground includes lying, sitting or having a knee on another player who is on the ground.

questions.stem: Which of these positions counts as being brought to ground in a tackle?

options.text: Bent over with one hand on the ground
Crouching with both feet on the ground
Leaning on an opponent who is standing

questions.explanation: Brought to ground means lying, sitting or having at least one knee on the ground or on a player who is on the ground.

questions.stem: How many knees must a held ball-carrier have on the ground to be brought to ground?

options.text: Both, with the ball also on the ground

questions.explanation: The ball-carrier is brought to ground when lying, sitting or with at least one knee on the ground.

questions.stem: In a tackle, how long must a tackler keep hold for the ball-carrier to count as held?

options.text: Until the ball-carrier stops moving forward
Until the ball has been released
Until the ball-carrier is on the ground

questions.explanation: Being held means a tackler continues to hold the ball-carrier until the ball-carrier is on the ground.

questions.stem: A defender grabs the ball-carrier's ankle and lets go, and the ball-carrier then stumbles to the ground with nobody holding them. Has a tackle occurred?

options.text: Yes, any contact that causes a fall is a tackle
No, the ball-carrier was not held when going to ground
Only if the ball-carrier stays down
Yes, the defender caused the fall

questions.explanation: Being held means the tackler keeps holding until the ball-carrier is on the ground. A hold that is let go before then is not a tackle.

questions.stem: How do the definitions describe a tackle?

options.text: Holding a ball-carrier and bringing that player to ground
Forcing a ball-carrier to release the ball
Stopping a ball-carrier from moving forward
Making contact with a ball-carrier above the waist

questions.explanation: A tackle is the method of holding a ball-carrier and bringing that player to ground.

questions.stem: Which groups of players does the law list as players in a tackle?

options.text: The tackled player and the tackler or tacklers only
Every player within one metre of the ball
The tackled player, the tackler or tacklers, and others
The tackled player, the tackler and the first arriving player only

questions.explanation: Players in a tackle are the tackled player, the tackler or tacklers, and others such as players who hold without going to ground or arrive to contest.

questions.stem: A defender holds the ball-carrier during a tackle but stays standing. In which group of players in a tackle does the law place this defender?
questions.explanation: A player who holds the ball-carrier during a tackle but does not go to ground is one of the others, not a tackler.

questions.stem: A player was already lying on the ground when a tackle happened right beside them. How does the law class this player?

options.text: As having no part in the tackle
As one of the other players in the tackle

questions.explanation: Players who are already on the ground are listed among the other players in a tackle.

questions.stem: A player arrives at a tackle to contest possession. How does the law class this player?

options.text: As one of the other players in the tackle
As a tackled player, once in contact
As a tackler, like the first defender
As a player in a ruck, from that moment

questions.explanation: Players who arrive to contest possession in the tackle are listed among the other players.

questions.stem: Under the definitions, what must an opponent do, as well as hold the tackled player, to be a tackler?
questions.explanation: A tackler is an opposition player who holds the tackled player and goes to ground.

questions.stem: Two defenders bring a ball-carrier down. One goes to ground with the ball-carrier and the other stays standing. Who is a tackler under the definitions?

options.text: Only the defender who went to ground
Only the defender who stayed standing

questions.explanation: A tackler holds the tackled player and goes to ground. The defender who stayed standing is one of the other players.

questions.stem: How do the definitions describe a tackled player?

options.text: Any player on the ground within a metre of the ball
A ball-carrier who is held by one or more opponents
A ball-carrier who falls to the ground for any reason
A ball-carrier who is held and taken to ground by a tackler or tacklers

questions.explanation: A tackled player is a ball-carrier who is held and taken to ground by a tackler or tacklers.

questions.stem: What do the definitions call the first team-mate of the tackler to arrive at the tackle?
questions.explanation: The jackler, or stealer, is the first arriving team-mate of the tackler at the tackle.

questions.stem: How must a jackler contest for the ball at a tackle?

options.text: With one knee on the ground for balance
On their feet and directly onto the ball
Only once a ruck has formed
From whichever side of the tackle is open

questions.explanation: A jackler must remain on their feet to contest directly onto the ball.

questions.stem: A player helps to make a tackle while staying on their feet and then wants to contest for the ball as the jackler. What must the player do first?

options.text: Retreat one metre from the tackle
Wait for a team-mate to arrive
Go to ground and get back up

questions.explanation: A jackler who was involved in the tackle must first clearly release the ball-carrier before contesting for the ball.

questions.stem: After a tackler and the ball-carrier have both gone to ground, what must the tackler do with the ball and the ball-carrier?

options.text: Release them once a ruck forms
Release the player but keep the ball

questions.explanation: Tacklers must immediately release the ball and the ball-carrier after both players go to ground.

questions.stem: How quickly must a tackler release the ball and the ball-carrier once both players are on the ground?
questions.explanation: Release must be immediate after both players go to ground.

questions.stem: A tackler brings the ball-carrier down and keeps both arms wrapped around the player on the ground for several seconds. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Once both players are on the ground the tackler must release the ball and the ball-carrier immediately.

questions.stem: After releasing, what must a tackler on the ground do next?

options.text: Lie between the ball and the opposition
Move away from the tackled player and the ball, or get up
Stay still until the ball has gone
Roll towards the ball to protect it

questions.explanation: Tacklers must immediately move away from the tackled player and from the ball, or get up.

questions.stem: A tackler releases the ball-carrier but stays lying beside the ball, in the way of arriving opponents. What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, as the tackler released

questions.explanation: Releasing is not enough. The tackler must also move away from the tackled player and the ball at once, or get up.

questions.stem: What must a tackler do before attempting to play the ball after a tackle?

options.text: Wait until the tackled player stands up
Let a team-mate play it first

questions.explanation: A tackler must be on their feet before attempting to play the ball.

questions.stem: A tackler, still on their knees after the tackle, reaches over and takes the ball from the tackled player. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A tackler must be on their feet before attempting to play the ball, and a kneeling player is off their feet.

questions.stem: A tackler lies on top of the tackled player so that the ball cannot be released. What is the decision?

options.text: Scrum to the team going forward

questions.explanation: Tacklers must allow the tackled player to release or play the ball.

questions.stem: After a tackle, the tackler keeps a grip on the tackled player's legs so the player cannot move away from the ball. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Tacklers must allow the tackled player to move away from the ball.

questions.stem: What is the sanction when a tackler fails to release the tackled player?
questions.explanation: A tackler who does not meet the tackler's responsibilities is penalised.

questions.stem: Which of these is one of a tackler's responsibilities after a tackle?

options.text: Playing the ball from whichever side is nearest
Staying on the ground until the ball has gone
Allowing the tackled player to release or play the ball
Holding the tackled player until a ruck forms

questions.explanation: Tacklers must release, move away or get up, be on their feet before playing the ball, and let the tackled player release, play or move away from the ball.

questions.stem: From which direction may a tackler who has got back to their feet play the ball?

options.text: From the opposition's side of the tackle
From the side nearest the touchline
From the direction of their own try line

questions.explanation: A tackler who has met their responsibilities may play the ball from the direction of their own try line, provided a ruck has not formed.

questions.stem: A tackler releases, gets up at once and wants to play the ball from their own side. What else must be true?

options.text: The tackled player has stood up
The ball has left the tackle

questions.explanation: Tacklers may play the ball from the direction of their own try line as long as they have met their responsibilities and no ruck has formed.

questions.stem: A tackler ends up on the opposition's side of the tackle, gets up and plays the ball from there. Is this allowed?

options.text: Yes, a tackler may play the ball from any side
Only if no opponent is over the ball
No, a tackler must play it from the direction of their own try line
Yes, as long as the tackler is on their feet

questions.explanation: A tackler who has got up may play the ball only from the direction of their own try line.

questions.stem: How quickly must a tackled player make the ball available?

options.text: When a team-mate is in position

questions.explanation: A tackled player must immediately make the ball available so that play can continue.

questions.stem: Which direction is ruled out when a tackled player passes or pushes the ball?
questions.explanation: A tackled player may release, pass or push the ball in any direction except forward.

questions.stem: In which directions may a tackled player place the ball?

options.text: Only towards their own try line

questions.explanation: A tackled player may release, pass or push the ball in any direction except forward, but may place it in any direction.

questions.stem: A tackled player reaches out and places the ball on the ground ahead of their body. Is this allowed?

options.text: Yes, the ball may be placed in any direction
Only if no opponent is near
