No, the ball must not go forward

questions.explanation: Passing, pushing or releasing the ball forward is ruled out, but placing it is allowed in any direction.

questions.stem: Which of these may a tackled player do with the ball?

options.text: Hold it until a team-mate arrives
Pass it to a team-mate straight away
Keep it until the tackler lets go

questions.explanation: A tackled player must make the ball available immediately by releasing, passing or pushing it.

questions.stem: By which three actions may a tackled player make the ball available?

options.text: Releasing, kicking or rolling on it

questions.explanation: The tackled player makes the ball available by releasing, passing or pushing it, and may also place it.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier is held and brought to ground, then gets back up and runs on without ever letting go of the ball. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A tackled player must immediately make the ball available by releasing, passing or pushing it. Getting up with it is not one of the options.

questions.stem: After making the ball available, what must a tackled player do?

options.text: Move away from the ball or get up
Keep one hand on the ball
Stay still until play moves on

questions.explanation: Tackled players must immediately move away from the ball or get up.

questions.stem: A tackled player places the ball and then lies over it so that the opposition cannot reach it. What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, as the ball was released
Scrum to the team going forward

questions.explanation: Tackled players must not lie on, over or near the ball to stop opponents gaining possession.

questions.stem: A tackled player must not lie near the ball to stop opponents getting it. How close is "near"?
questions.explanation: The definitions say that near means within one metre.

questions.stem: A tackled player holds on to the ball on the ground while an opponent on their feet tries to take it. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A tackled player must immediately make the ball available. Holding on is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: A defender helps to hold the ball-carrier in a tackle but stays standing. What must this defender do once the ball-carrier is on the ground?

options.text: Keep hold of the ball but let go of the player
Release the ball and the ball-carrier immediately
Keep hold until a ruck forms
Go to ground beside the ball-carrier

questions.explanation: Other players must stay on their feet and release the ball and the ball-carrier immediately.

questions.stem: A defender who stayed standing while helping to make a tackle keeps hold of the ball and tries to rip it free without letting go first. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player who holds the ball-carrier in a tackle without going to ground must release the ball and the ball-carrier immediately.

questions.stem: What must players arriving at a tackle do when they play the ball?

options.text: Go to ground over the ball
Keep one knee on the ground

questions.explanation: Other players must remain on their feet when they play the ball.

questions.stem: From which direction must a player arrive at a tackle before playing the ball?

options.text: From the direction of their own try line
From either side of the tackle

questions.explanation: Other players must arrive at the tackle from the direction of their own try line before playing the ball.

questions.stem: An arriving player comes in from the side of a tackle and picks up the ball. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Other players must arrive at the tackle from the direction of their own try line before playing the ball.

questions.stem: A player is lying on the ground within a metre of a tackle and hooks the ball back with a hand. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players must not play the ball while on the ground near the tackle.

questions.stem: A player on the ground near a tackle grabs the legs of an opponent who has just picked up the ball. What is the decision?

options.text: Scrum to the team in possession
Free-kick against the player on the ground
Play on, as a tackle has been made
Penalty against the player on the ground

questions.explanation: Players must not attempt to tackle an opponent while on the ground near the tackle.

questions.stem: An arriving player grabs an opponent who is on their feet over the ball at a tackle and twists that opponent to the ground. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players must not roll, pull or twist an opponent who is involved in the tackle to the ground.

questions.stem: What do the definitions call rolling, twisting or pulling a player who is on their feet in the tackle area to the ground?
questions.explanation: The definitions describe this prohibited action as a crocodile roll.

questions.stem: On which part of the body do the definitions say a crocodile roll often lands?
questions.explanation: The definition notes that the action often lands on the player's lower limbs.

questions.stem: What is the sanction when an arriving player goes off their feet to play the ball at a tackle?
questions.explanation: Other players must remain on their feet when they play the ball, and the sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: A player on their feet picks up the ball at a tackle. What must the player do?

options.text: Play it immediately by moving away, passing or kicking
Wait for team-mates to bind on
Hold it until an opponent makes contact
Go to ground to set up a ruck

questions.explanation: A player who gains possession at a tackle must play the ball immediately by moving away, passing or kicking.

questions.stem: Which three ways of playing the ball does the law give a player who gains possession at a tackle?

options.text: Passing, kicking or going to ground
Kicking, placing or waiting for support

questions.explanation: The player must play the ball immediately by moving away, or by passing or kicking it.

questions.stem: A player picks up the ball at a tackle and, without being touched, drops to the ground beside the tackle to secure it. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player who gains possession at a tackle must stay on their feet and not go to ground at or near the tackle unless tackled.

questions.stem: When may a player who has gained possession at a tackle go to ground at or near it?

options.text: When a team-mate is in support
When the tackler has moved away

questions.explanation: Such a player must stay on their feet and may go to ground at or near the tackle only if tackled by the opposition.

questions.stem: A player picks up the ball at a tackle. From which direction must a defender come in order to tackle this player?

options.text: From either side of the tackle area
From the direction of the defender's own try line
From at least a metre away from the tackle
From any direction the defender chooses

questions.explanation: A player who gains possession may be tackled, provided the tackler comes from the direction of their own try line.

questions.stem: What is the sanction if a player who gains possession at a tackle fails to play the ball immediately?
questions.explanation: A player who gains possession at a tackle must play the ball immediately, and the sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: When are offside lines created at a tackle?

options.text: When the tackler releases the ball-carrier
When the tackled player releases the ball
When a player on their feet is over the ball on the ground
When the ball-carrier is brought to ground

questions.explanation: Offside lines are created when at least one player is on their feet and over the ball, which is on the ground.

questions.stem: How many players need to be on their feet over the ball to create offside lines at a tackle?

options.text: At least one from each team
At least two from the same team

questions.explanation: One player on their feet over the ball, which is on the ground, is enough to create offside lines.

questions.stem: A tackle has been made and the ball is on the ground, but no player is on their feet over it. Have offside lines been created?

options.text: No, they need a player on their feet over the ball
Yes, every tackle creates offside lines
Yes, they run through the ball

questions.explanation: Offside lines at a tackle exist only when at least one player is on their feet and over the ball.

questions.stem: Through which point does each team's offside line run at a tackle?

options.text: The centre of the ball as it lies on the ground
The hindmost foot of the tackled player only
The front foot of the player standing over the ball
The hindmost point of any player in the tackle or over the ball

questions.explanation: Each team's offside line runs through the hindmost point of any player in the tackle or on their feet over the ball.

questions.stem: In which direction do the offside lines at a tackle run?

options.text: In a circle one metre from the ball
Along the line of the tackled player's body

questions.explanation: Each team's offside line at a tackle runs parallel to the try line.

questions.stem: At a tackle close to the try line, the hindmost point of the defending team's players is behind their own try line. Where is that team's offside line?

options.text: The hindmost point, wherever it is

questions.explanation: If the hindmost point is on or behind the try line, the offside line for that team is the try line.

questions.stem: What does "hindmost" mean in the laws?

options.text: Nearest a team's own try line

questions.explanation: Hindmost means nearest a team's own try line.

questions.stem: Which of these ends a tackle?

options.text: The tackler gets to their feet
The tackled player places the ball

questions.explanation: A tackle ends when a ruck forms, a player on their feet gains the ball and plays it away, the ball leaves the tackle area, or the ball is unplayable.

questions.stem: A player on their feet picks up the ball at a tackle and runs away with it. What has happened to the tackle?

options.text: It lasts until the tackled player stands up

questions.explanation: The tackle ends when a player on their feet from either team gains possession and moves away, passes or kicks.

questions.stem: The ball rolls clear of the tackle area. What has happened to the tackle?

options.text: It lasts until a player picks up the ball

questions.explanation: The tackle ends when the ball leaves the tackle area.

questions.stem: The ball becomes unplayable at a tackle and the referee is in doubt about which player failed to conform to law. What does the referee order?
questions.explanation: If there is doubt about which player did not conform to law, the referee orders a scrum.

questions.stem: The ball is unplayable at a tackle and a scrum is ordered. Which team throws in?

options.text: The team that had the ball before the tackle
The team moving forward before the stoppage
The team that made the tackle

questions.explanation: The throw is taken by the team that was moving forward prior to the stoppage.

questions.stem: The ball is unplayable at a tackle, a scrum is ordered, and neither team was moving forward. Which team throws in?

options.text: The team that was in possession
The team that made the tackle

questions.explanation: If no team was moving forward, the attacking team throws in. That is the team playing in the opposition's half.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a ruck?

options.text: To let players compete for the ball on the ground
To let the defending team reorganise
To restart play after a minor infringement
To let players compete for a ball held off the ground

questions.explanation: The purpose of a ruck is to allow players to compete for the ball, which is on the ground.

questions.stem: In the definitions, which four things are phases of play?
questions.explanation: A phase of play means a scrum, lineout, ruck or maul.

questions.stem: Where can a ruck take place?

options.text: Only in the field of play

questions.explanation: A ruck can take place only in the field of play.

questions.stem: Players from both teams are on their feet, in contact, over a ball lying in in-goal. Is this a ruck?

options.text: No, a ruck can take place only in the field of play
Yes, a ruck can form anywhere in the playing area
Only if it formed before the ball crossed the line
Yes, if the ball was carried in by an attacker

questions.explanation: In-goal is not part of the field of play, so there can be no ruck there.

questions.stem: What is the smallest number of players that can form a ruck?

options.text: Three, with two from one team

questions.explanation: A ruck is formed when at least one player from each team are in contact, on their feet and over the ball on the ground.

questions.stem: Where must the ball be for a ruck to form?

options.text: In the air above the players
Held off the ground between the players

questions.explanation: A ruck forms over the ball, which is on the ground.

questions.stem: After a tackle, two team-mates stand over the ball with no opponent in contact with them. Is this a ruck?

options.text: No, a ruck needs a player from each team in contact
Yes, two players on their feet over the ball form a ruck
Only if the two are bound together
Yes, once the ball is on the ground

questions.explanation: A ruck needs at least one player from each team, in contact, on their feet and over the ball.

questions.stem: One player from each team are on their feet, in contact with each other, over the ball on the ground. What has formed?
questions.explanation: At least one player from each team in contact, on their feet and over the ball on the ground forms a ruck.

questions.stem: Which of these must be true of the players who form a ruck?

options.text: They have one knee on the ground
They number at least two from each team
They are bound with both arms

questions.explanation: A ruck is formed by players who are in contact, on their feet and over the ball.

questions.stem: How must players position their heads and shoulders at a ruck?
questions.explanation: Players involved in all stages of the ruck must have their heads and shoulders no lower than their hips.

questions.stem: A player joins a ruck with head and shoulders lower than the hips. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Having the head and shoulders lower than the hips at a ruck is a free-kick offence.

questions.stem: At which stages of a ruck must players keep their heads and shoulders no lower than their hips?

options.text: Only once the ball is won

questions.explanation: The requirement applies to players involved in all stages of the ruck.

questions.stem: Through which point does each team's offside line run at a ruck?

options.text: The hindmost point of any ruck participant
The front foot of the hindmost player
The middle line of the ruck
The position of the ball in the ruck

questions.explanation: Each team's offside line runs through the hindmost point of any ruck participant.

questions.stem: In which direction do the offside lines at a ruck run?

options.text: In a circle around the ruck

questions.explanation: Each team's offside line at a ruck runs parallel to the try line.

questions.stem: How many offside lines are there at a ruck?

options.text: Four, one on each side of the ruck
One, through the middle of the ruck

questions.explanation: Each team has its own offside line through the hindmost point of any ruck participant.

questions.stem: A ruck forms close to a team's try line and the hindmost point of the ruck participants is behind that line. Where is that team's offside line?

options.text: The hindmost point of the ruck

questions.explanation: If the hindmost point is on or behind the try line, the offside line for that team is the try line.

questions.stem: A ruck participant's trailing foot is the part of the ruck nearest that player's own try line. Where is that team's offside line?
questions.explanation: The offside line runs through the hindmost point of any ruck participant, and hindmost means nearest a team's own try line.

questions.stem: From where must an arriving player join a ruck?

options.text: From any position, if on their feet
From in front of the ball

questions.explanation: An arriving player must be on their feet and join from behind their offside line.

questions.stem: An arriving player dives into a ruck off their feet. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: An arriving player must be on their feet when joining a ruck.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for joining a ruck from an offside position?
questions.explanation: Joining a ruck from in front of the offside line is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: Where may a player join a ruck in relation to the hindmost player?

options.text: In front, if bound to a team-mate
Alongside but not in front of that player

questions.explanation: A player may join alongside but not in front of the hindmost player.

questions.stem: A player joins a ruck from the side, in front of the hindmost team-mate. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player may join alongside the hindmost player but not in front of that player.

questions.stem: Onto whom may a player joining a ruck bind?

options.text: A team-mate or an opposition player

questions.explanation: A player joining a ruck must bind onto a team-mate or an opposition player.

questions.stem: When must a joining player's bind happen, compared with contact by any other part of the body?

options.text: At any time before the ruck ends
Before it or at the same time

questions.explanation: The bind must precede or be simultaneous with contact with any other part of the body.

questions.stem: A player charges into a ruck shoulder first and makes no attempt to bind. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player joining a ruck must bind, and the bind must come before or at the same time as any other contact.

questions.stem: A ruck has formed. What two choices does a nearby player who is not in it have?

options.text: Join the ruck or stand still beside it
Wait beside the ruck or follow the ball
Retire five metres or stand beside the ruck
Join the ruck or retire behind the offside line at once

questions.explanation: Players must join the ruck or retire behind their offside line immediately.

questions.stem: A defender stands beside a ruck, in front of the offside line, without joining it. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players must join the ruck or retire behind their offside line immediately.

questions.stem: A player leaves a ruck. May that player rejoin it?

options.text: No, a player may join a ruck only once
Only after the ball has emerged

questions.explanation: Players who have been part of the ruck may rejoin it, provided they do so from an onside position.

questions.stem: Under the definitions, which part of another player's body must be grasped for a legal bind?

options.text: Between the hips and the knees
Between the shoulders and the hips

questions.explanation: Binding means grasping another player's body firmly between the shoulders and the hips.

questions.stem: Under the definitions, how much of the arm must be in contact for a legal bind?

options.text: The whole arm, from hand to shoulder
From the elbow to the shoulder

questions.explanation: Binding needs the whole arm in contact, from hand to shoulder.

questions.stem: By which two methods may possession be won at a ruck?

options.text: Rucking, or picking the ball up
Handling, or kicking the ball out
Pushing, or falling on the ball
Rucking, or pushing the opposition off the ball

questions.explanation: Possession may be won either by rucking or by pushing the opposing team off the ball.

questions.stem: What does "rucking" mean in the definitions?

options.text: Using the shoulder to clear opponents out of a ruck
Using the feet legally to win or keep the ball in a ruck
Using the hands to move the ball back through a ruck
Pushing opponents backwards to win the ball in a ruck

questions.explanation: Rucking is legally using one's feet to try to win or keep possession of the ball in a ruck.

questions.stem: Once a ruck has formed, which player may go on handling the ball?

options.text: Any player who is bound to the ruck with one full arm
The tackled player, until a team-mate takes the ball
One who had hands on it before the ruck formed and stays on their feet
The first player from each team to arrive at the ruck

questions.explanation: No player may handle the ball in a ruck unless they got their hands on it before the ruck formed and stay on their feet.

questions.stem: A jackler on their feet has both hands on the ball before an opponent makes contact and a ruck forms. May the jackler keep contesting with the hands?

options.text: Only if a team-mate binds on
Yes, as long as the jackler stays on their feet
No, all hands must come off once a ruck forms
Yes, but only for two more seconds

questions.explanation: A player who got hands on the ball before the ruck formed may continue, provided they stay on their feet.

questions.stem: A ruck has formed. A player bound in it, who had no hands on the ball beforehand, reaches down and picks the ball up from the middle of the ruck. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Once a ruck has formed, a player who did not already have hands on the ball may not handle it.

questions.stem: What must players try to do throughout a ruck?

options.text: Keep a hand on the ball
Get the ball out within three seconds

questions.explanation: Players must endeavour to remain on their feet throughout the ruck.

questions.stem: A player stands alongside a ruck with one hand resting on a team-mate's back, neither caught in nor bound to it. Is the player part of the ruck?

options.text: Yes, if behind the hindmost foot
Yes, any contact with the ruck is enough
Only if the ball is on that side
No, players must be caught in or bound to the ruck

questions.explanation: All players in a ruck must be caught in or bound to it, and not just alongside it.

questions.stem: May players in a ruck play the ball with their feet?

options.text: Yes, in any manner they choose
No, the ball may only be pushed over
Yes, provided they do so safely

questions.explanation: Players may play the ball with their feet, provided they do so in a safe manner.

questions.stem: What must players on the ground in a ruck do?

options.text: Attempt to move away from the ball
Push the ball back with a hand
Hold their position until the ruck ends

questions.explanation: Players on the ground must attempt to move away from the ball.

questions.stem: A player lying in a ruck uses a hand to slow the ball as it emerges. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players on the ground must not play the ball in the ruck or as it emerges.

questions.stem: A player in a ruck traps the ball between the lower legs and lifts it up. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players must not pick the ball up with their legs in a ruck.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for intentionally collapsing a ruck?
questions.explanation: Intentionally collapsing a ruck is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: An arriving player jumps on top of a ruck. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players must not intentionally collapse a ruck or jump on top of it.

questions.stem: A player in a ruck intentionally steps on an opponent who is lying on the ground. What is the sanction under the ruck law?
questions.explanation: Players must not intentionally step on another player in a ruck.

questions.stem: As the ball emerges from a ruck, a defender dives over it while it is on the ground within a metre of the ruck. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players must not fall onto or over the emerging ball while it is on the ground near the ruck.

questions.stem: A defender bound in a ruck kicks the ball out through the opposition's side of the ruck. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players must not kick, or attempt to kick, the ball out of a ruck.

questions.stem: A player in a ruck swings a foot to kick the ball out of it but misses the ball. Has an offence been committed?

options.text: Yes, the attempt is itself an offence
Only if an opponent was struck
No, the ball was not touched
Only if the ball then emerges

questions.explanation: Players must not kick, or attempt to kick, the ball out of a ruck.

questions.stem: The ball comes out of a ruck and a player pushes it back in. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Returning the ball into a ruck is a free-kick offence.

questions.stem: A player at a ruck makes a dummy movement so that opponents believe the ball is out when it is still in the ruck. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Players must not take any action to make opponents believe that the ruck has ended when it has not. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: Which of these ruck offences is sanctioned with a free-kick?

options.text: Picking the ball up with the legs
Kicking the ball out of the ruck
Returning the ball into the ruck

questions.explanation: Returning the ball into the ruck and pretending the ruck has ended are free-kick offences. The others listed are penalties.

questions.stem: Which of these ruck offences is sanctioned with a penalty?

options.text: Joining with the head lower than the hips
Kicking the ball out of the ruck
Returning the ball into the ruck
Pretending that the ruck has ended

questions.explanation: Kicking the ball out of a ruck is a penalty offence. The other three are free-kick offences.

questions.stem: What does the referee call when the ball has been clearly won at a ruck and is available to be played?
questions.explanation: When the ball has been clearly won and is available, the referee calls "use it".

questions.stem: After the referee calls "use it" at a ruck, within how long must the ball be played away?
questions.explanation: After the call of "use it" the ball must be played away from the ruck within five seconds.

questions.stem: The referee calls "use it" at a ruck and the ball is still there more than five seconds later. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: If the ball is not played away within five seconds of the call, a scrum is awarded.

questions.stem: A scrum-half is trying to play the ball away from a ruck. A defender who is part of the ruck reaches out and grabs the scrum-half. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player who is, or was, part of the ruck may not play an opponent who is near it and trying to play the ball away.

questions.stem: A player who was part of a ruck may not play an opponent who is near the ruck and trying to play the ball away. How close is "near"?
questions.explanation: The law gives the distance as within one metre.

questions.stem: The ball leaves a ruck. What happens?

options.text: The ruck goes on until the referee calls "use it"
The ruck ends and play continues
The ruck turns into a maul

questions.explanation: The ruck ends and play continues when the ball leaves the ruck.

questions.stem: A ruck near the try line moves so that the ball in the ruck is on the try line. What happens to the ruck?

options.text: It carries on as a ruck in in-goal

questions.explanation: The ruck ends and play continues when the ball in the ruck is on or over the try line.

questions.stem: The ball in a ruck is on the try line and an attacker bound in the ruck reaches down and grounds it. Had the ruck already ended?

options.text: No, it ends only on the referee's call
Only if a defender had touched the ball
No, it ends only when the ball leaves the ruck
Yes, it ends when the ball in it is on or over the try line

questions.explanation: A ruck ends when the ball in it is on or over the try line, so the ball may then be grounded.

questions.stem: The referee decides that the ball will probably not emerge from a ruck within a reasonable time. What is awarded?
questions.explanation: If the ball will probably not emerge within a reasonable time, a scrum is awarded.

questions.stem: The ball becomes unplayable in a ruck and no offence has been seen. How does play restart?
questions.explanation: The ruck ends when the ball becomes unplayable, and a scrum is awarded.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a maul?

options.text: To let players compete for a ball held off the ground
To restart play after a stoppage
To let players compete for the ball on the ground
To let the team in possession rest

questions.explanation: The purpose of a maul is to allow players to compete for the ball, which is held off the ground.

questions.stem: Where can a maul take place?

options.text: Only in the field of play

questions.explanation: A maul can take place only in the field of play.

questions.stem: What is the smallest number of players that can form a maul?
questions.explanation: A maul needs a ball-carrier and at least one player from each team, so at least three players.

questions.stem: Who must be present for a maul to form?

options.text: A ball-carrier and any two opponents
A ball-carrier and at least one player from each team

questions.explanation: A maul consists of a ball-carrier and at least one player from each team, bound together and on their feet.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier is held on their feet by an opponent, and a team-mate of the ball-carrier binds on. What has formed?
questions.explanation: A ball-carrier and at least one player from each team, bound together and on their feet, form a maul.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier is held on their feet by two opponents, with no team-mate bound on. Is this a maul?

options.text: Yes, once the ball-carrier is held up
Only if it moves towards a try line
No, a maul also needs a team-mate of the ball-carrier
Yes, three players are bound together

questions.explanation: A maul needs the ball-carrier and at least one player from each team, so a team-mate must also be bound in.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier and a team-mate bind together and drive forward with no opponent bound to them. Is this a maul?

options.text: No, a maul needs at least one player from each team
Yes, if they are moving towards a try line
Yes, two bound players with the ball form a maul
Only if it follows a lineout

questions.explanation: A maul needs at least one player from each team as well as the ball-carrier.

questions.stem: In what position must the players in a maul be?

options.text: In contact, with the ball on the ground
Bound together and on their feet
Side by side, with no binding needed
Bound together with one knee down

questions.explanation: The players in a maul are bound together and on their feet.

questions.stem: Where is the ball in a maul?

options.text: On the ground between the players
Held by a ball-carrier, off the ground

questions.explanation: A maul is formed around a ball-carrier, so the ball is held off the ground.

questions.stem: A player rips the ball from the ball-carrier in a maul. What must that player do until the ball has been transferred?

options.text: Let go of the ball-carrier at once
Stay in contact with the ball-carrier
Move to the back of the maul

questions.explanation: A player ripping the ball from the ball-carrier must stay in contact with that player until the ball has been transferred.

questions.stem: A player ripping the ball from the ball-carrier in a maul breaks contact with that player before the ball has been transferred. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: The ripping player must stay in contact with the ball-carrier until the ball has been transferred. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: Once a maul has formed, in which direction must it move?
questions.explanation: Once formed, a maul must move towards a try line.

questions.stem: Through which point does each team's offside line run at a maul?

options.text: The front foot of the ball-carrier
The position of the ball in the maul
The middle line of the maul
The maul's hindmost foot nearest that team's try line

questions.explanation: Each team's offside line runs through the maul participants' hindmost foot that is nearest to that team's try line.

questions.stem: In which direction do the offside lines at a maul run?

options.text: In a circle around the maul

questions.explanation: Each team's offside line at a maul runs parallel to the try line.

questions.stem: A maul is driven up to a try line, and the defending team's hindmost foot in the maul is behind that line. Where is the defending team's offside line?
questions.explanation: If the hindmost foot is on or behind the try line, the offside line for that team is the try line.

questions.stem: A maul has formed. What must a nearby player who is not in it do?

options.text: Join from wherever they happen to be standing
Stand still until the maul has ended
Join from an onside position or retire behind the offside line
Retire ten metres from the maul

questions.explanation: A player must either join a maul from an onside position or retire behind their offside line immediately.

questions.stem: A defender stands beside a maul, ahead of the offside line, waiting for the ball to come out. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player must join a maul from an onside position or retire behind the offside line immediately.

questions.stem: A player leaves a maul. What must that player do at once?

options.text: Move at least five metres away

questions.explanation: Players who leave a maul must immediately retire behind the offside line.

questions.stem: A player has left a maul and retired behind the offside line. May the player rejoin the maul?

options.text: No, a player may join a maul only once
Only if the maul is in the player's own half
Yes, players who leave a maul may re-join it
Only once the maul has stopped moving

questions.explanation: Players who leave a maul must retire behind the offside line, and they may then re-join the maul.

questions.stem: From what position must a player join a maul?
questions.explanation: Players joining a maul must do so from an onside position.

questions.stem: Onto which player must a player joining a maul bind?

options.text: The hindmost player in the maul

questions.explanation: Players joining a maul must bind on to the hindmost player in the maul.

questions.stem: A player joins a maul from the side, binding on a team-mate in the middle of it. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players joining a maul must do so from an onside position and bind on to the hindmost player.

questions.stem: A player joins a maul with head and shoulders lower than the hips. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Players joining a maul must have their heads and shoulders no lower than their hips. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: Which of these offences when joining a maul is sanctioned with a free-kick?

options.text: Binding on a player other than the hindmost
Head and shoulders lower than the hips
Joining in front of the ball-carrier

questions.explanation: Joining with the head and shoulders lower than the hips is a free-kick offence. The others are penalties.

questions.stem: May the ball-carrier in a maul go to ground?

options.text: Yes, at any time and without condition
Only within five metres of a try line
Yes, if the ball is made available immediately
No, every player must stay on their feet

questions.explanation: The ball-carrier in a maul may go to ground provided that player makes the ball available immediately.

questions.stem: The ball-carrier in a maul goes to ground and the ball is not made available immediately. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: If the ball-carrier goes to ground and the ball is not immediately available, a scrum is awarded.

questions.stem: What must players in a maul, other than the ball-carrier, try to do?

options.text: Keep a hand on the ball
Move to the back of the maul
Go to ground when the maul stops

questions.explanation: All other players in a maul must endeavour to stay on their feet.

questions.stem: A player stands alongside a maul with one hand on a team-mate, neither caught in nor bound to it. Is the player legally part of the maul?

options.text: No, players must be caught in or bound to the maul
Yes, any contact with the maul is enough
Yes, if the player came from an onside position
Yes, if the player is behind the ball-carrier

questions.explanation: All players in a maul must be caught in or bound to it, and not just alongside it.

questions.stem: The ball-carrier in a maul slides backwards through it to the rear while team-mates stay bound in front. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player in possession of the ball must not slide or move backwards in the maul.

questions.stem: What is the sanction when the player with the ball slides backwards in a maul?
questions.explanation: A player in possession must not slide or move backwards in the maul. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for intentionally collapsing a maul?
questions.explanation: Intentionally collapsing a maul is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: A player jumps on top of a maul. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players must not intentionally collapse a maul or jump on top of it.

questions.stem: A defender tries to drag an opponent out of a maul. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Players must not attempt to drag an opponent out of a maul.

questions.stem: A player acts to make opponents believe that a maul has ended when it has not. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Making opponents believe that the maul has ended when it has not is a free-kick offence.

questions.stem: Which of these maul offences is sanctioned with a free-kick?

options.text: Making opponents believe the maul has ended
Dragging an opponent out of the maul
Jumping on top of the maul

questions.explanation: Pretending that the maul has ended is a free-kick offence. The other three are penalties.

questions.stem: Every defender intentionally leaves a maul, so that only players of the team in possession remain bound. What is the status of the maul?
questions.explanation: When the team not in possession intentionally leaves the maul so that none of its players are left, the maul continues.

questions.stem: All the defenders have intentionally left a maul and now want to rejoin. On whom must the first of them bind?

options.text: The frontmost player of the team in possession
The hindmost player of the team in possession

questions.explanation: They may re-join provided that the first player binds on the frontmost player of the team in possession.

questions.stem: All the defenders intentionally leave a maul. The first of them to rejoin binds on the side, directly onto the ball-carrier at the back. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: The first player to re-join must bind on the frontmost player of the team in possession.

questions.stem: A maul stops moving towards a try line for more than five seconds, but the ball is being moved and the referee can see it. What does the referee do?

options.text: Lets the maul go on with no call
Instructs the players to use the ball

questions.explanation: When a maul has stopped for more than five seconds but the ball is being moved and can be seen, the referee instructs the players to use the ball.

questions.stem: A maul stops moving towards a try line. Within how long must it start moving again to carry on as before?
questions.explanation: A stopped maul may restart moving towards a try line providing it does so within five seconds.

questions.stem: A maul stops, restarts within five seconds, then stops a second time with the ball being moved and visible. What does the referee do?

options.text: Allows another five seconds to restart
Instructs the team to use the ball

questions.explanation: If the maul stops a second time but the ball is being moved and the referee can see it, the referee instructs the team to use the ball.

questions.stem: How many times may a stopped maul restart before the referee, at the next stop, tells the team to use the ball?
questions.explanation: A maul may restart once within five seconds. If it stops a second time, the referee instructs the team to use the ball.

questions.stem: The ball-carrier breaks away from a maul with the ball. What happens?

options.text: The maul ends and play continues
The maul goes on until the whistle
The maul turns into a ruck

questions.explanation: A maul ends and play continues when the ball or the ball-carrier leaves the maul.

questions.stem: The ball is dropped to the ground inside a maul. What happens to the maul?

options.text: It carries on as a maul

questions.explanation: A maul ends and play continues when the ball is on the ground.

questions.stem: A maul is driven forward until the ball is over the try line. What happens to the maul?
questions.explanation: A maul ends and play continues when the ball is on or over the try line.

questions.stem: Which of these ends a maul with play continuing?

options.text: The maul collapses without foul play
The maul stays still and the ball does not emerge

questions.explanation: A maul ends and play continues when the ball or ball-carrier leaves it, the ball is on the ground, or the ball is on or over the try line.

questions.stem: What is the sanction when a maul ends unsuccessfully?
questions.explanation: When a maul ends unsuccessfully, a scrum is awarded.

questions.stem: Which of these ends a maul unsuccessfully?

options.text: The ball is over the try line
The ball is on the ground

questions.explanation: A maul ends unsuccessfully when, for example, the ball becomes unplayable. The other three end the maul with play continuing.

questions.stem: A maul collapses with no foul play involved. What does the referee award?
questions.explanation: A maul that collapses, not as a result of foul play, has ended unsuccessfully and a scrum is awarded.

questions.stem: A maul stays still for longer than five seconds and the ball does not emerge. What does the referee award?
questions.explanation: A maul that does not move towards a try line for longer than five seconds, with the ball not emerging, ends unsuccessfully.

questions.stem: At a maul the ball is available and the referee calls "use it". Within how long must it be played?
questions.explanation: If the ball has not been played within five seconds of the call, the maul ends unsuccessfully and a scrum is awarded.

questions.stem: A scrum-half is trying to play the ball away from the back of a maul. A defender who was in the maul reaches round and grabs the scrum-half. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A player who is, or was, part of the maul may not play an opponent who is near it and trying to play the ball away.

questions.stem: A player who was part of a maul may not play an opponent who is near the maul and trying to play the ball away. How close is "near"?
questions.explanation: The law gives the distance as within one metre.

questions.stem: A player catches an opponent's kick directly in open play and a maul forms immediately. The maul ends unsuccessfully. Which team throws in at the scrum?

options.text: The team of the player who caught the kick
The team that kicked the ball
The team that was moving forward

questions.explanation: If a maul forms immediately after a direct catch of an opponent's kick in open play, the scrum goes to the catcher's team.

questions.stem: For the catcher's team to get the scrum when a maul that follows a caught kick ends unsuccessfully, how must the kick have been caught?

options.text: Directly, inside the catcher's own 22 only
After one bounce, in open play
After a touch by a team-mate

questions.explanation: The rule applies when a maul is formed immediately after a player has directly caught an opponent's kick in open play.

questions.stem: What does claiming a mark achieve?

options.text: It stops play and wins a penalty
It lets the catcher run on without being tackled
It stops play and wins a scrum
It stops play and wins a free-kick

questions.explanation: A mark is a way of suspending play and winning a free-kick by directly catching an opponent's kick.

questions.stem: In which areas may a player claim a mark?

options.text: In their own 22 or their own in-goal
Anywhere in the field of play

questions.explanation: A mark is claimed by directly catching an opponent's kick in the catcher's own 22 or in in-goal.

questions.stem: A player catches an opponent's kick cleanly on the halfway line and calls "mark". What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, as no mark has been made

questions.explanation: A mark can be claimed only in the catcher's own 22 or in-goal.

questions.stem: What does "directly caught" mean in the definitions?

options.text: Caught with both hands at the first attempt
Caught without first touching anyone else or the ground
Caught before the catcher's feet leave the ground
Caught without the catcher having to move

questions.explanation: Directly caught means the ball is caught without first touching anyone else or the ground.

questions.stem: Is the 22-metre line itself part of the 22?

options.text: Only when the ball is on the ground
No, the 22 starts just behind the line

questions.explanation: The definitions say the 22 includes the 22-metre line but not the try line or the touchlines.

questions.stem: Where must the catcher's feet be to claim a mark?

options.text: At least one foot behind the halfway line
Both feet behind their own 22-metre line
Both feet inside their own in-goal
At least one foot on or behind their own 22-metre line

questions.explanation: The catcher must have at least one foot on or behind their own 22-metre line.

questions.stem: A player catches an opponent's kick with one foot on their own 22-metre line and the other foot beyond it, and calls "mark". Is the mark good?

options.text: No, the line is outside the 22
Yes, one foot on the line is enough
Only if the other foot then steps back
No, both feet must be behind the line

questions.explanation: At least one foot on or behind the catcher's own 22-metre line is enough.

questions.stem: A player standing with both feet outside their own 22 catches an opponent's kick and calls "mark". Is the mark good?

options.text: No, at least one foot must be on or behind the 22-metre line
Yes, if the call was made in time
Only if the player then retreats into the 22
Yes, if the ball had crossed the 22-metre line

questions.explanation: The catcher must have at least one foot on or behind their own 22-metre line when catching the ball.

questions.stem: For a mark caught in the air, when is the position of the catcher's feet judged?
questions.explanation: The catcher must have at least one foot on or behind the 22-metre line when catching the ball, or when landing having caught it in the air.

questions.stem: A player jumps and catches an opponent's kick that has reached the plane of the 22-metre line, lands with one foot on that line and calls "mark". Is the mark good?

options.text: No, both feet must land behind the line
Only if the player took off inside the 22
No, a mark cannot be claimed in the air
Yes, the foot position on landing is what counts

questions.explanation: For a catch in the air, the catcher needs at least one foot on or behind the 22-metre line when landing.

questions.stem: A player catches an opponent's kick cleanly inside the opposition's 22 and calls "mark". What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, as no mark can be made there

questions.explanation: The catcher must be on or behind their own 22-metre line, so no mark is possible in the opposition's 22.

questions.stem: From whose kick must the ball come for a mark to be claimed?
questions.explanation: The ball must be caught directly from an opponent's kick.

questions.stem: An opponent's kick bounces once in the 22 before a defender catches it and calls "mark". Is the mark awarded?

options.text: Only if the bounce was in in-goal
No, the ball touched the ground before the catch
Yes, the catch was made inside the 22

questions.explanation: The ball must be caught before it touches the ground or another player.

questions.stem: An opponent's kick brushes a team-mate of the catcher before being caught in the 22 with a call of "mark". Is the mark awarded?

options.text: No, the ball touched another player before the catch
Only if the team-mate was inside the 22
Yes, the ball did not touch the ground
Yes, a touch by a team-mate is ignored

questions.explanation: The ball must be caught directly from the kick, before it touches the ground or another player.

questions.stem: An opponent's kick is touched in flight by a chasing opponent and is then caught in the 22 with a call of "mark". Is the mark awarded?

options.text: Yes, the ball did not touch the ground
Yes, the touch was by an opponent
Only if the touch was accidental
No, the ball touched another player before the catch

questions.explanation: The ball must be caught directly from the kick, before it touches the ground or any other player.

questions.stem: A team-mate's kick goes straight up and a player in their own 22 catches it and calls "mark". Is the mark awarded?

options.text: Yes, any kick may be marked in the 22
Only if the catcher is in in-goal
No, the ball must come from an opponent's kick
Yes, if the ball did not touch the ground

questions.explanation: A mark can be claimed only from an opponent's kick.

questions.stem: An opponent throws a long pass that a defender intercepts in the defender's own 22, calling "mark". Is the mark awarded?

options.text: Yes, if the ball did not touch the ground
No, a mark can be claimed only from a kick
Only if the pass was thrown forward
Yes, the ball came directly from an opponent

questions.explanation: A mark is claimed by catching a ball directly from an opponent's kick, not from a pass.

questions.stem: A player with a foot on their own 22-metre line reaches forward and catches an opponent's kick before the ball has reached the plane of that line. Can a mark be claimed?

options.text: Yes, the catcher's foot is on the line
Yes, if the catcher calls "mark" in time
Only if the catcher then steps back into the 22
No, the ball must have reached the plane of the 22-metre line

questions.explanation: The ball must have reached the plane of the 22-metre line directly from the opponent's kick.

questions.stem: What must a player call to claim a mark?
questions.explanation: To claim a mark the catcher must call "mark".

questions.stem: When must the call of "mark" be made?

options.text: Within three seconds of the catch
Once the catcher has landed and steadied
At the same time as the catch

questions.explanation: The catcher must call "mark" simultaneously with the catch.

questions.stem: A player in their own 22 cleanly catches an opponent's kick, runs three strides and then calls "mark". Is the mark awarded?

options.text: Yes, the call may come at any time before a tackle
No, the call must be made at the same time as the catch
Only if the player is still inside the 22
Yes, if no opponent has touched the player

questions.explanation: The call of "mark" must be simultaneous with the catch.

questions.stem: An opponent's kick hits a goal post and is then caught cleanly by a defender in the 22, who calls "mark". Is the mark awarded?

options.text: No, the ball was not caught directly
Only if the catcher is in in-goal
Yes, a mark may be claimed after the ball hits a post
No, the ball is dead once it hits a post

questions.explanation: A player may claim a mark even if the ball hits a goal post or crossbar before being caught.

questions.stem: An opponent's drop-kick at goal rebounds off the crossbar and is caught by a defender in in-goal, who calls "mark". Is the mark awarded?

options.text: No, a mark cannot be claimed from a kick at goal
No, the ball touched the crossbar first
Only if the catcher's feet are on the try line
Yes, a mark may be claimed after the ball hits the crossbar

questions.explanation: A player may claim a mark even if the ball hits a goal post or crossbar before being caught.

questions.stem: Which of these does the law allow the ball to touch before a mark is claimed?

options.text: A goal post or the crossbar

questions.explanation: A mark may still be claimed if the ball hits a goal post or crossbar, but not if it touches the ground or another player.

questions.stem: What does the referee award when a mark is called correctly?
questions.explanation: When a mark is called correctly, the referee awards a free-kick.

questions.stem: A mark is called correctly. What is awarded, and to whom?

options.text: A free-kick to the catcher's team
A scrum to the catcher's team
A penalty to the catcher's team
A free-kick to the kicking team

questions.explanation: The referee awards a free-kick to the team in possession, which is the catcher's team.

questions.stem: When a mark is called correctly, what does the referee do about play?

options.text: Waits for the catcher to stop moving
Stops the game once the catcher is tackled
Lets play run to see if advantage develops

questions.explanation: When a mark is called correctly, the referee immediately stops the game.

questions.stem: A defender correctly claims a mark, but team-mates are well placed to counter-attack. May the referee let play run on?

options.text: Yes, if the catcher asks to play on
No, the referee stops the game immediately
Only if no opponent is nearby
Yes, the referee may play advantage

questions.explanation: When a mark is called correctly, the referee immediately stops the game and awards a free-kick.

questions.stem: Which kicks does the law exclude from being marked?

options.text: A punt and a kick along the ground
A drop-out and a kick in open play
A kick-off and a restart kick after a score
A penalty kick and a free-kick

questions.explanation: A mark may not be claimed from a kick-off or a restart kick after a score.

questions.stem: A player catches the kick-off cleanly inside their own 22 and calls "mark". What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, a kick-off may not be marked

questions.explanation: A mark may not be claimed from a kick-off.

questions.stem: After a try, the restart kick is caught cleanly in the receiving team's 22 with a call of "mark". What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, as this kick may not be marked

questions.explanation: A mark may not be claimed from a restart kick after a score.

questions.stem: An opponent punts the ball in open play and a defender catches it cleanly inside the defender's own 22, calling "mark". Is the mark awarded?

options.text: Only if no opponent is within ten metres
No, a mark can be claimed only in in-goal
No, a mark needs a drop-kick
Yes, every condition for a mark is met

questions.explanation: A direct catch of an opponent's kick in the catcher's own 22, with a simultaneous call, is a mark.

questions.stem: An opponent's 22-metre drop-out travels a long way and is caught cleanly inside the catcher's own 22 with a call of "mark". Can the mark be awarded?

options.text: Only if the catcher is in in-goal
Yes, only kick-offs and restart kicks after a score are excluded
No, a mark can be claimed only from a punt
No, a mark cannot be claimed from any drop-kick

questions.explanation: The law excludes only a kick-off and a restart kick after a score, so a drop-out may be marked.

questions.stem: An opponent's penalty kick at goal falls short and a defender catches it cleanly in in-goal, calling "mark". Is the mark awarded?

options.text: Only if the ball first hit a post
No, a mark cannot be claimed from a penalty kick
No, a mark cannot be claimed in in-goal
Yes, only kick-offs and restart kicks after a score are excluded

questions.explanation: A mark may be claimed in in-goal, and the law excludes only a kick-off and a restart kick after a score.

questions.stem: Who takes the free-kick awarded for a mark?

options.text: The player who claimed the mark

questions.explanation: The player who claimed the mark takes the free-kick.

questions.stem: A full-back claims a mark, and the fly-half steps up to take the free-kick straight away. Is this allowed?

options.text: Yes, any player may take a free-kick
Only if the kick is taken quickly
No, the player who claimed the mark takes the kick

questions.explanation: The player who claimed the mark takes the free-kick, unless that player is unable to do so within one minute.

questions.stem: A team-mate may take the free-kick if the player who claimed the mark is unable to take it within what time?
questions.explanation: If the player is unable to take the free-kick within one minute, a team-mate may take it.

questions.stem: A player claims a mark but is hurt in the catch and cannot take the free-kick within one minute. What happens?

options.text: A team-mate may take the free-kick
A scrum is awarded to the same team
The opposition is awarded the free-kick

questions.explanation: If the player who claimed the mark cannot take the free-kick within one minute, a team-mate may take it.

questions.stem: A mark is made inside the 22, well away from the try line. Where is the free-kick taken?

options.text: At the place of the mark

questions.explanation: For a mark within the 22, the free-kick is at the place of the mark, as long as that is at least five metres from the try line.

questions.stem: A mark is made inside the 22, two metres from the try line. Where is the free-kick taken?

options.text: Five metres from the try line, in line with the mark
On the try line, in line with the mark
Two metres from the try line, where the mark was made
On the 22-metre line, in line with the mark

questions.explanation: The free-kick is at the place of the mark but at least five metres from the try line, in line with the place of the mark.

questions.stem: A mark is made in in-goal. Where is the free-kick taken?

options.text: In in-goal, where the mark was made
On the try line, in line with the mark
On the 5-metre line, in line with the mark
On the 22-metre line, in line with the mark

questions.explanation: For a mark in in-goal, the free-kick is on the five-metre line in line with the place of the mark.

questions.stem: What is the closest to the try line that a free-kick for a mark may be taken?
questions.explanation: The free-kick for a mark is taken at least five metres from the try line.

questions.stem: A mark is made in the 22, four metres from the try line and ten metres in from touch. Where is the free-kick taken?

options.text: On the 22-metre line, ten metres in from touch
Five metres from the try line, ten metres in from touch
Four metres from the try line, ten metres in from touch
Five metres from the try line, fifteen metres in from touch

questions.explanation: The kick moves out to five metres from the try line but stays in line with the place of the mark.

questions.stem: When a mark is made in in-goal, the free-kick is taken on the 5-metre line. In line with what?

options.text: The place where the ball was kicked
The middle of the goal posts

questions.explanation: For a mark in in-goal, the free-kick is on the five-metre line in line with the place of the mark.

questions.stem: What happens to the ball when it goes into touch?

options.text: It stays live until the whistle
It stays live if it bounces back in
It stays live for the non-kicking team

questions.explanation: When play reaches a touchline, the ball is in touch and becomes dead.

questions.stem: What do the definitions call the area alongside the field of play that includes the touchlines and beyond?
questions.explanation: Touch is the area alongside the field of play that includes the touchlines and beyond.

questions.stem: What is the plane of touch?

options.text: The vertical space rising directly above the touchline
The strip of ground just inside the touchline
The area of ground beyond the touchline
The line along which a lineout throw is made

questions.explanation: The plane of touch is the vertical space rising immediately above the touchline or touch-in-goal line.

questions.stem: A kick lands in the field of play and then bounces into touch. Was it kicked directly into touch?

options.text: Yes, if it bounced only once
No, it landed on the playing area first
Only if it was kicked from inside the 22

questions.explanation: A ball is kicked directly into touch when it goes into touch without first landing on the playing area or touching a player or the referee.

questions.stem: A kick glances off the referee and goes into touch without bouncing. Was it kicked directly into touch?

options.text: Only if the referee was inside the 22
No, it touched the referee on the way
Yes, as it did not land on the playing area
Yes, a touch by the referee is ignored

questions.explanation: Kicked directly into touch means without first landing on the playing area or touching a player or the referee.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier's foot touches the touchline. Is the ball in touch?

options.text: No, unless the ball also crosses the line
Yes, the touchline itself is in touch
Only if the next step lands beyond the line
No, the foot must be wholly beyond the line

questions.explanation: The ball is in touch when the ball or ball-carrier touches the touchline or anything beyond it.

questions.stem: A ball rolling along the ground comes to rest touching the touchline. Is it in touch?

options.text: No, more than half the ball must be over the line
Only if a player then touches it
Yes, the ball is touching the touchline
No, the whole ball must cross the line

questions.explanation: The ball is in touch when it touches the touchline or anything beyond.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier with both feet in the field of play holds the ball out over the touchline without it touching anything. Is the ball in touch?

options.text: Only if an opponent is holding the ball-carrier
Yes, unless it is pulled back within a second
Yes, the ball has crossed the plane of touch
No, neither ball nor ball-carrier has touched the line or beyond

questions.explanation: The ball is in touch when the ball or ball-carrier touches the touchline or anything beyond it, not when the ball is merely held over the line.

questions.stem: A player standing in touch catches an opponent's kick after the ball has reached the plane of touch. What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, the ball is not in touch

questions.explanation: If the ball has reached the plane of touch when it is caught, the catcher is not deemed to have taken it into touch, so the catcher's team throws in.

questions.stem: A player standing in touch reaches infield and catches an opponent's kick before the ball has reached the plane of touch. What is the decision?

options.text: Play on, the ball is not in touch

questions.explanation: If the ball has not reached the plane of touch when it is caught, the catcher is deemed to have taken it into touch, so the opposition throws in.

questions.stem: A player standing in touch picks up a stationary ball that is lying in the field of play near the touchline. Has the ball been taken into touch?

options.text: No, unless the player then steps further out
No, a stationary ball cannot be taken into touch
Only if the ball was last played by an opponent
Yes, by the player who picked it up

questions.explanation: A player in touch who picks up a ball that has not reached the plane of touch has taken it into touch, whether the ball was moving or stationary.

questions.stem: The ball crosses the plane of touch in the air, and a player standing in the playing area catches it. Is the ball in touch?

options.text: No, it was caught by a player in the playing area
Yes, unless the player was in the 22
Yes, the ball crossed the plane of touch
Only if the ball was kicked by an opponent

questions.explanation: The ball is not in touch if it reaches the plane of touch but is caught, knocked or kicked by a player who is in the playing area.

questions.stem: The ball has reached the plane of touch when a player with both feet in the playing area knocks it back infield. What is the decision?

options.text: Scrum for playing a ball that was in touch
Play on, the ball is not in touch
Lineout, as the ball was knocked and not caught
Lineout, the ball crossed the plane of touch

questions.explanation: A ball that reaches the plane of touch is not in touch if a player in the playing area catches, knocks or kicks it.

questions.stem: A player jumps from in touch, catches the ball in the air and lands in the playing area. Is the ball in touch?

options.text: Yes, the player jumped from in touch
No, the player landed in the playing area
Yes, if the ball had crossed the plane of touch
Only if the ball had been kicked directly

questions.explanation: A player who jumps from within or outside the playing area, catches the ball and lands in the playing area has not put it in touch.

questions.stem: A player jumps from the field of play, catches the ball beyond the plane of touch and lands back in the field of play. Is the ball in touch?

options.text: Yes, the catch was made beyond the touchline
Only if the player was in their own 22
Yes, the ball had crossed the plane of touch
No, the player landed in the playing area

questions.explanation: If the catcher lands in the playing area, the ball is not in touch, whether or not it had reached the plane of touch.

questions.stem: A player jumps from the playing area, knocks the ball back into the playing area while in the air, and then lands in touch. Is the ball in touch?

options.text: No, the ball was sent back before the player landed
Yes, the player landed in touch
Only if the player caught the ball first
Yes, if the ball had crossed the plane of touch

questions.explanation: A player who jumps from the playing area and knocks the ball back in before landing in touch has kept it in play.

questions.stem: A player jumps from the playing area, catches the ball beyond the plane of touch and releases it back infield before landing in touch. What is the decision?

options.text: Lineout, the ball was caught beyond the plane
Play on, the ball is not in touch
Lineout, the player landed in touch

questions.explanation: A player who jumps from the playing area and catches and releases the ball back into it before landing in touch has kept it in play.

questions.stem: A player standing in touch kicks a ball that is rolling in the field of play and has not reached the plane of touch. The ball stays infield. Is the ball in touch?

options.text: Only if the ball was rolling towards touch
Yes, any contact by a player in touch counts
Yes, the player was standing in touch
No, the player kicked it without holding it

questions.explanation: A player in touch may kick or knock the ball, without holding it, provided it has not reached the plane of touch.

questions.stem: What may a player standing in touch do to a ball that has not reached the plane of touch, without putting it in touch?

options.text: Pick it up and place it infield
Kick or knock it, without holding it
Hold it for up to one second
Catch it and pass it at once

questions.explanation: The ball is not in touch if a player in touch kicks or knocks it but does not hold it, provided it has not reached the plane of touch.

questions.stem: What must a player who carries the ball into touch do with the ball?

options.text: Keep it until a lineout forms
Hand it to the assistant referee

questions.explanation: A player who carries the ball into touch must release it immediately so that a quick throw may be taken.

questions.stem: A player is forced into touch while holding the ball and keeps hold of it so that opponents cannot take a quick throw. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A player who carries the ball into touch must release it immediately so that a quick throw may be taken. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: Which team may take a quick throw?

options.text: Either team, whichever gets the ball first
The team in whose half the ball went out
The team that put the ball into touch
The team that would have thrown in at the lineout

questions.explanation: A quick throw is taken by the team that would have thrown the ball into the lineout.

questions.stem: When, in relation to the lineout, is a quick throw taken?

options.text: After the referee signals for it
Once two players from each team are in line
Straight after the lineout is formed

questions.explanation: A quick throw is a throw from touch taken before the lineout is formed.

questions.stem: Where along the touchline may a quick throw be taken?

options.text: Between the mark of touch and the thrower's own try line
Only at the mark of touch
Between the mark of touch and the opposition's try line

questions.explanation: A quick throw is taken between the mark of touch and the thrower's own try line.

questions.stem: In which directions may the ball be thrown at a quick throw?

options.text: Parallel to or towards the thrower's own try line
Parallel to or towards the opposition's try line
Only straight along the mark of touch

questions.explanation: At a quick throw the ball is thrown parallel to or towards the thrower's own try line.

questions.stem: At a quick throw, the ball is thrown towards the opposition's try line to a team-mate. What does the referee award?

options.text: An option of lineout or scrum to the opposition
A lineout to the same team

questions.explanation: A quick throw must be parallel to or towards the thrower's own try line. An incorrect quick throw gives the opposition the option of a lineout or scrum.

questions.stem: How far must the ball travel at a quick throw before it touches the ground or a player?
questions.explanation: At a quick throw the ball must reach the five-metre line before it touches the ground or hits a player.

questions.stem: A quick throw is taken and the ball touches the ground three metres in from the touchline. What does the referee award?

options.text: An option of lineout or scrum to the opposition
A lineout to the same team

questions.explanation: The ball must reach the five-metre line before it touches the ground. The sanction is an option of lineout or scrum.

questions.stem: Where must the thrower's feet be at a quick throw?

options.text: Both outside the field of play
Both at least a metre beyond the touchline
At least one outside the field of play

questions.explanation: A quick throw is taken by a player whose feet are both outside the field of play.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for an incorrectly taken quick throw, such as one thrown by a player with a foot in the field of play?
questions.explanation: An incorrect quick throw gives the opposition the option of a lineout or a scrum.

questions.stem: A lineout has already formed when a player throws the ball in quickly to a team-mate further along the touchline. What is the decision?

options.text: Quick throw disallowed, lineout to the opposition
Quick throw disallowed, free-kick to the opposition
Quick throw disallowed, lineout to the same team

questions.explanation: A quick throw is disallowed if a lineout had already been formed, and a lineout is awarded to the same team.

questions.stem: The ball is kicked into touch, and a ball person catches it and hands it to a player, who takes a quick throw. What is the decision?

options.text: Quick throw disallowed, lineout to the same team
Quick throw disallowed, lineout to the opposition
Quick throw disallowed, free-kick to the opposition

questions.explanation: A quick throw is disallowed if the ball was touched after going into touch by anyone other than the thrower or the player who carried it into touch.

questions.stem: After the ball goes into touch, who may touch it without ruling out a quick throw?

options.text: The thrower and one ball person or spectator
The thrower and the player who carried it into touch
Any player of either team, but no one else
Any player of the team that is throwing in

questions.explanation: A quick throw is ruled out if anyone other than the player throwing in or the player who carried the ball into touch has touched it.

questions.stem: A ball kicked into touch is fielded by a replacement warming up, who tosses it to a team-mate for a quick throw. Is the quick throw allowed?

options.text: No, someone other than the thrower touched the ball
Yes, the ball stayed with the same team
Yes, as the lineout had not formed
Yes, as the same ball was used

questions.explanation: The ball must not have been touched by anyone other than the thrower or the player who carried it into touch.

questions.stem: The match ball lands in the crowd and a player takes a quick throw with a spare ball. What is the decision?

options.text: Quick throw disallowed, free-kick to the opposition
Quick throw disallowed, lineout to the same team
Quick throw disallowed, scrum to the opposition

questions.explanation: A quick throw is disallowed if a different ball is used from the one that went into touch.

questions.stem: When a quick throw is disallowed, which team throws in at the lineout that follows?

options.text: The team that last kicked the ball
The team in whose half the lineout is

questions.explanation: When a quick throw is disallowed, a lineout is awarded to the same team.

questions.stem: At a quick throw, an opponent stands two metres infield and blocks the ball before it reaches the 5-metre line. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A player must not prevent the ball from travelling five metres at a quick throw. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: The mark of touch is outside the 22, but the defending team takes its quick throw inside the 22. Which team is deemed to have taken the ball into the 22?

options.text: The team that last kicked the ball
The team that put the ball into touch

questions.explanation: The defending team may take the quick throw inside the 22 but is deemed to have taken the ball into the 22.

questions.stem: The mark of touch is just outside a team's 22. The team takes a quick throw inside its 22 and the receiver at once kicks directly to touch. Is there a gain in ground?

options.text: Yes, the kick was made inside the 22
No, the team took the ball into its own 22
Yes, a quick throw resets the 22
Only if an opponent chased the kick

questions.explanation: The defending team is deemed to have taken the ball into the 22, so a direct kick to touch brings no gain in ground.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier steps into touch. Which team throws in at the lineout?

options.text: Whichever team is in its own half
Whichever team reaches the ball first

questions.explanation: When the ball-carrier goes into touch, the opposition throws in.

questions.stem: In open play a kick from between the two 22-metre lines bounces in the field of play and rolls into touch on the opposition's 10-metre line. Where is the lineout, and who throws in?

options.text: Where the ball went into touch, thrown by the opposition
In line with where the ball was kicked, thrown by the kicking team
Where the ball went into touch, thrown by the kicking team
In line with where the ball was kicked, thrown by the opposition

questions.explanation: When the ball is kicked indirectly into touch, the lineout is where the ball touches the touchline and the opposition throws in.

questions.stem: A player unintentionally passes the ball into touch. Which team throws in, and where?

options.text: The opposition, in line with where the pass was made
The passer's team, in line with where the pass was made
The passer's team, where the ball reached the touchline
The opposition, where the ball reached the touchline

questions.explanation: When a player unintentionally knocks, passes or throws the ball into touch, the opposition throws in where the ball reached the touchline.

questions.stem: The ball hits a player, bounces on the ground and then goes into touch. Where is the mark of touch?

options.text: Where the ball reached the touchline
Level with where the ball bounced
Level with where the ball hit the player

questions.explanation: When the ball hits a player and bounces into touch, the mark of touch is where the ball reached the touchline.

questions.stem: The ball hits a player and goes directly into touch. Which team throws in?

options.text: The team in whose half it went out
The team that last kicked the ball

questions.explanation: When the ball hits a player and goes into touch, the opposition throws in.

questions.stem: The ball hits a player and goes directly into touch without bouncing. Where is the mark of touch?

options.text: Level with where the ball hit the player, wherever it crossed
Where the ball crossed the touchline, wherever it hit the player
Where it crossed or level with where it hit the player, whichever is nearer that player's try line
Where it crossed or level with where it hit the player, whichever is nearer the opposition's try line

questions.explanation: The mark is where the ball reached the touchline or the point on the touchline closest to where it hit the player, whichever is nearer that player's try line.

questions.stem: A player in their own half kicks the ball, which bounces in the field of play and goes into touch inside the opposition's 22. The team had not taken the ball back into its own half. What is the decision?

options.text: Lineout to the opposition in line with the kick
Lineout to the kicking team where the ball went out
Scrum to the kicking team on the 22-metre line
Lineout to the opposition where the ball went out

questions.explanation: A kick from a player's own half that goes indirectly into touch in the opposition's 22 earns the throw-in for the kicking team.

questions.stem: For a kicking team to earn the throw-in from a kick that goes into touch in the opposition's 22, from where must the kick be made?

options.text: From inside the kicker's own 22 only

questions.explanation: The kicker must be in their own half when kicking the ball indirectly into touch in the opposition's 22.

questions.stem: A kick from a player's own half goes into touch in the opposition's 22. For the kicking team to get the throw-in, how must the ball have gone into touch?
questions.explanation: The ball must be kicked indirectly into touch in the opposition's 22.

questions.stem: A team passes the ball back from the opposition's half into its own half. With no tackle, ruck, maul or opposition touch, a player then kicks it indirectly into touch in the opposition's 22. What is the decision?

options.text: Lineout to the kicking team where the ball went out
Lineout to the opposition in line with the kick
Lineout to the kicking team on the 22-metre line
Lineout to the opposition where the ball went out

questions.explanation: The kicking team gets the throw only if it did not take the ball into its half, or a tackle, ruck or maul took place there, or an opponent touched the ball there.

questions.stem: A team takes the ball back into its own half, where a ruck then takes place. From that ruck a player kicks from inside the half and the ball bounces into touch in the opposition's 22. What is the decision?

options.text: Lineout to the kicking team where the ball went out
Lineout to the opposition where the ball went out
Lineout to the opposition in line with the kick
Lineout to the kicking team on the 22-metre line

questions.explanation: Because a ruck took place within the kicking team's half, the kicking team throws in where the ball reached the touchline.

questions.stem: A kick-off bounces into touch inside the opposition's 22. Does the kicking team get the throw-in?

options.text: Only if no opponent touched the ball
No, the rule does not apply at a kick-off or restart kick
