Yes, the kick came from the kicker's own half
Yes, as the ball bounced first

questions.explanation: The variation that gives the kicking team the throw does not apply at a kick-off or any type of restart kick.

questions.stem: A kick-off goes directly into touch in the non-kicking team's half, and that team chooses the lineout. Where is the lineout?

options.text: Where the ball crossed the touchline

questions.explanation: The throw is where the ball reached the touchline or on the halfway line, whichever is nearer the kicker's try line.

questions.stem: A 22-metre drop-out is kicked directly into touch near halfway, and the non-kicking team takes the lineout option. Where is the lineout?

options.text: On the 22-metre line the drop-out was taken from
Where the ball crossed the touchline

questions.explanation: The throw is where the ball reached the touchline or on the drop-out's sanction line, whichever is nearer the kicker's try line. For a 22-metre drop-out the sanction line is the 22-metre line.

questions.stem: A team kicks a penalty into touch. Which team throws in at the lineout?

options.text: Neither: play restarts with a scrum
Neither: play restarts with a free-kick

questions.explanation: When a penalty is kicked into touch, the kicking team throws in.

questions.stem: A penalty kick for touch bounces in the field of play before going out. Does the kicking team still throw in?

options.text: No, the ball must go out directly
Only if it bounced inside the 22
Yes, a bounce makes no difference
Only if an opponent touched it

questions.explanation: From a penalty the kicking team throws in whether the ball goes into touch directly, after bouncing in the field of play, or off an opponent or the referee.

questions.stem: From a penalty, where is the lineout when the ball is kicked directly into touch?

options.text: Where the ball reached the touchline
In line with where the penalty was taken
In line with where the offence took place

questions.explanation: From a penalty kicked into touch, the lineout is where the ball reached the touchline.

questions.stem: An opponent's kick is caught by a defender inside the defender's own 22, and the defender kicks directly into touch downfield. Where is the lineout?

options.text: In line with where the ball was kicked
Where the ball reached the touchline

questions.explanation: The defending team did not take the ball into its 22, so there is a gain in ground and the lineout is where the ball reached the touchline.

questions.stem: A team passes the ball back into its own 22 and, with no tackle, ruck, maul or opposition touch, a player kicks it directly into touch downfield. Where is the lineout?

options.text: In line with where the ball was kicked
Where the ball reached the touchline

questions.explanation: The defending team took the ball into its 22, so there is no gain in ground and the throw is in line with where the ball was kicked.

questions.stem: A team carries the ball back into its own 22, where a ruck takes place. From the ruck the ball is kicked directly into touch downfield. Where is the lineout?

options.text: In line with where the ruck took place
In line with where the ball was kicked
Where the ball reached the touchline

questions.explanation: Because a ruck took place within the 22, there is a gain in ground and the lineout is where the ball reached the touchline.

questions.stem: A team passes the ball back into its own 22, where an opponent touches the ball before a defender gathers it and kicks directly into touch downfield. Is there a gain in ground?

options.text: Yes, an opponent touched the ball within the 22
Only if a ruck or maul also formed
Only if the kick was a drop-kick
No, the defending team took the ball into the 22

questions.explanation: There is a gain in ground if an opponent touched the ball within the 22, even though the defending team took it in.

questions.stem: A player standing inside their own 22 reaches out and picks up a ball lying outside the 22, then kicks it directly into touch from inside the 22. Who is treated as having taken the ball into the 22?

options.text: The last player to kick the ball
Nobody: the ball is treated as starting in the 22

questions.explanation: A player inside their own 22 who picks up a ball that is outside the 22 has taken the ball back into the 22.

questions.stem: A player inside their own 22 catches the ball before it reaches the plane of the 22-metre line and kicks directly to touch from within the 22. Is there a gain in ground?

options.text: Only if the ball came from an opponent's kick
No, the player has taken the ball back into the 22
Yes, as the catch was made in the air
Yes, the player was standing in the 22

questions.explanation: A player inside the 22 who catches the ball before it reaches the plane of the 22-metre line has taken it back into the 22.

questions.stem: A player kicks directly into touch from inside their own 22. Does gain in ground change which team throws in?

options.text: No, the non-kicking team throws in either way
Yes, a scrum replaces the lineout if no ground is gained
Yes, the kicking team throws in if no ground is gained
Yes, the kicking team throws in if ground is gained

questions.explanation: The non-kicking team throws in whether or not there is a gain in ground. Only the place of the lineout changes.

questions.stem: A free-kick is awarded to a team inside its own 22 and is kicked directly into touch. Where is the lineout?

options.text: In line with where the free-kick was taken
Where the ball reached the touchline

questions.explanation: From a free-kick awarded within the 22, the lineout is where the ball reached the touchline.

questions.stem: A player outside their own 22 kicks the ball directly into touch downfield in open play. Where is the lineout?

options.text: Where the ball reached the touchline
In line with where the ball was kicked

questions.explanation: A direct kick to touch from outside the 22 brings no gain in ground, so the throw is in line with where the ball was kicked.

questions.stem: A player outside their own 22 slices a kick that goes directly into touch behind the place it was kicked from. Where is the lineout?

options.text: Where the ball reached the touchline
Level with the place of the last ruck
In line with where the ball was kicked

questions.explanation: The throw is where the ball reached the touchline or in line with the kick, whichever is nearer the kicker's try line.

questions.stem: A free-kick awarded outside the kicker's 22 is kicked directly into touch downfield. Is there a gain in ground?

options.text: Only if the kick was a punt
No, the lineout is in line with where the ball was kicked
Yes, a free-kick gains ground from anywhere
Yes, if the kick travelled more than ten metres

questions.explanation: A direct kick to touch from outside the 22, in open play or from a free-kick, brings no gain in ground.

questions.stem: The ball goes into touch from a knock forward and the non-offending team chooses the lineout. Where is it formed?

options.text: Five metres from where the ball went out
Where the ball reached the touchline
Level with where the knock forward happened

questions.explanation: When the ball goes into touch from a knock or throw forward, the lineout is where the ball reached the touchline.

questions.stem: A team is awarded a penalty for a lineout infringement and chooses another lineout. Where is it formed, and who throws in?

options.text: On the 15-metre line, thrown by the offending team
Ten metres downfield, thrown by the non-offending team
At the original lineout, thrown by the offending team
At the original lineout, thrown by the non-offending team

questions.explanation: A lineout chosen from a penalty or free-kick for a lineout infringement is where the original lineout took place, and the opposition of the offenders throws in.

questions.stem: After an incorrect lineout throw, the opposition chooses another lineout. Where is it formed?

options.text: Five metres nearer the offending team's try line
Where the original lineout took place
In line with where the ball landed

questions.explanation: Following an incorrect throw, the lineout is where the original lineout took place and the opposition throws in.

questions.stem: On what is a lineout formed?
questions.explanation: A lineout is formed on the mark of touch.

questions.stem: How close to a try line may the mark of touch be?
questions.explanation: The mark of touch cannot be within five metres of a try line.

questions.stem: What is the mark of touch?

options.text: An imaginary line parallel to the touchline, five metres infield
The spot on the touchline where the thrower stands
The line ten metres behind the lineout
An imaginary line at right angles to the touchline where the ball is thrown in

questions.explanation: The mark of touch is an imaginary line in the field of play at right angles to the touchline through the place where the ball is thrown in.

questions.stem: How far from the mark of touch does each team's line of players stand at a lineout?
questions.explanation: Each team forms a single line parallel to and half a metre from the mark of touch on its own side.

questions.stem: How wide is the gap between the two lines of players at a lineout?
questions.explanation: Each line is half a metre from the mark of touch, which leaves a gap of one metre between the two lines.

questions.stem: Between which two lines do the lineout players stand?
questions.explanation: Each team forms its line between the five-metre and 15-metre lines.

questions.stem: Until when must the gap between the two lines at a lineout be maintained?

options.text: Until the ball is thrown in
Until the thrower raises the ball

questions.explanation: The gap between the lines must be maintained until the ball is thrown in.

questions.stem: A team closes the gap at a lineout before the ball is thrown in. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: The gap must be maintained until the ball is thrown in. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of players from each team needed to form a lineout?
questions.explanation: A minimum of two players from each team are required to form a lineout.

questions.stem: Within what time of the mark being made must teams form the lineout?
questions.explanation: Teams form the lineout within 30 seconds of a mark being made.

questions.stem: A team takes longer than 30 seconds to form a lineout after the mark is made. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Teams must form the lineout within 30 seconds of the mark being made. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: Which team decides the maximum number of players each team may have in a lineout?

options.text: The team in whose half the lineout is
The team with fewer players on the field

questions.explanation: The team throwing in determines the maximum number of players that each team may have in the lineout.

questions.stem: The throwing team puts five players in the lineout and does not throw at once. The non-throwing team lines up six. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: The non-throwing team may not have more players in the lineout than the throwing team. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: May the non-throwing team have fewer players in the lineout than the throwing team?

options.text: Yes, fewer is allowed but more is not
No, the numbers must match exactly
Yes, and it may also have more

questions.explanation: The non-throwing team may not have more players than the throwing team, but may have fewer.

questions.stem: The throw is taken as soon as the lineout is formed, while the non-throwing team has one more player in the line than the throwing team. Is the non-throwing team liable to sanction?

options.text: Only if the extra player wins the ball
No, as the throw was taken as soon as the lineout formed

questions.explanation: The limit on numbers applies unless the throw is taken as soon as the lineout is formed.

questions.stem: Where must the non-throwing team have a player at a lineout, besides those in the line?

options.text: Between the touchline and the 5-metre line
Directly behind its own line of players
Between the 15-metre line and the far touchline

questions.explanation: The non-throwing team must have a player between the touchline and the five-metre line.

questions.stem: The non-throwing team's player between the touchline and the 5-metre line stands how far from the mark of touch?
questions.explanation: That player stands two metres from the mark of touch on their own team's side of the lineout.

questions.stem: The non-throwing team's player between the touchline and the 5-metre line stands how far from the 5-metre line?
questions.explanation: That player stands two metres from the mark of touch and two metres from the five-metre line.

questions.stem: How many receivers may each team have at a lineout?

options.text: As many as the throwing team allows

questions.explanation: Each team may have only one receiver.

questions.stem: Is a team required to have a receiver at a lineout?

options.text: Yes, each team must have one

questions.explanation: The law covers a team that elects to have a receiver, so a receiver is optional.

questions.stem: How far from team-mates in the lineout must a receiver stand?
questions.explanation: A receiver stands two metres away from their team-mates in the lineout.

questions.stem: Between which lines does a receiver stand?

options.text: The 15-metre line and the far touchline

questions.explanation: A receiver stands between the five-metre and 15-metre lines, two metres from team-mates in the lineout.

questions.stem: A team lines up with two receivers at a lineout. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Each team may have only one receiver. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: What is a receiver at a lineout?

options.text: The player at the front of the line
The lineout player who catches the throw
A player placed to take the ball from the lineout
The player who throws the ball in

questions.explanation: The receiver is the player in a position to receive the ball if it is knocked or passed back from a lineout.

questions.stem: Once a lineout is formed, for what reason may a player of the throwing team leave it?

options.text: Only to change positions with other participating players
To join the backline before the ball is thrown
To reduce the numbers in the lineout at any time
For any reason, provided the throw has not been made

questions.explanation: Players of the throwing team may not leave the lineout other than to change positions with other participating players.

questions.stem: Once a lineout is formed, for what reason may a player of the non-throwing team leave it?

options.text: Only so the team does not outnumber the opposition
To take up a second receiver position
For any reason before the throw

questions.explanation: Players of the non-throwing team may leave the lineout only to ensure they do not have more players than the opposition.

questions.stem: May participating players change places in the lineout?

options.text: Only the throwing team's players may
Yes, before the ball is thrown
No, positions are fixed once the lineout forms

questions.explanation: Participating players may change places in the lineout before the ball is thrown.

questions.stem: Before the ball is thrown in, a lineout player pushes the opponent standing opposite. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Players must not make any contact with an opponent before the ball is thrown in. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: Before the throw, may a lifter take hold of the team-mate they are going to lift?

options.text: Only once the jumper has left the ground
No, no contact until the ball is thrown
Yes, pre-gripping is allowed within limits

questions.explanation: Players who are going to lift or support a jumper may pre-grip that team-mate, within limits on where they grip.

questions.stem: When pre-gripping a jumper from behind, below what must a supporting player not grip?
questions.explanation: A supporting player must not grip below the shorts from behind.

questions.stem: When pre-gripping a jumper from the front, below what must a supporting player not grip?
questions.explanation: A supporting player must not grip below the thighs from the front.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for pre-gripping a jumper below the permitted level?
questions.explanation: Gripping below the shorts from behind or below the thighs from the front is a free-kick offence.

questions.stem: From what moment may a lineout player jump or be lifted?

options.text: Once the thrower's arms start to move
Once the ball has left the thrower's hands

questions.explanation: Players must not jump or be lifted or supported before the ball has left the hands of the player throwing in.

questions.stem: A jumper is lifted before the ball has left the thrower's hands. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Jumping, lifting or supporting before the ball has left the thrower's hands is a free-kick offence.

questions.stem: Where does the thrower stand to throw into a lineout?

options.text: On the mark of touch, both feet outside the field of play
Anywhere behind the mark of touch
On the 5-metre line, facing the lineout
On the mark of touch, one foot in the field of play

questions.explanation: The thrower stands on the mark of touch with both feet outside the field of play.

questions.stem: The thrower steps into the field of play before releasing the ball at a lineout. What is the sanction?

options.text: Lineout retaken by the same team

questions.explanation: The thrower must not step into the field of play until the ball has been thrown. The sanction is an option of lineout or scrum.

questions.stem: How must the ball be thrown in at a lineout?

options.text: In any direction beyond the 5-metre line
Straight along the mark of touch towards a lineout player
Towards the thrower's own line of players

questions.explanation: The ball must be thrown in straight along the mark of touch towards a lineout player.

questions.stem: A lineout throw is not straight, and the non-throwing team did not lift a team-mate to compete for the ball. What is the decision?

options.text: Lineout retaken by the same team
Option of lineout or scrum to the non-throwing team

questions.explanation: If the non-throwing team does not lift a team-mate to compete for the ball, play continues after a throw that is not straight.

questions.stem: A lineout throw is not straight, and the non-throwing team lifted a team-mate to compete for the ball. What is the decision?

options.text: Option of lineout or scrum to the non-throwing team

questions.explanation: If the non-throwing team lifts a team-mate to compete for the ball, it is offered the option of a lineout or scrum.

questions.stem: What decides whether a lineout throw that is not straight is sanctioned?

options.text: Whether the ball went beyond the 15-metre line
How far the ball drifted from the mark of touch
Whether the throwing team won the ball
Whether the non-throwing team lifted a team-mate to compete

questions.explanation: Play continues unless the non-throwing team lifted a team-mate to compete for the ball.

questions.stem: How far must a lineout throw travel before it hits the ground or is played?
questions.explanation: The ball must reach the five-metre line before it hits the ground or is played.

questions.stem: A lineout throw is caught by the front player before the ball has reached the 5-metre line. What does the referee award?

options.text: A retaken lineout to the same team
An option of lineout or scrum to the opposition

questions.explanation: The ball must reach the five-metre line before it is played. The sanction is an option of lineout or scrum.

questions.stem: Team A's throw is ruled incorrect, and Team B chooses the lineout. Team B's throw is then not straight. What is awarded?
questions.explanation: If the lineout is chosen and the ball is again not thrown straight, a scrum is awarded to the team that originally threw in.

questions.stem: Once the lineout is formed, the thrower delays the throw. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: The ball must be thrown in without delay once the lineout is formed. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: The thrower at a lineout makes a dummy throw to draw the opposition's jumpers. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: The thrower must not pretend to throw the ball. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: An opponent at the front of the lineout stretches out an arm and blocks the throw before the ball has travelled five metres. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: No player can block the throw or prevent the ball from travelling five metres. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: When does a lineout commence?

options.text: When a jumper touches the ball
When the ball leaves the thrower's hands
When the thrower raises the ball

questions.explanation: The lineout commences once the ball leaves the hands of the thrower.

questions.stem: Once the lineout has commenced, when may the thrower move to the receiver position?

options.text: Only if the opposition won the throw
Only once the lineout has ended

questions.explanation: The thrower may move to the receiver position if that position is empty.

questions.stem: Once the lineout has commenced, the thrower may stay within what distance of the touchline?
questions.explanation: The thrower and the thrower's immediate opponent may stay within five metres of the touchline.

questions.stem: Once the lineout has commenced, may the thrower join the lineout?

options.text: Yes, the thrower may join the lineout
Only if a team-mate leaves the line
No, the thrower must stay in touch
Only after the ball has been caught

questions.explanation: Once the lineout has commenced, the thrower may join the lineout.

questions.stem: Once the lineout has commenced, the thrower runs across to stand level with the lineout, beyond the 15-metre line, while the lineout is still going on. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: The thrower may join the lineout, retire to the non-participants' offside line, stay within five metres of touch or fill an empty receiver position. Anywhere else is offside.

questions.stem: From what moment may lineout players compete for possession of the ball?

options.text: Once the ball has touched the ground
Once the ball has passed the 15-metre line

questions.explanation: Once the lineout has commenced, any player in the lineout may compete for possession of the ball.

questions.stem: When may a jumper catch or deflect the ball with the outside arm?

options.text: At any time during the lineout
Only when both hands are above the head
Only when the inside arm is being held
Only on the jumper's own team's throw

questions.explanation: A jumper may catch or deflect the ball with the outside arm only if both hands are above the head.

questions.stem: A jumper keeps the inside hand down by the waist and taps the ball back using only the outside arm. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: The outside arm may be used alone only if the jumper has both hands above the head. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: What must lifters do as soon as the ball has been won by either team?

options.text: Lower the jumper to the ground safely
Hold the jumper up until a maul forms
Step back out of the lineout
Let go of the jumper at once

questions.explanation: Players who lift or support a team-mate must lower that player to the ground safely as soon as the ball is won by either team.

questions.stem: Lifters let go of a jumper in the air once the ball is won, instead of lowering the player safely. What is the sanction under the lineout law?
questions.explanation: Lifters must lower the jumper to the ground safely as soon as the ball is won. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: A lineout player leaves the lineout to be in a position to receive the ball. Within what distance of the mark of touch must the player stay?
questions.explanation: A player who leaves the lineout to receive the ball must remain within 10 metres of the mark of touch.

questions.stem: A lineout player peels away to receive the ball. Besides staying within 10 metres of the mark of touch, what must the player do?

options.text: Keep moving until the lineout is over

questions.explanation: A player who leaves the lineout to receive the ball must keep moving until the lineout is over.

questions.stem: A jumper catches the ball and is still in the air when an opposing lineout player grabs the jumper and pulls them down. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: An opponent in possession may be grasped and brought to ground only when that player is not in the air.

questions.stem: A jumper catches the ball, lands on both feet and is then grasped and brought to ground by an opposing lineout player. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A lineout player may grasp and bring to ground an opponent in possession of the ball, provided that player is not in the air.

questions.stem: How do lineout players stay onside before the throw has touched a player or the ground?

options.text: By standing at least a metre from the mark of touch
By remaining on their side of the mark of touch
By keeping bound to a team-mate

questions.explanation: Lineout players are onside if they remain on their side of the mark of touch until the ball has been thrown in and has touched a player or the ground.

questions.stem: A jumper crosses the mark of touch while competing for the ball and does not catch it. What must the jumper do?

options.text: Stay there until the ball is won
Return to their own side immediately

questions.explanation: Players jumping for the ball who cross the mark of touch and do not catch the ball must immediately return to their own side.

questions.stem: Before the ball has been thrown in and has touched a player or the ground, where is the offside line for lineout players?

options.text: Ten metres behind the mark of touch

questions.explanation: Until the ball is thrown in and has touched a player or the ground, the offside line for lineout players is the mark of touch.

questions.stem: Once the throw has touched a player or the ground, where is the offside line for lineout players?

options.text: The hindmost foot of the lineout
Ten metres behind the mark of touch

questions.explanation: After the ball has touched a player or the ground, the lineout players' offside line is a line through the ball.

questions.stem: A maul forms at the mark of touch from a lineout. A lineout player who does not join it must retire to which offside line?

options.text: Ten metres behind the mark of touch
The hindmost foot of that player's team in the maul

questions.explanation: When a ruck or maul forms at the mark of touch, a participating player joins it or retires to the hindmost foot of their team in it.

questions.stem: A ruck forms at the mark of touch during a lineout. What two choices does a participating player have?

options.text: Join the ruck or retire to their team's hindmost foot
Leave the lineout or stand still
Join the ruck or stay on the mark of touch
Retire ten metres or stay in the line

questions.explanation: A participating player may either join the ruck or maul, or retire to the offside line at the hindmost foot of their team in it.

questions.stem: When may a lineout player move beyond the 15-metre line?

options.text: Once the ball has been thrown
Once the thrower has raised the ball
Only when the lineout has ended

questions.explanation: Once the ball has been thrown, a lineout player may move beyond the 15-metre line.

questions.stem: A lineout player runs beyond the 15-metre line as the ball is thrown, but the throw does not go beyond the 15-metre line. What must the player do?

options.text: Stay there until the lineout ends

questions.explanation: If the ball does not go beyond the 15-metre line, the player must immediately return to the lineout.

questions.stem: How far from the mark of touch must players who are not taking part in the lineout stay?
questions.explanation: Players not participating in the lineout must remain at least 10 metres from the mark of touch on their own team's side.

questions.stem: A lineout is formed seven metres from the defending team's try line. Where is the offside line for that team's players who are not taking part?

options.text: Three metres behind the try line

questions.explanation: Non-participants must be at least 10 metres from the mark of touch or behind the try line if this is nearer.

questions.stem: The ball is thrown in before a non-participating player has got back onside. What must that player do to avoid sanction?

options.text: Wait to be put onside by a team-mate
Stand still until the lineout ends
Retire immediately to the onside position

questions.explanation: The player is not liable to sanction if the player immediately retires to the onside position.

questions.stem: Can a non-participating player who is offside at a lineout be put onside by the action of another player?

options.text: No, the player must retire to the onside position
Yes, when a team-mate runs past from behind
Yes, when an opponent kicks the ball
Yes, when an opponent runs five metres with the ball

questions.explanation: The player cannot be put onside by the action of any other player.

questions.stem: The throwing team's backs move forward as soon as their team-mate throws the ball in. May the opposing backs also move forward?

options.text: No, they must wait until the lineout ends
Only once the ball has been caught
Yes, once the throwing team's players have moved forward
Only if the ball passes the 15-metre line first

questions.explanation: Once the ball has been thrown in by a team-mate, non-participants may move forward, and if they do their opponents may also move forward.

questions.stem: The throwing team's backs move forward at the throw, but the ball does not go beyond the 15-metre line. What must they do to avoid sanction?

options.text: Carry on, as the throw has been made
Retire immediately to their offside line

questions.explanation: If the ball does not go beyond the 15-metre line, the players are not liable to sanction if they immediately retire to their offside lines.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for being offside at a lineout?
questions.explanation: Offside at a lineout is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: The ball is passed back out of the lineout. What has happened to the lineout?

options.text: It goes on until the ball passes the 15-metre line
It goes on until the receiver passes the ball

questions.explanation: The lineout ends when the ball or a player in possession of it leaves the lineout.

questions.stem: A lineout player catches the ball and carries it into the area between the touchline and the 5-metre line. Has the lineout ended?

options.text: Yes, the ball-carrier has entered that area
No, the ball must leave the lineout backwards
No, the ball must go beyond the 15-metre line

questions.explanation: The lineout ends when the ball or a player in possession enters the area between the touchline and the five-metre line.

questions.stem: The throw goes over the back of the lineout and beyond the 15-metre line. What has happened to the lineout?

options.text: It goes on until a player catches the ball
It goes on until the ball touches the ground

questions.explanation: The lineout ends when the ball goes beyond the 15-metre line.

questions.stem: Which line must the ball or ball-carrier go beyond, on the infield side, to end a lineout?
questions.explanation: The lineout ends when the ball or a player in possession goes beyond the 15-metre line.

questions.stem: A maul forms at a lineout. When does the lineout end?

options.text: As soon as the maul has formed
When the maul has moved five metres
When every foot in the maul is beyond the mark of touch
When one team's hindmost foot crosses the mark

questions.explanation: The lineout ends when a ruck or maul forms and all of the feet of all of the players in it move beyond the mark of touch.

questions.stem: A maul from a lineout has been driven forward, but one player's foot is still on the mark of touch. Has the lineout ended?

options.text: Yes, a maul ends the lineout when it forms
No, every foot in the maul must be beyond the mark of touch
Only for the team going backwards
Yes, the maul has moved forward

questions.explanation: All of the feet of all of the players in the maul must move beyond the mark of touch before the lineout ends.

questions.stem: Which of these ends a lineout?

options.text: The receiver moves towards the line

questions.explanation: The lineout ends when the ball becomes unplayable, as well as when the ball leaves it or a ruck or maul moves beyond the mark of touch.

questions.stem: On what condition may a lineout player move to the receiver position before the lineout has ended?

options.text: The player is at the back of the line

questions.explanation: Other than by moving to the receiver position if that position is empty, no lineout player may leave the lineout until it has ended.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a scrum?

options.text: To restart play with a throw after the ball has gone into touch
To restart play with a kick after points have been scored
To restart play with a contest for possession after a minor infringement or stoppage
To give the non-offending team possession without a contest

questions.explanation: The purpose of a scrum is to restart play with a contest for possession after a minor infringement or stoppage.

questions.stem: A player knocks the ball forward in open play. Which team throws in at the scrum?
questions.explanation: After a knock forward or throw forward, the non-offending team throws in.

questions.stem: Where is the scrum after a knock forward in open play?

options.text: In the middle of the field, level with the infringement
In the scrum zone, closest to the place of infringement
In the scrum zone, closest to where the ball was regathered
In the scrum zone, closest to where the ball came to rest

questions.explanation: The scrum is in the scrum zone at the point closest to the place of infringement.

questions.stem: A knock forward happens in a lineout. Where is the scrum?

options.text: Where the ball landed after the knock forward
On the mark of touch, 15 metres in from the touchline
In midfield, level with the mark of touch
On the mark of touch, 5 metres in from the touchline

questions.explanation: For a knock forward or throw forward at a lineout, the scrum is 15 metres in from touch on the mark of touch.

questions.stem: A lineout throw is incorrect and the opposition takes the scrum option. How far in from the touchline is the scrum?
questions.explanation: After an incorrect throw at a lineout, or an incorrect quick throw, the scrum is 15 metres in from touch on the mark of touch.

questions.stem: A team takes the scrum option for offside in open play. Where is the scrum?

options.text: Closest to where the offside player interfered
Closest to where the ball landed
Closest to where the offside player was standing
Closest to where the offending team last played the ball

questions.explanation: The scrum is in the scrum zone at the point closest to where the offending team last played the ball.

questions.stem: A team awarded a penalty chooses a scrum. Where is the scrum?

options.text: In the middle of the field, level with the infringement
Ten metres on from where the infringement took place
Closest to where the infringement took place
Closest to where the ball was when play stopped

questions.explanation: A scrum chosen from a penalty is in the scrum zone at the point closest to where the infringement took place.

questions.stem: A defender carries the ball into their own in-goal and makes it dead. Which team throws in at the scrum?
questions.explanation: When the defending team takes the ball into its in-goal and makes it dead, the attacking team throws in at the scrum.

questions.stem: A tackle becomes unplayable with no offence seen. One team was moving forward before the stoppage. Which team throws in at the scrum?

options.text: The team in possession before the tackle

questions.explanation: After an unplayable tackle or ruck, the team last moving forward throws in.

questions.stem: A ruck becomes unplayable and neither team was moving forward. Which team throws in at the scrum?

options.text: The team that took the ball into the ruck
The team that did not take the ball into the ruck

questions.explanation: After an unplayable tackle or ruck, if neither team was moving forward, the attacking team throws in.

questions.stem: A maul ends unsuccessfully. Which team normally throws in at the scrum?

options.text: The team not in possession at the start of the maul
The team in possession at the start of the maul

questions.explanation: After a maul that ends unsuccessfully, the team not in possession at the start of the maul throws in.

questions.stem: A maul ends unsuccessfully and the referee cannot decide which team had possession at the start. One team was moving forward before the maul stopped. Which team throws in?

options.text: The team moving forward before the maul stopped
The team with the ball when the maul stopped

questions.explanation: If the referee cannot decide which team had possession at the start, the team moving forward before the maul stopped throws in.

questions.stem: A maul ends unsuccessfully. The referee cannot decide which team had possession at the start, and neither team was moving forward. Which team throws in?

options.text: The team with the ball when the maul stopped
The team that last won a lineout

questions.explanation: If possession at the start cannot be decided and neither team was moving forward, the attacking team throws in.

questions.stem: A maul forms straight after a player catches a kick in open play and then becomes unplayable. Which team throws in at the scrum?

options.text: The team not in possession at the start of the maul
The team in possession at the start of the maul
The team that kicked the ball

questions.explanation: For an unplayable maul after a kick in open play, the team in possession at the start of the maul throws in.

questions.stem: A kick-off is taken incorrectly and the non-kicking team chooses a scrum. Where is the scrum?

options.text: As near as possible to the middle of the halfway line

questions.explanation: The scrum is as near as possible to the middle point of the line behind which the kick was taken, which for a kick-off is the halfway line.

questions.stem: A team fails to play the ball after the call of "use it" at a ruck. Which team throws in at the scrum?
questions.explanation: For a failure to use it at a scrum, ruck or maul, the team not in possession throws in.

questions.stem: The ball touches the referee and one team gains an advantage from it. Which team throws in at the scrum?

options.text: The team that did not last play the ball
The team that last played the ball

questions.explanation: When the ball or ball-carrier touches the referee and either team gains an advantage, the team that last played the ball throws in.

questions.stem: Play is stopped because of an injury, with no infringement. Which team throws in at the scrum?

options.text: The team of the injured player

questions.explanation: After a stoppage due to injury, the team last in possession throws in.

questions.stem: Play is stopped for an injury. Where is the scrum?

options.text: In the middle of the field, level with the injury
In the scrum zone, where the ball was last played
In the scrum zone, closest to the injured player

questions.explanation: After a stoppage due to injury, the scrum is in the scrum zone at the point where the ball was last played.

questions.stem: A kicker fails to take a penalty attempt at goal within the time limit. What is awarded?
questions.explanation: When a penalty attempt at goal is not taken within the time limit, a scrum is awarded to the non-offending team where the penalty was awarded.

questions.stem: The referee awards a scrum for a reason not covered elsewhere in law. Which team throws in?

options.text: The team last in possession or, failing that, the defending team
The team that last threw in at a scrum
The team in whose half play had stopped
The team last moving forward or, failing that, the attacking team

questions.explanation: For any other reason not covered in law, the team that was last moving forward throws in or, if neither was, the attacking team.

questions.stem: Where on the pitch is a scrum formed?

options.text: In the scrum zone, at a mark indicated by the referee
On the nearest 15-metre line in every case
Anywhere in the playing area, in-goal included
Exactly where the infringement happened, wherever that is

questions.explanation: A scrum is formed in the scrum zone at a mark indicated by the referee.

questions.stem: In which direction does the middle line of a scrum run?

options.text: Along the line of the last pass

questions.explanation: The referee's mark creates the middle line of the scrum, which runs parallel to the try lines.

questions.stem: Within what time of the mark being made must teams be ready to form a scrum?
questions.explanation: Teams must be ready to form the scrum within 30 seconds of the mark being made.

questions.stem: A team is not ready to form the scrum within 30 seconds of the mark being made. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Teams must be ready to form the scrum within 30 seconds of the mark being made. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: When both teams have 15 players, how many players from each team form the scrum?
questions.explanation: When both teams have 15 players, eight players from each team bind together in formation.

questions.stem: Which players make up the front row of a scrum?
questions.explanation: Each team must have two props and one hooker in the front row.

questions.stem: How many locks must each team have in the second row of a full scrum?
questions.explanation: Each team must have two locks in the second row.

questions.stem: How many back-row players complete each team's side of a full scrum?
questions.explanation: Three back-row players from each team complete the scrum.

questions.stem: Both teams have 15 players, but one team packs down with only seven in the scrum. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: When both teams have 15 players, eight from each team must form the scrum. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: What is the fewest players a team may have in a scrum?
questions.explanation: A team must not have fewer than five players in the scrum.

questions.stem: When may the number of players in a scrum be reduced below eight?

options.text: When a team is reduced to fewer than 15 players
Whenever the captain of the team throwing in chooses
When the two packs agree before the engagement
When the scrum is within five metres of a try line

questions.explanation: When a team is reduced to fewer than 15 for any reason, the number of players in the scrum may be similarly reduced.

questions.stem: One team is down to 14 players and reduces its scrum to seven. Must the other team also reduce to seven?

options.text: Only if the scrum is uncontested
Yes, numbers in the scrum must match
No, the other team need not make a similar reduction
Only if the reduced team is throwing in

questions.explanation: Where a permitted reduction is made by one team, there is no requirement for the other team to make a similar reduction.

questions.stem: To whom do the props bind in a scrum?
questions.explanation: The props bind to the hooker.

questions.stem: How does the hooker bind in a scrum?

options.text: With both arms, under the props' arms only
With both arms, over or under the props' arms
With both arms, over the props' arms only
With one arm, over a prop's shoulder

questions.explanation: The hooker binds with both arms, either over or under the arms of the props.

questions.stem: With whom do the locks bind in a scrum?

options.text: The props in front of them only
The props in front of them and each other
The flankers and the number eight

questions.explanation: The locks bind with the props immediately in front of them and with each other.

questions.stem: How must the back-row players bind in a scrum?

options.text: On a lock's body with both arms
On each other with both arms
On a prop's body with at least one arm
On a lock's body with at least one arm

questions.explanation: All other players in the scrum bind on a lock's body with at least one arm.

questions.stem: A flanker stands beside the scrum without binding on a lock. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: All players in the scrum other than the front five must bind on a lock's body with at least one arm. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: How do the two packs line up in relation to the middle line of the scrum?

options.text: Both on the same side of it
Either side of it and parallel to it
Either side of it and at an angle to it

questions.explanation: The two groups face each other, either side of and parallel to the middle line.

questions.stem: How far apart do the two front rows stand before engagement?

options.text: Not more than an arm's length

questions.explanation: The two front rows stand not more than an arm's length apart.

questions.stem: Which players are at the mark when the front rows line up for a scrum?
questions.explanation: The two front rows stand not more than an arm's length apart with the hookers at the mark.

questions.stem: What is the first call in the scrum engagement sequence?
questions.explanation: The referee calls "crouch", then "bind", then "set".

questions.stem: What is the second call in the scrum engagement sequence?
questions.explanation: The referee calls "crouch", then "bind", then "set".

questions.stem: On which call do the two packs engage?
questions.explanation: The teams engage on the call of "set".

questions.stem: In what condition must both sides be before the referee makes each call in the engagement sequence?
questions.explanation: Each call is made when both sides are square, stable and stationary.

questions.stem: How must front-row players hold their heads and shoulders in the crouch?
questions.explanation: In the crouch the front rows have their heads and shoulders no lower than their hips.

questions.stem: For how long must front-row players keep their heads and shoulders no lower than their hips?

options.text: For the duration of the scrum
Until the ball is thrown in

questions.explanation: The position is maintained for the duration of the scrum.

questions.stem: On which side of the immediate opponent's head does a front-row player place their head in the crouch?
questions.explanation: The front rows crouch with their heads to the left of their immediate opponents' heads.

questions.stem: Why do front-row players crouch with their heads to the left of their opponents' heads?

options.text: So that the hookers can see the ball
So that no head touches an opponent's neck or shoulders
So that the props can bind with the right arm
So that the scrum-half can see the tunnel

questions.explanation: The heads go to the left so that no player's head is touching the neck or shoulders of an opponent.

questions.stem: Which player must have a "brake" foot in position during the crouch?
questions.explanation: Hookers must have a brake foot positioned to help stability and to avoid axial loading.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the hooker's brake foot?

options.text: To help stability and avoid axial loading
To win the ball more quickly
To mark the middle line for the scrum-half
To stop the scrum from wheeling

questions.explanation: The brake foot is placed forward in the middle of the tunnel to help stability and to avoid axial loading.

questions.stem: During which calls of the engagement sequence is the hooker's brake foot kept in place?
questions.explanation: The brake foot position is adopted throughout the "crouch" and "bind" elements of the engagement sequence.

questions.stem: When may the hooker withdraw the brake foot?

options.text: Only once the ball has been won
As soon as the referee calls "crouch"
After the "set" and before the strike for the ball

questions.explanation: The brake foot can only be withdrawn after the "set" and before the strike for the ball.

questions.stem: A hooker fails to position a brake foot during the crouch. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Hookers must have a brake foot positioned. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: How does a loose-head prop bind on the opposing tight-head prop?

options.text: Left arm outside the tight-head's right arm
Left arm inside the tight-head's right arm
Right arm inside the tight-head's left arm
Right arm outside the tight-head's left arm

questions.explanation: Each loose-head prop binds by placing the left arm inside the right arm of the opposing tight-head prop.

questions.stem: How does a tight-head prop bind on the opposing loose-head prop?

options.text: Left arm inside the loose-head's right upper arm
Right arm inside the loose-head's left upper arm
Right arm outside the loose-head's left upper arm
Left arm outside the loose-head's right upper arm

questions.explanation: Each tight-head prop binds by placing the right arm outside the left upper arm of the opposing loose-head prop.

questions.stem: What must each prop grip when binding on an opponent?

options.text: The back or side of the opponent's jersey

questions.explanation: Each prop binds by gripping the back or side of the opponent's jersey.

questions.stem: For how long must all players maintain their binding in a scrum?

options.text: Until the ball is thrown in
For the duration of the scrum

questions.explanation: All players' binding is maintained for the duration of the scrum.

questions.stem: A prop binds on the opponent's arm instead of the back or side of the jersey. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Each prop must bind by gripping the back or side of the opponent's jersey. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: What is created when the two packs engage on the "set"?

options.text: A mark for the next restart
A tunnel into which the ball is thrown
A gap for the scrum-halves to stand in
An offside line through the ball

questions.explanation: The teams engage, completing the formation of the scrum and creating a tunnel into which the ball will be thrown.

questions.stem: On the "set", what must all players in the scrum be?

options.text: In position and ready to push forward

questions.explanation: On the "set" all players must be in position and ready to push forward.

questions.stem: On the "set", how must each front-row player's feet be placed?

options.text: One on the ground and one raised to strike
Both on the ground, with weight equally on each
Both on the ground, with weight firmly on at least one
Both level with the hooker's brake foot

questions.explanation: Each front-row player must have both feet on the ground, with their weight firmly on at least one foot.

questions.stem: Where must each hooker's feet be on the "set"?

options.text: Level with the feet of the locks
In the middle of the tunnel
In front of the foremost foot of that team's props
In line with, or behind, the foremost foot of that team's props

questions.explanation: Each hooker's feet must be in line with, or behind, the foremost foot of that team's props.

questions.stem: A front row engages before the referee calls "set". What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: The teams engage only on the call of "set". The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: Who chooses which side of the scrum the ball is thrown in from?

options.text: The hooker of the team throwing in

questions.explanation: The scrum-half chooses which side of the scrum to throw in the ball.

questions.stem: From where does the scrum-half throw the ball into the scrum?
questions.explanation: The scrum-half throws in the ball from the chosen side, from outside the tunnel.

questions.stem: How many forward movements may the scrum-half make when throwing the ball in?

options.text: As many as are needed to time the strike
Two movements, a dummy then the throw

questions.explanation: The ball is thrown in with a single forward movement.

questions.stem: At what speed must the ball be thrown into the scrum?

options.text: At a slow speed, so both hookers can strike
At any speed the scrum-half chooses

questions.explanation: The ball is thrown in at a quick speed.

questions.stem: How may the scrum-half line up when throwing the ball in straight?

options.text: Standing inside the tunnel between the front rows
With both feet beside the feet of their own locks
Directly behind the feet of their own hooker
With a shoulder on the middle line, nearer their own side

questions.explanation: The scrum-half may align a shoulder on the middle line of the scrum, standing a shoulder-width closer to their own side.

questions.stem: Where must the ball first touch the ground when it is thrown into the scrum?
questions.explanation: The ball must be thrown in so that it first touches the ground inside the tunnel.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for a throw-in at the scrum that is not straight?
questions.explanation: The ball must be thrown in straight. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: Both packs are square, stable and stationary, and the scrum-half delays the throw-in. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: The scrum-half must throw in the ball without delay. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: When does a scrum begin?

options.text: When the ball touches the ground in the tunnel
When the ball leaves the scrum-half's hands

questions.explanation: The scrum begins when the ball leaves the hands of the scrum-half.

questions.stem: From what moment may the teams push in a scrum?

options.text: When the ball leaves the scrum-half's hands
When the front rows have bound
When the ball has been hooked

questions.explanation: Only when the scrum begins, as the ball leaves the scrum-half's hands, may the teams push.

questions.stem: A pack pushes before the ball has left the scrum-half's hands. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Only when the scrum begins may the teams push. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: Besides striking for the ball, how may possession be gained in a scrum?

options.text: By pushing the opposition backwards and off the ball
By handling the ball in the tunnel
By wheeling the scrum through 90 degrees
By standing up in the front row

questions.explanation: Possession may be gained by pushing the opposition backwards and off the ball.

questions.stem: In what direction must players push in a scrum?

options.text: At an angle towards the ball
Straight and parallel to the ground

questions.explanation: Players may push provided they do so straight and parallel to the ground.

questions.stem: A prop drives in at an angle instead of pushing straight. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Players must push straight and parallel to the ground. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: From what moment may front-row players strike for the ball?

options.text: Once the ball touches the ground in the tunnel
Once the ball has passed the first prop
Once the ball leaves the scrum-half's hands

questions.explanation: Front-row players may strike for the ball only once it touches the ground in the tunnel.

questions.stem: A hooker strikes for the ball before it has touched the ground in the tunnel. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Front-row players may strike only once the ball touches the ground in the tunnel. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: With which foot may a front-row player strike for the ball?

options.text: The foot nearer the scrum-half only
Either foot, but not both at once

questions.explanation: A front-row player striking for the ball may do so with either foot but not both at the same time.

questions.stem: A front-row player strikes for the ball with both feet at the same time. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A front-row player may strike with either foot but not both at the same time. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: Which player is required to strike for the ball in a scrum?

options.text: The hooker of the team that threw in
The loose-head prop of the team that threw in
The number eight of the team that threw in
The hooker of the team that did not throw in

questions.explanation: The hooker from the team which threw in the ball must strike for the ball.

questions.stem: The hooker of the team throwing in makes no attempt to strike for the ball. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: The hooker from the team which threw in the ball must strike for it. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: A front-row player intentionally kicks the ball back out of the tunnel the way it came in. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A front-row player must not intentionally kick the ball out of the tunnel from the direction it was thrown. The sanction is a free-kick.

questions.stem: With which parts of the body may players in the scrum play the ball?
questions.explanation: Any player within the scrum may play the ball, but only with their feet or lower legs.

questions.stem: A lock in the scrum traps the ball and lifts it with the legs. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Players in the scrum may play the ball with their feet or lower legs but must not lift it. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: A scrum collapses. What must the referee do?

options.text: Let play go on if the ball is at the back of the scrum
Call "use it" to the team in possession
Wait to see which side gains an advantage
Blow the whistle immediately so that players stop pushing

questions.explanation: If a scrum collapses, the referee must blow the whistle immediately so that players stop pushing.

questions.stem: A prop is forced upwards out of a scrum. What must the referee do?

options.text: Wait for the ball to emerge
Play advantage to the team going forward

questions.explanation: If a player is lifted or forced upwards out of the scrum, the referee must blow the whistle immediately so that players stop pushing.

questions.stem: The scrum is stationary and the ball is available at the back. After how long does the referee call "use it"?
questions.explanation: When the scrum is stationary and the ball has been available at the back for three to five seconds, the referee calls "use it".

questions.stem: After "use it" is called at a scrum, how quickly must the ball be played out?
questions.explanation: After the call of "use it" the team must play the ball out of the scrum immediately.

questions.stem: A team fails to play the ball out of the scrum after the call of "use it". What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: If the ball is not played out of the scrum after the call of "use it", a scrum is awarded.

questions.stem: For how long must players remain onside at a scrum?

options.text: For the duration of the scrum
Until the ball reaches the back row
Until the scrum-half touches the ball

questions.explanation: Players remain onside for the duration of the scrum.

questions.stem: Before play in the scrum begins, where may the scrum-half of the team not throwing in stand?

options.text: At the far end of the tunnel, facing the opposing scrum-half
On whichever side of the scrum they choose, level with the ball
Beside the opposing scrum-half on their own side, or five metres back
Directly behind their own number eight, within one metre

questions.explanation: That scrum-half stands on their team's side of the middle line next to the opposing scrum-half, or at least five metres behind the hindmost foot.

questions.stem: The scrum-half of the team not throwing in chooses to stand back from the scrum. How far behind their team's hindmost foot must they be?
questions.explanation: That scrum-half may stand at least five metres behind the hindmost foot of their team's last player in the scrum.

questions.stem: A scrum-half of the team not throwing in starts five metres behind the hindmost foot. Until when must that player stay there?

options.text: Until the opposing scrum-half touches the ball
Until the completion of the scrum
Until the ball is thrown in

questions.explanation: A scrum-half who starts at least five metres behind the hindmost foot remains there until the completion of the scrum.

questions.stem: Once play in the scrum has begun, where must the scrum-half of the team in possession be?

options.text: With at least one foot level with or behind the ball
Anywhere on their own side of the scrum
With both feet behind the ball
With both feet behind the hindmost foot

questions.explanation: Once play in the scrum begins, the scrum-half of the team in possession has at least one foot level with or behind the ball.

questions.stem: Once play in the scrum has begun, how far may the scrum-half of the team not in possession advance beside the scrum?

options.text: As far as the opposition's hindmost foot
No further than their own hindmost foot
No further than the centre line of the tunnel

questions.explanation: That scrum-half takes up a position near the scrum with both feet no further than the centre line of the tunnel.

questions.stem: The scrum-half of the team not in possession retires to the offside line at their team's hindmost foot. May that player then come back to follow the ball round the scrum?

options.text: Yes, once the ball reaches the number eight

questions.explanation: A scrum-half who retires to the hindmost foot, or to five metres behind it, does so permanently.

questions.stem: How far behind the hindmost foot of their team must players not taking part in a scrum stay?
questions.explanation: All players not participating at the scrum remain at least five metres behind the hindmost foot of their team.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for a back who is offside at a scrum?
questions.explanation: Offside at a scrum is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: A scrum is set close to a team's try line, with that team's hindmost foot three metres from the line. Where is the offside line for that team's non-participants?

options.text: Five metres behind the hindmost foot, in in-goal

questions.explanation: When a team's hindmost foot is in in-goal or within five metres of its try line, the offside line for its non-participants is the try line.

questions.stem: When do the offside lines at a scrum stop applying?

options.text: As soon as the scrum ends
When the scrum has moved five metres
When the ball reaches the number eight

questions.explanation: As soon as the scrum ends, offside lines no longer apply.

questions.stem: The ball is thrown in and comes straight out of the far end of the tunnel with no infringement. What happens?

options.text: The other team throws in at a new scrum

questions.explanation: With no infringement, the scrum is reset if the ball is thrown in and comes out at either end of the tunnel.

questions.stem: A scrum breaks up before it has otherwise ended, with no infringement. What happens?
questions.explanation: With no infringement, the scrum is reset if it collapses or breaks up before it has otherwise ended.

questions.stem: Through more than how many degrees must a scrum wheel, without infringement, for it to be reset?
questions.explanation: The scrum is reset if it is wheeled through more than 90 degrees.

questions.stem: How does the law describe a scrum that has wheeled through more than 90 degrees?

options.text: The middle line has become parallel to the try line
The two front rows have swapped sides
The middle line has passed beyond parallel to the touchline
The tunnel is pointing at the goal posts

questions.explanation: A scrum has wheeled through more than 90 degrees when the middle line has passed beyond a position parallel to the touchline.

questions.stem: Neither side wins possession in a scrum and there is no infringement. What happens?

options.text: A scrum is awarded to the other team
A free-kick is awarded to the team throwing in

questions.explanation: With no infringement, the scrum is reset if neither side wins possession.

questions.stem: The ball is unintentionally kicked out of the tunnel. What happens?
questions.explanation: With no infringement, the scrum is reset if the ball is unintentionally kicked out of the tunnel.

questions.stem: The ball is repeatedly kicked out of the tunnel. How must the referee treat this?

options.text: As a reason for uncontested scrums

questions.explanation: If the ball is repeatedly kicked out of the tunnel, the referee must treat this as intentional and award a penalty.

questions.stem: When a scrum is reset, which team throws the ball in?

options.text: The team that previously threw it in
The team that did not throw it in before

questions.explanation: When a scrum is reset, the ball is thrown in by the team that previously threw it in.

questions.stem: The ball comes out of the side of a scrum, not through the tunnel. What has happened to the scrum?

options.text: It goes on until the scrum-half plays the ball

questions.explanation: The scrum ends when the ball comes out of the scrum in any direction except the tunnel.

questions.stem: The ball is at the feet of the hindmost player in the scrum and that team's scrum-half plays it. What has happened to the scrum?

options.text: It goes on until the ball is passed
It goes on until the packs break up

questions.explanation: The scrum ends when the ball reaches the feet of the hindmost player and is picked up by that player or played by that team's scrum-half.

questions.stem: The number eight picks up the ball from the feet of a second-row player. Is this allowed, and what happens to the scrum?

options.text: No, it is a free-kick offence
No, it is a penalty for handling in the scrum

questions.explanation: The scrum ends when the number eight picks up the ball from the feet of a second-row player.

questions.stem: Which of these ends a scrum?

options.text: The referee blows the whistle for an infringement
The ball reaches the second row
The scrum-half calls for the ball

questions.explanation: The scrum ends when the referee blows the whistle for an infringement.

questions.stem: A scrum is pushed towards the try line until the ball in the scrum is on the line. What has happened to the scrum?

options.text: It must be reset five metres out

questions.explanation: The scrum ends when the ball in the scrum is on or over the try line.

questions.stem: A front row charges against the opposition at a scrum. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A front row charging against the opposition is dangerous play in a scrum. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: A prop pulls the opposing prop during a scrum. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Pulling an opponent is dangerous play in a scrum. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: A prop intentionally lifts the opposing prop off their feet in a scrum. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Intentionally lifting an opponent off their feet or forcing them upwards out of the scrum is dangerous play. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: What is the sanction for intentionally collapsing a scrum?
questions.explanation: Intentionally collapsing a scrum is dangerous play and a penalty offence.

questions.stem: A front-row player intentionally kneels during a scrum. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Intentionally falling or kneeling in a scrum is dangerous play. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: A flanker dives on the ball immediately after it emerges from the scrum. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Falling on or over the ball immediately after it has emerged from the scrum is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: A scrum-half kicks the ball while it is still in the scrum. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A scrum-half kicking the ball while it is in the scrum is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: A flanker holds an opposing flanker to stop that player breaking from the scrum. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A non-front-row player holding or pushing an opponent at a scrum is a penalty offence.

questions.stem: The ball leaves the scrum and a player brings it back in. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Bringing the ball back into the scrum once it has left is a free-kick offence.

questions.stem: A flanker reaches a foot into the tunnel and plays the ball. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: Non-front-row players playing the ball in the tunnel is a free-kick offence.

questions.stem: A scrum-half pretends the ball is out of the scrum to draw an opponent offside. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: A scrum-half attempting to make an opponent believe the ball is out of the scrum when it is not commits a free-kick offence.

questions.stem: Which of these scrum offences is sanctioned with a free-kick?

options.text: A scrum-half kicking the ball while it is in the scrum
Bringing the ball back into the scrum once it has left
Falling on the ball as it emerges from the scrum

questions.explanation: Bringing the ball back into the scrum is a free-kick offence. The other three are penalties.

questions.stem: Which of these scrum offences is sanctioned with a penalty?

options.text: A scrum-half pretending the ball is out of the scrum
A flanker playing the ball in the tunnel
A scrum-half kicking the ball while it is in the scrum
Bringing the ball back into the scrum once it has left

questions.explanation: A scrum-half kicking the ball while it is in the scrum is a penalty offence. The other three are free-kick offences.

questions.stem: Why are penalties and free-kicks awarded?

options.text: To restart play after a score
To restart play after an injury
To restart play after the ball goes into touch

questions.explanation: Penalties and free-kicks are awarded to restart play after infringements.

questions.stem: In the definitions, for what kind of infringement is a penalty awarded?
questions.explanation: A penalty is awarded against a team for a serious infringement.

questions.stem: Apart from an infringement by the opposition, for what is a free-kick awarded to a team?

options.text: A ball held up in in-goal

questions.explanation: A free-kick is awarded against a team for an infringement or to a team for a mark.

questions.stem: What is the closest to a try line that the mark for a penalty or free-kick can be?
questions.explanation: The mark for a penalty or free-kick must be no closer than five metres from the try line.

questions.stem: In which part of the ground must the mark for a penalty or free-kick be?

options.text: In the field of play or in in-goal

questions.explanation: The mark for a penalty or free-kick must be in the field of play.

questions.stem: An offence is committed in midfield while the ball is in play, and it is not a late charge on a kicker. Where is the penalty?

options.text: Where the ball was at the time

questions.explanation: For an infringement while the ball is in play, other than a late charge after a kick, the mark is at the place of infringement.

questions.stem: A penalty offence is committed while the ball is dead. Where, in general, is the mark?

options.text: In the middle of the halfway line

questions.explanation: For an infringement while the ball is dead, the mark is at the point where play would have restarted.

questions.stem: A penalty is awarded while the ball is dead, and play would have restarted eight metres in from touch. Where is the mark?

options.text: In midfield, in line with that place
Eight metres in from touch, at that place
On the 5-metre line, in line with that place
On the 15-metre line, in line with that place

questions.explanation: If the restart would have been on the touchline or within 15 metres of it, the mark is on the 15-metre line, in line with that place.

questions.stem: A penalty is awarded while the ball is dead, and play would have restarted with a drop-out. Where is the mark?

options.text: In the middle of the drop-out's sanction line
In the middle of the halfway line
Anywhere on the drop-out's sanction line
At the place where the offence took place

questions.explanation: If play would have restarted with a drop-out, the mark is anywhere on the drop-out's sanction line and the non-offending team decides where.

questions.stem: A player commits an offence in touch, outside the playing area, while the ball is in play. Where is the penalty?

options.text: On the touchline, in line with where the offence occurred
On the 15-metre line, in line with where the offence occurred
On the 5-metre line, in line with where the offence occurred
Where the ball was when the offence occurred

questions.explanation: For an infringement outside the playing area while the ball is in play, the mark is on the 15-metre line, in line with where the offence occurred.

questions.stem: An offence takes place beyond the dead-ball line while the ball is in play. Where is the penalty?

options.text: On the 5-metre line, in line with the offence, at least 15 metres from touch
On the 15-metre line, level with the 22-metre line
On the 22-metre line, in line with the offence, at least 15 metres from touch
On the try line, in line with the offence

questions.explanation: If the offence occurred in touch-in-goal or beyond the dead-ball line, the mark is on the five-metre line, in line with the place of infringement, but no less than 15 metres from the touchline.

questions.stem: A penalty is awarded for an infringement in a lineout. Where is the mark?

options.text: Where the offending player was standing
On the mark of touch, 5 metres from the touchline
Ten metres back from the mark of touch
On the mark of touch, 15 metres from the touchline

questions.explanation: For any infringement in a lineout, the mark is 15 metres from the touchline on the mark of touch.

questions.stem: A player is penalised for offside at a ruck. Where is the mark?

options.text: At the offending team's offside line
Where the ball was in the ruck
Where the offside player was standing

questions.explanation: For offside at a phase of play, the mark is at the offending team's offside line.

questions.stem: After a penalty is awarded but before it is taken, the same team offends again. What happens to the mark?

options.text: It moves to the place of the new offence

questions.explanation: A further infringement by the original offending team before the kick is taken advances the mark 10 metres.

questions.stem: An offence is committed in the field of play, two metres from the offending team's try line. Where is the penalty?

options.text: On the try line, in line with the offence
Five metres from the try line, in line with the offence
Two metres from the try line, at the place of the offence
On the 22-metre line, in line with the offence

questions.explanation: For an infringement within five metres of a try line, the mark is five metres from the try line, in line with the place of infringement.

questions.stem: A defender commits a penalty offence in their own in-goal. Where is the penalty?

options.text: On the try line, in line with the offence
On the 22-metre line, in line with the offence
In in-goal, at the place of the offence
Five metres from the try line, in line with the offence

questions.explanation: For an infringement in in-goal, the mark is in the field of play, five metres from the try line, in line with the place of infringement.

questions.stem: A kicker is late charged after kicking the ball. Which places may the non-offending team choose for the penalty?

options.text: The place of infringement, where the ball landed or where it was next played
Only the place where the ball landed
The place of infringement or the middle of the halfway line

questions.explanation: For a late charge on the kicker, the opposition chooses the place of the infringement, where the ball landed or where it was next played.

questions.stem: Who chooses where the penalty for a late charge on the kicker is taken?

options.text: The match official who saw the offence

questions.explanation: For late charging the kicker, the opposition chooses the place of the penalty from the options the law gives.

questions.stem: A kicker is late charged and the ball lands in touch. Where is the optional penalty?

options.text: On the 5-metre line, in line with where the ball went into touch
On the touchline, where the ball went into touch
In midfield, in line with where the ball went into touch
On the 15-metre line, in line with where the ball went into touch

questions.explanation: If the ball lands in touch, the optional penalty is on the 15-metre line, in line with where it went into touch.

questions.stem: A kicker is late charged and the ball lands in the field of play eight metres in from touch. Where is the optional penalty?

options.text: On the 15-metre line, opposite where the ball landed
On the 5-metre line, opposite where the ball landed
Eight metres in from touch, where the ball landed
In midfield, opposite where the ball landed

questions.explanation: If the ball lands within 15 metres of the touchline, the mark is on the 15-metre line opposite where the ball landed.

questions.stem: A kicker is late charged and the ball lands in the opposition's in-goal. Where is the optional penalty?

options.text: In in-goal, at the place where the ball landed
On the 22-metre line, in line with where the ball landed
Five metres from the try line, in line with where the ball crossed it
On the try line, at the place where the ball crossed it

questions.explanation: If the ball lands in in-goal, the optional penalty is five metres from the try line, in line with where the ball crossed the try line and at least 15 metres from touch.

questions.stem: A kicker is late charged and the kick hits a goal post. Where is the optional penalty?

options.text: Where the ball struck the post
On the 22-metre line, in front of the posts
Five metres out, in front of the posts

questions.explanation: If the ball hits a goal post or crossbar, the optional penalty is awarded where the ball lands.

questions.stem: A kicker is late charged inside their own in-goal, and the penalty is taken for the place of infringement. Where is the mark?

options.text: Five metres from the try line, in line with the offence, at least 15 metres from touch
In in-goal, at the place where the offence took place
On the 22-metre line, in line with the place of the offence
On the try line, in line with the place of the offence

questions.explanation: If the infringement takes place in the kicker's in-goal, the penalty is five metres from the try line in line with the place of infringement, but at least 15 metres from the touchline.

questions.stem: A player in the field of play intentionally knocks the ball into touch from a spot six metres in from the touchline. Where is the penalty?

options.text: Level with the infringement, 5 metres in from touch
Level with the infringement, 15 metres in from touch
On the touchline, where the ball went out
At the place of the infringement, six metres in

questions.explanation: The mark is where the infringement occurred, but no closer than 15 metres from the touchline.
