questions.stem: A defender in in-goal intentionally throws the ball into touch-in-goal. Where is the penalty?

options.text: On the try line, 15 metres from the touchline
On the 22-metre line, in the middle of the field
In in-goal, where the ball was thrown from
On the 5-metre line, at least 15 metres from the touchline

questions.explanation: If the ball is intentionally thrown or knocked into touch or touch-in-goal from in in-goal, the mark is on the five-metre line at least 15 metres from the touchline.

questions.stem: A defender in in-goal intentionally knocks the ball over the dead-ball line. Where is the penalty?

options.text: In in-goal, at the place where the infringement occurred
On the 22-metre line, in line with where the infringement occurred
On the 5-metre line, in line with where the infringement occurred
On the try line, in line with where the infringement occurred

questions.explanation: If the ball is intentionally knocked over the dead-ball line from in-goal, the mark is on the five-metre line in line with where the infringement occurred.

questions.stem: From where may a penalty or free-kick be taken?

options.text: Anywhere within one metre of the mark
At the mark, or behind it on a line through the mark
At the mark and nowhere else
Anywhere behind the mark, to either side of it

questions.explanation: A penalty or free-kick is taken from where it is awarded or anywhere behind it on a line through the mark and parallel to the touchlines.

questions.stem: In which direction does the line through the mark for a penalty run?
questions.explanation: The kick may be taken anywhere behind the mark on a line through the mark and parallel to the touchlines.

questions.stem: A penalty is taken quickly from two metres to the side of the mark. What happens?

options.text: A scrum is awarded to the opposition

questions.explanation: When a penalty or free-kick is taken at the wrong place, it must be re-taken.

questions.stem: A team is awarded a penalty in open play. What may it choose in place of the kick?
questions.explanation: A team awarded a penalty may instead choose a scrum.

questions.stem: Which of these teams may choose a scrum in place of the kick?

options.text: A team awarded a free-kick at a lineout
A team awarded a free-kick in open play
A team awarded a free-kick for a mark

questions.explanation: The option of a scrum is given to a team awarded a penalty. A free-kick at a lineout may be swapped only for a lineout.

questions.stem: A team is awarded a penalty at a lineout. What may it choose in place of the kick?

options.text: A scrum at the same mark only
A lineout at the same mark only
A lineout or a scrum at the same mark

questions.explanation: A team awarded a penalty at a lineout may instead choose a lineout or a scrum at the same mark.

questions.stem: A team is awarded a free-kick at a lineout. What may it choose in place of the kick?

options.text: A penalty at the same mark
A lineout or a scrum at the same mark
A lineout at the same mark
A scrum at the same mark

questions.explanation: A team awarded a free-kick at a lineout may instead choose a lineout at the same mark.

questions.stem: A team chooses a lineout in place of a penalty awarded at a lineout. Where is the lineout?

options.text: Where the ball would have been kicked to

questions.explanation: The lineout or scrum chosen in place of a penalty at a lineout is at the same mark.

questions.stem: How soon must a penalty or free-kick be taken?
questions.explanation: A penalty or free-kick must be taken without delay.

questions.stem: Who may take a penalty kick?

options.text: Only the player who was fouled
Any player of the non-offending team

questions.explanation: Any player from the non-offending team may take a penalty or free-kick, other than a free-kick awarded for a mark.

questions.stem: Which free-kick must be taken by one particular player?

options.text: A free-kick awarded for a mark
A free-kick awarded at a lineout
A free-kick awarded at a scrum

questions.explanation: Any player may take a penalty or free-kick, other than a free-kick awarded for a mark, which the player who claimed the mark takes.

questions.stem: Which ball must the kicker use for a penalty or free-kick?

options.text: Any ball that the kicker chooses to use
The ball that was in play, even if it is defective
A new ball handed over by the ball person
The ball that was in play, unless the referee decides it is defective

questions.explanation: The kicker must use the ball that was in play unless the referee decides it is defective.

questions.stem: Which types of kick may be used to take a penalty or free-kick?

options.text: A punt or a drop-kick only
A punt, a drop-kick or a place-kick

questions.explanation: The kicker may punt, drop-kick or place-kick the ball, though a place-kick may not be used for touch.

questions.stem: A kicker places the ball on the ground and place-kicks a penalty into touch. Is this allowed?

options.text: Only inside the kicker's own half
Yes, if the referee is told first
Yes, any type of kick may be used
No, a place-kick may not be used for touch

questions.explanation: The kicker may punt, drop-kick or place-kick the ball, but a place-kick may not be used to kick for touch.

questions.stem: In which direction may a penalty or free-kick be kicked?

options.text: Only towards touch or the posts

questions.explanation: The kicker may kick the ball in any direction.

questions.stem: Where must the kicker's team-mates be when a penalty or free-kick is taken?

options.text: Behind the ball until it has been kicked
Anywhere, as long as they do not interfere
At least five metres behind the mark

questions.explanation: The kicker's team must remain behind the ball until it has been kicked.

questions.stem: Which team-mate of the kicker is exempt from having to stay behind the ball at a place-kick?
questions.explanation: Other than the placer at a place-kick, the kicker's team must remain behind the ball until it has been kicked.

questions.stem: A team-mate is standing in front of the ball when a tap penalty is taken. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: The kicker's team must remain behind the ball until it has been kicked. The sanction is a scrum.

questions.stem: How far must the ball be kicked when a penalty or free-kick is taken?
questions.explanation: The ball must be kicked a visible distance.

questions.stem: A kicker taking a quick tap penalty holds the ball and touches it against a boot without the ball leaving the hands. Is the kick valid?

options.text: No, the ball must clearly leave the hands
Yes, if the kicker then runs forward
Yes, the ball touched the foot
Only if no opponent is within ten metres

questions.explanation: If the kicker is holding the ball, it must clearly leave the hands.

questions.stem: The ball is on the ground at the mark for a tap penalty. What must the kick do to the ball?

options.text: Move it at least one metre
Send it backwards to a team-mate
Make it clearly leave the mark

questions.explanation: If the ball is on the ground, it must clearly leave the mark.

questions.stem: After successfully tapping a penalty, may the kicker play the ball again?

options.text: Yes, the kicker may play the ball again
Only after an opponent has touched it
Only after the ball has travelled five metres
No, a team-mate must play it next

questions.explanation: Once the kick has been successfully taken the kicker may play the ball again.

questions.stem: A free-kick is taken but the ball is not kicked a visible distance. What is the sanction?
questions.explanation: The ball must be kicked a visible distance. The sanction is a scrum.

questions.stem: Under the definitions, with which part of the body is a kick made?

options.text: Any part of the leg, including the knee
The leg or foot from toe to knee, but not the knee or heel
The foot only, including the heel

questions.explanation: A kick is made by hitting the ball with any part of the leg or foot, except the heel, from the toe to the knee but not including the knee.

questions.stem: A player taking a tap penalty knees the ball forward out of the hands. Is this a valid kick?

options.text: Yes, as the ball left the hands
Yes, any part of the leg may be used
Only if the ball travels a metre
No, a kick is not made with the knee

questions.explanation: A kick uses the leg or foot from the toe to the knee, but not including the knee.

questions.stem: How far must the opposing team retreat when a penalty or free-kick is awarded?
questions.explanation: The opposing team must immediately retreat 10 metres towards their own try line.

questions.stem: A penalty is awarded six metres from the offending team's try line. How far must that team retreat?
questions.explanation: The opposing team retreats 10 metres or until they have reached their try line if that is closer.

questions.stem: In which direction must the opposing team retreat at a penalty?

options.text: Away from the ball in any direction

questions.explanation: The opposing team must retreat 10 metres towards their own try line.

questions.stem: How quickly must the opposing team retreat when a penalty is awarded?

options.text: Once the referee makes the mark

questions.explanation: When a penalty or free-kick is awarded, the opposing team must immediately retreat.

questions.stem: A penalty is taken quickly while opponents are still retreating. What must those opponents do?

options.text: Stand still until the ball passes them

questions.explanation: Even if the kick is taken quickly, opposing players must keep retreating the necessary distance and may not take part until they have done so.

questions.stem: A penalty is taken so quickly that an opponent had no opportunity to retreat. Is that opponent sanctioned for being within 10 metres?

options.text: Only if the player is within five metres
No, but the player may not take part until onside
Yes, a further penalty is awarded
No, and the player may tackle at once

questions.explanation: Opponents who had no opportunity to retreat are not sanctioned, but they may not take part in the game until they are onside.

questions.stem: An opponent caught within 10 metres of a quickly taken penalty wants to rejoin play. What must happen first?

options.text: The ball is played by any player other than the kicker
The kicker passes the ball to a team-mate, who is tackled
The kicker runs at least five metres with the ball in hand
The player retreats 10 metres, or a team-mate from 10 metres back passes them

questions.explanation: The player may not take part until they have retreated 10 metres from the mark or a team-mate who was 10 metres from the mark has moved in front of them.

questions.stem: After a penalty is awarded, an opponent throws the ball away to stop a quick tap. What is the sanction?

options.text: A second penalty at the same mark
A scrum at the original mark
A free-kick, 10 metres in front of the original mark
A second penalty, 10 metres in front of the original mark

questions.explanation: The opposing team may not delay the kick. The sanction is a second penalty, 10 metres in front of the original mark.

questions.stem: After a free-kick is awarded, an opponent kicks the ball away to delay the kick. What is the sanction?

options.text: A second free-kick, 10 metres in front of the original mark
A scrum, 10 metres in front of the original mark
A scrum at the original mark
A second free-kick at the same mark

questions.explanation: The opposing team may not delay the kick. The sanction is a second free-kick, 10 metres in front of the original mark.

questions.stem: A second penalty is awarded 10 metres on from the first. When may it be taken?

options.text: Once the captains have been spoken to
Once the referee has made the mark
At once, from anywhere beyond the first mark
Once the offending team has retreated

questions.explanation: The second penalty or free-kick must not be taken before the referee has made the mark.

questions.stem: Which of these counts as illegally delaying a penalty?

options.text: Lining up along their own try line
Retreating 10 metres as soon as the whistle goes
Intentionally kicking the ball out of the kicking team's reach
Standing still 10 metres back from the mark

questions.explanation: The opposing team may not delay the kick, including by intentionally taking, throwing or kicking the ball out of reach.

questions.stem: From what moment may the opposing team charge a free-kick?

options.text: As soon as the kicker initiates movement to kick
As soon as the free-kick is awarded
Once the ball has been kicked
Once the kicker has the ball in hand

questions.explanation: As soon as the kicker initiates movement to kick, the opposing team may charge.

questions.stem: What may opponents who charge a free-kick try to do?

options.text: Stand in the kicker's path without contact
Tackle the kicker or block the kick
Take the ball from the mark
Block the kick, but not tackle the kicker

questions.explanation: Opponents may charge and try to prevent the free-kick being taken by tackling the kicker or blocking the kick.

questions.stem: Opponents charge fairly and prevent a free-kick from being taken. What happens to the kick?

options.text: It is re-taken 10 metres further on

questions.explanation: If the opposing team charge fairly and prevent the free-kick being taken, the kick is disallowed.

questions.stem: A free-kick is fairly charged and prevented from being taken. How does play restart?

options.text: A penalty to the kicking team
A scrum at the mark, the charging team throwing in
A scrum at the mark, the kicking team throwing in

questions.explanation: Play restarts with a scrum at the mark, with the team that charged throwing in.

questions.stem: At which kick does the law give opponents the right to charge once the kicker starts to move?
questions.explanation: The right to charge as soon as the kicker initiates movement is given to the opposing team at a free-kick.

questions.stem: Is the try line part of in-goal?

options.text: Yes, in-goal includes the try line
No, in-goal starts just behind the try line
Only when the ball is on the ground

questions.explanation: The definitions say in-goal includes the try line but not the dead-ball line or the touch-in-goal lines.

questions.stem: An attacker grounds the ball on the try line itself. What is the decision?

options.text: No try, the ball must be beyond the line
Try, the try line is part of in-goal

questions.explanation: In-goal includes the try line, so a ball grounded on the line by an attacker is a try.

questions.stem: Is the dead-ball line part of in-goal?

options.text: No, the dead-ball line is outside in-goal
Yes, in-goal includes the dead-ball line
Only when the ball is grounded on it

questions.explanation: In-goal includes the try line but not the dead-ball line or the touch-in-goal lines.

questions.stem: A player holding the ball touches the ground in in-goal with it. Has the ball been grounded?

options.text: Yes, holding it and touching the ground with it is enough
No, downward pressure is also needed
Only if both hands are on the ball
No, the player must let go of the ball

questions.explanation: The ball can be grounded by holding it and touching the ground with it.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier dives over the try line and the ball, held in one arm, touches the ground in in-goal. Is downward pressure also needed?

options.text: Yes, both hands must be on the ball
No, touching the ground with a held ball is enough
Yes, pressure must be applied with a hand
Only if a defender is also holding the ball

questions.explanation: A player holding the ball grounds it simply by touching the ground with it.

questions.stem: A ball is lying on the ground in in-goal. How may a player ground it without picking it up?

options.text: By touching it with any part of the body at all
By standing over it with a foot on either side
By pressing down on it with a hand, an arm or the front of the body
By kicking it firmly down against the ground

questions.explanation: A loose ball is grounded by pressing down on it with a hand or hands, arm or arms, or the front of the body from waist to neck.

questions.stem: Which part of the front of the body may be used to press down on the ball to ground it?
questions.explanation: The ball may be grounded by pressing down on it with the front of the player's body from waist to neck.

questions.stem: An attacker dives on a loose ball in in-goal and presses down on it with the chest. What is the decision?

options.text: No try, the hands must be used

questions.explanation: Pressing down on the ball with the front of the body from waist to neck grounds it.

questions.stem: A ball is loose in in-goal and an attacker presses down on it with a forearm. Has it been grounded?

options.text: No, only a hand may be used
No, the ball must be held
Yes, pressing down with an arm grounds the ball
Only if a hand touches it as well

questions.explanation: The ball can be grounded by pressing down on it with a hand or hands, or an arm or arms.

questions.stem: A player slides into in-goal and presses down on a loose ball with a thigh only. Has the ball been grounded?

options.text: Yes, if the player is an attacker
No, the thigh is not among the parts the law lists
Only if the ball stops moving

questions.explanation: A loose ball is grounded with a hand, an arm or the front of the body from waist to neck. The legs are not included.

questions.stem: A player picks up a loose ball in in-goal. Has the ball been grounded?

options.text: Yes, the ball was touched while on the ground
Yes, if the player is a defender
Only if the player then stands still
No, picking up a ball is not grounding it

questions.explanation: Picking up a ball is not grounding it.

questions.stem: An attacker picks up the ball in in-goal near the corner, runs towards the posts and grounds it there. What is the decision?

options.text: Try, where the ball was grounded
Try, where the ball was picked up
No try, the ball had to be grounded at once

questions.explanation: A player may pick up the ball in in-goal and ground it elsewhere in in-goal.

questions.stem: A defender picks up the ball in their own in-goal. May the defender run with it and ground it somewhere else in in-goal?

options.text: Only within five metres of the pick-up
No, picking it up has already grounded it
Yes, the ball may be grounded elsewhere in in-goal
No, it must be grounded where it was picked up

questions.explanation: A player may pick up the ball in in-goal and ground it elsewhere in in-goal.

questions.stem: A player standing in touch-in-goal reaches into in-goal and presses down on a loose ball without holding it. Can this be a try or a touch down?

options.text: No, a player in touch-in-goal cannot ground the ball
Yes, provided the player is not holding the ball
Only if one foot is in in-goal
It can be a touch down but not a try

questions.explanation: A player in touch or touch-in-goal can make a touch down or score a try by grounding the ball in in-goal, provided they are not holding it.

questions.stem: A player standing in touch-in-goal picks up a ball lying in in-goal and then places it on the ground there. Is this a valid grounding?

options.text: Yes, the ball was grounded in in-goal
Yes, if the player is a defender
Only if it was done in one movement
No, by picking it up the player made the ball dead

questions.explanation: A player in touch-in-goal may ground a ball only if not holding it. Picking it up makes the ball dead.

questions.stem: An attacking player grounds the ball in the opponents' in-goal. What is the result?
questions.explanation: An attacking player grounding the ball in in-goal scores a try.

questions.stem: A defender fumbles the ball in in-goal and an attacker dives on it, pressing down with both hands. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: An attacking player grounding the ball in in-goal scores a try.

questions.stem: A defending player grounds the ball in their own in-goal. What is this called?
questions.explanation: A defending player grounding the ball in in-goal results in a touch down.

questions.stem: What separates a try from a touch down?

options.text: Whether the ball is held or loose
Which team's player grounds the ball in in-goal
Whether a hand or the body is used
Which part of in-goal the ball is grounded in

questions.explanation: An attacking player grounding the ball in in-goal scores a try. A defending player doing so makes a touch down.

questions.stem: An attacker grounds the ball in in-goal while a foot is touching the dead-ball line at the same moment. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: An attacker who grounds the ball while simultaneously touching the dead-ball line or touch-in-goal line concedes a 22-metre drop-out.

questions.stem: An attacker holding the ball grounds it in in-goal and simultaneously touches the touch-in-goal line. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Grounding the ball while simultaneously in contact with the touch-in-goal line gives the defending team a 22-metre drop-out.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier grounds the ball in in-goal while a foot touches the touchline at the same moment. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: The ball is in touch in the field of play, so a lineout is awarded to the opposition.

questions.stem: Why is no try awarded when the ball-carrier grounds the ball in in-goal while touching the touchline?

options.text: The ball is dead in in-goal
The ball is in touch in the field of play

questions.explanation: When the ball-carrier grounds the ball and simultaneously touches the touchline, the ball is in touch in the field of play.

questions.stem: A defender is tackled just outside their own in-goal, and momentum carries them over the try line. May the defender make a touch down?

options.text: No, the ball must be released in the field of play
Only if the tackler has let go
Yes, a tackled player carried in by momentum may touch down
Only if no attacker is within a metre

questions.explanation: If a tackled player has momentum that carries them into their own in-goal, they can make a touch down.

questions.stem: A defender is tackled close to their own try line. May the defender reach back and ground the ball in in-goal?

options.text: Only if momentum carries the player in
Yes, provided it is done immediately
Yes, at any time before a ruck forms
No, the ball must be released where the tackle was made

questions.explanation: A tackled player near their own try line may reach out and ground the ball in in-goal to make a touch down, provided it is done immediately.

questions.stem: A defender tackled near their own try line waits, then crawls back and grounds the ball in in-goal. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: A tackled player may reach out to make a touch down only if it is done immediately. The sanction is a penalty.

questions.stem: A tackled attacker is reaching out to ground the ball for a try. What may a defender legally do to the ball?

options.text: Knock it backwards or pull it from the player's possession
Nothing at all: the ball must be left alone
Knock it away in any direction, forward included
Kick it out of the player's hands with the foot

questions.explanation: Defending players may knock the ball backwards or pull it from the player's possession, but must not kick or attempt to kick it.

questions.stem: A tackled attacker reaches out to ground the ball for a try. Is a defender allowed to kick the ball out of the attacker's hands?

options.text: No, defenders must not kick or attempt to kick the ball
Yes, any part of the body may be used
Only if the kick is below knee height
Yes, if the ball has not yet touched the ground

questions.explanation: Defenders may knock the ball backwards or pull it away, but must not kick or attempt to kick the ball.

questions.stem: A tackled attacker reaches out to ground the ball and a defender swings a foot at the ball but misses. Has the defender offended?

options.text: Only if the attacker then loses the ball
Yes, attempting to kick the ball is also forbidden
No, the ball was not touched
Only if the attacker was struck

questions.explanation: Defending players must not kick or attempt to kick the ball in this situation.

questions.stem: An attacking player in the field of play kicks the ball in open play and it rolls over the opponents' dead-ball line. What may the defending team choose?

options.text: A scrum where the ball was kicked and nothing else
A 22-metre drop-out or a scrum where the ball was kicked
A try line drop-out or a 5-metre scrum

questions.explanation: The defending team can choose a drop-out on or behind the 22-metre line, or a scrum at the place where the ball was kicked.

questions.stem: A team kicks the ball from the field of play through the opponents' in-goal into touch-in-goal. Which team chooses how play restarts?
questions.explanation: The defending team can choose a drop-out or a scrum at the place where the ball was kicked.

questions.stem: From where must the ball have been kicked for the defending team to get the choice of a 22-metre drop-out or a scrum when it goes dead through in-goal?

options.text: From anywhere in the playing area
From inside the kicking team's own half

questions.explanation: The choice applies when a team kicks the ball through the opponents' in-goal from the field of play.

questions.stem: The defending team chooses a drop-out after the attackers kick the ball dead through in-goal. Where is it taken?

options.text: On or behind the try line
Anywhere on or behind the 22-metre line
In the middle of the 22-metre line only

questions.explanation: The drop-out is taken anywhere on or behind the 22-metre line.

questions.stem: The defending team chooses a scrum after the attackers kick the ball dead through in-goal. Where is the scrum?

options.text: Where the ball crossed the try line

questions.explanation: The scrum is at the place where the ball was kicked.

questions.stem: A penalty kick at goal misses and the ball goes over the dead-ball line. How does play restart?

options.text: A scrum where the kick was taken

questions.explanation: After an unsuccessful kick at goal, the defending team restarts with a 22-metre drop-out.

questions.stem: A dropped goal attempt misses and goes dead through in-goal. May the defending team choose a scrum where the ball was kicked?

options.text: Yes, if the kick was from outside the 22
Only if the ball crossed the dead-ball line in the air
No, play restarts with a 22-metre drop-out

questions.explanation: An unsuccessful kick at goal or attempted dropped goal is an exception. The defending team restarts with a 22-metre drop-out.

questions.stem: A defender has one foot in in-goal and one foot in the field of play. Where is the defender considered to be?
questions.explanation: If any part of a defending player is in in-goal, that player is considered to be in in-goal.

questions.stem: How much of a defending player must be in in-goal for the player to be considered in in-goal?

options.text: More than half of the body

questions.explanation: If any part of a defending player is in in-goal, the player is considered to be in in-goal, provided they are not also in touch or on or over the dead-ball line.

questions.stem: A defender standing in in-goal reaches out and picks up a ball that is still in the field of play. Who has taken the ball into in-goal?

options.text: The last attacker to play it
The team that last kicked it

questions.explanation: A player in in-goal who catches or picks up a ball that is still in the field of play has taken the ball into in-goal.

questions.stem: An attacker's kick stops just short of the try line. A defender standing in in-goal picks the ball up from the field of play and grounds it. How does play restart?

options.text: Scrum to the defending team where the ball was kicked

questions.explanation: The defender took the ball into in-goal and made it dead, so the attacking team throws in at a scrum.

questions.stem: A player standing beyond the dead-ball line catches a ball that is still within in-goal. What has that player done?
questions.explanation: A player on or beyond the dead-ball line who catches or picks up a ball within in-goal has made the ball dead.

questions.stem: A defender with a foot on the touch-in-goal line picks up a ball that is rolling in in-goal. What is the status of the ball?

options.text: It is in touch in the field of play
It is live until the defender grounds it
It is dead, made dead by the defender
It is live, as the ball was in in-goal

questions.explanation: A player in touch-in-goal who catches or picks up a ball within in-goal has made the ball dead.

questions.stem: The ball-carrier touches a corner flag post without otherwise being in touch or touch-in-goal. What happens?
questions.explanation: If the ball or ball-carrier touches a corner flag or corner flag post without otherwise being in touch or touch-in-goal, play continues.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier brushes the corner flag post while diving for the line, without touching touch or touch-in-goal, and grounds the ball in in-goal. What is the decision?
questions.explanation: Touching a corner flag post does not stop play unless the ball is grounded against the post.

questions.stem: The ball touches a corner flag post while otherwise in play. In which one case does play stop?

options.text: When the post is knocked over
When the ball touches the flag itself
When the ball-carrier also touches the post
When the ball is grounded against the post

questions.explanation: Play continues unless the ball is grounded against the post.

questions.stem: A ball-carrier is held up in in-goal and can neither ground the ball nor play it. What is the status of the ball?

options.text: The ball is live until the whistle

questions.explanation: When a player carrying the ball is held up in in-goal so that the ball cannot be grounded or played, the ball is dead.

questions.stem: What decides how play restarts after the ball is held up in in-goal?

options.text: How many players were holding it up
How long the ball was held up

questions.explanation: Play restarts with a try line drop-out or a 5-metre scrum, depending on how the ball entered in-goal.

questions.stem: An attacker carries the ball into the opponents' in-goal and is held up. How does play restart?
questions.explanation: When an attacking player takes the ball into in-goal and it is held up, play restarts with a try line drop-out.

questions.stem: A defender carries the ball back into their own in-goal and is held up there by attackers. How does play restart?
questions.explanation: When the defending team takes the ball into its own in-goal and it is made dead, the attacking team throws in at a scrum.

questions.stem: There is doubt about which team first grounded the ball in in-goal. How does play restart?

options.text: A 5-metre scrum, defending team throwing in
A 5-metre scrum, attacking team throwing in

questions.explanation: If there is doubt about which team first grounded the ball, play restarts with a five-metre scrum and the attacking team throws in.

questions.stem: Where is the scrum when there is doubt about which team first grounded the ball in in-goal?

options.text: On the try line, in line with the grounding
Five metres out, in front of the posts
Five metres out, in line with where the ball was grounded
On the 22-metre line, in line with the grounding

questions.explanation: The five-metre scrum is in line with the place where the ball was grounded.

questions.stem: An attacker and a defender dive on a loose ball in in-goal together, and the referee cannot tell who grounded it first. Which team throws in at the scrum?

options.text: The team that last kicked the ball

questions.explanation: When there is doubt about which team first grounded the ball, the attacking team throws in at the five-metre scrum.
